details.Description: Aberystwyth University was the first university in Wales and is an established traditional university, founded in 1872. The university welcomes students from all parts of the EU and has strong links with Denmark. It is recognised as leading in the field of research for Computer Science, the Arts, Political Studies, Environmental Sciences, Creative Writing, Theatre and Performance and Celtic and Medieval History. Aberystwyth University welcomes well over 100 exchange students from over 15 countries around Europe into a wide range of academic departments.

details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . As a result, students applying for exchange places in the UK cannot be guaranteed an Erasmus+ grant at the time of application. Eligibility for Erasmus+ funding will depend on whether the host university joins the programme and concludes an Erasmus+ agreement with the University of Copenhagen. Students nominated to a UK university will be informed of their grant eligibility no later than March 2027.
details.Additional information: Department of Life Science is an internationally-recognised research and teaching centre providing a unique base for research in response to global challenges such as food security, bioenergy and sustainability, and the impacts of climate change.

details.Description: Åbo Akademi University is Finland’s only Swedish-language multidisciplinary university, founded in 1918, with its main activities in two campuses: Åbo (Turku) and Vasa. It has around 7,000 students, including about 1,000 international students each year. The official language of instruction is Swedish, but there is a wide array of courses taught in English (around 250 annually) for exchange students. Turku (Åbo in Swedish) is Finland’s oldest city and a charming place to live and study. With over 40,000 students in the city and a historic, cultural atmosphere, there's always something going on — theatre, museums or festivals. Turku lies on the southwest coast of Finland, close to the archipelago, has good transport links to other parts of Finland and beyond, and provides a picturesque natural environment (coastline, islands, parks) for both study and recreation.

details.Description: Aix-Marseille Université (AMU) is France's largest French-speaking multidisciplinary university, formed from a 2012 merger of three universities, offering a wide range of studies across its 19 faculties and 12 doctoral schools on five major campuses in southern France. With around 80,000 students, including 12,000 international students, AMU is known for its strong research focus, extensive partnerships, and high-quality welcome for international students, holding a prestigious "Welcome to France" label.

details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: 1st semester: Late August – with exams in December. Winter semester: 2nd semester: Early January – with exams throughout the whole month of May. See additional information in the ‘ calendrier universitaire (https://facdedroit.univ-amu.fr/fr/international/venir-fdsp/etudiants-internationaux-programmes-echange-freemover#section-7858) ’
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: A good level of French language is required (oral and written). A minimum level of B2 in French is required according to the self-assessment CEFR-grid (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) . A language test like TCF, DELF or DALF are accepted (use e.g.  google find info on test options). Only very few law courses are taught in English, therefore please do not expect that you will be able to take a full study load of 30 ECTS with courses only taught in English. It will be necessary for you to take law courses taught in French. In order to familiarise exchange students with French legal terminology, the Faculty of Law at Aix-Marseille Université offers a free intensive course. Additional information will follow at the admission procedures.
details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. The majority of courses are offered as lectures called ‘cours magistraux’ (CM) and generally they have a duration of three (3) hours. Educational material such as text books are not used at lectures, instead students must take notes from the lecturers' presentations and use these when preparing for the final exams. In addition to ordinary lectures you can register for 1 class called ‘Travaux Dirigés’ (TD) – based on a special permission for Danish law students. With registration in an TD class which is connected to one of the ordinary law courses with lectures – you can gain additional ECTS. The education in a TD class will be interactive with presentations, assignments, group work etc. – an educational style familiar to the teaching methods in Copenhagen. You are strongly advised to read travel reports in KUnet (https://kunet.ku.dk/studie/sider/RedirectToTopic.aspx?topicId=6c9c7e02-d3bb-4735-8e65-33a2cfb91209) and student evaluations in Mobility online from Aix-Marseille Université as the teaching style will be significantly different from what you are used to at UCPH.

See course descriptions (https://facdedroit.univ-amu.fr/index.php/international/venir-fdsp/etudiants-internationaux-programmes-echange-freemover#section-5629) (also for a few courses taught in English). details.Description: Al Akhawayn University in Ifrane (AUI) educates the future citizen-leaders of Morocco and the world through a globally oriented, English-language liberal arts curriculum based on American education. The academic community composed of students, faculty, and staff work together to foster excellence and identity through teaching and learning favorable to the development of equity and social responsibility. Home to students from all around the world, the 75-hectare campus houses 7 academic buildings, a library, 21 student residences, 4 dining halls, shops, sports centers, and research labs.

details.Description: The university was founded in 1885 and is among the largest universities in the US with more than 74,000 students from 120 countries. ASU has four campuses located throughout the Phoenix metropolitan area, but are easily accessible by free intercampus shuttles. While international exchange students can study at any campus, most take courses at the Tempe campus due to the high number of classes and programs offered. Tempe is a lively university city, only a five-minute drive from Phoenix.

details.Restrictions: Course Restrictions: W.P. Carey School of Business (undergraduate programs): seats are limited depending on the specific academic unit or course; one example is Supply Chain Management (SCM) which has extremely limited spaces for exchange students. W.P. Carey School of Business (MBA): prior approval required during exchange program nomination phase (limited course offerings) Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts: students studying a similar major at their home university will be required to submit a portfolio of work or audition to gain access to courses Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering: Engineering students cannot take any engineering capstone courses at ASU.  In addition, some schools in engineering have further enrollment restrictions for engineering students: Schools of Computing and Augmented Intelligence: Students can take any lower division courses they wish.  For upper division courses, they need instructor approval to receive access to the course. Sustainable Engineering and the Built Environment: If there are a large number of open seats, students will be allowed to enroll in courses for which they meet prerequisites.  If there are very few seats available, advisors will wait until 1-2 weeks before the start of the semester before giving permission for exchange students to enroll. Engineering of Matter, Transport, and Energy: After all registration has opened, students may be given overrides into courses that still have a lot of seats open, depending on the course demand for ASU majors.  For these courses, advisers will wait until the FIRST WEEK of the semester before giving permission for exchange students to enroll. Walter Cronkite School of Journalism & Mass Comm: JMC courses are not available; MCO courses are limited.  Alternative courses in other colleges may be found under the following prefixes: COM & ENG College of Health Solutions: seats are limited depending on the specific academic unit or course Edson College of Nursing and Health Innovation: most courses are restricted Mary Lou Fulton Teacher’s College: most courses are restricted
details.Course information: Students should use the most recent semester Class Search ( LINK (https://catalog.apps.asu.edu/catalog/classes/classlist?term=2227) ) to search course offerings, as the Course Catalog Search will include many courses that are not currently scheduled. International exchange students are eligible to enroll in most classes for which they meet applicable prerequisites, as long as the course has not filled to capacity.   Please note that students are not guaranteed to receive all of their preferred classes, even if they meet prerequisites. Online courses: ASU offers several iCourses that are 100% online; international exchange students may take iCourses, but must be enrolled in at least 9 credits of in-person coursework (undergraduate) or 6 credits of in-person coursework (graduate). Internet - Hybrid courses: ASU offers several courses that have both an inperson and online component. International exchange students are not restricted from taking hybrid classes. Course Restrict

details.Description: Ashoka University is a pioneer in its focus on providing a liberal education at par with the best in the world. The aim at Ashoka is to help students become well-rounded individuals who can think critically about issues from multiple perspectives, communicate effectively, and become leaders with a commitment to public service. An Ashoka education carries a strong emphasis on foundational knowledge, thorough academic research based on rigorous pedagogy, and hands-on experience with real-world challenges. The 2800 plus students on campus, drawn from 28 states and over 287 cities in India and 21 other countries, receive a world-class interdisciplinary education through undergraduate and post-graduate programmes led by internationally renowned faculty.

details.Description: Athens University of Economics and Business (AUEB), founded in 1920, is Greece’s leading institution in the fields of economics, business, and information sciences. With eight academic departments spanning economics, international and European studies, business administration, marketing, accounting, informatics, and statistics, AUEB offers a strong academic foundation rooted in both theory and applied research. The university also hosts a variety of postgraduate programs, many of which are taught in English, and it maintains active participation in European exchange programs like Erasmus+. Known for its international outlook, research excellence, and highly qualified faculty, AUEB provides a rigorous and relevant education, especially for students interested in global business and economic issues. Located in the heart of Athens, the university gives students easy access to a lively and culturally rich city. From ancient landmarks and bustling markets to cafés and local neighborhoods, Athens blends history and modern energy in a way few European cities can. Exchange students benefit from being part of a dynamic urban environment, with opportunities to explore the city’s vibrant culture while studying in a well-connected central location. The combination of strong academics and an exciting city life makes AUEB an appealing choice for students looking to deepen their knowledge of economics and business while experiencing life in the Greek capital.

details.Description: Founded in 1946, the Australian National University (ANU) supports a community of over 25,500 students. The ANU campus is located in Canberra, the capital of Australia and comprises seven academic colleges, which host a number of schools and research centres specialising in a variety of disciplines. The university is especially renowned for the strength of its Arts and Humanities and Natural Sciences departments. ANU courses are taught in small classes and state-of-the-art collaborative spaces that stimulate students to think differently. As ANU students, incoming exchange participants will have the support of our vibrant and talented community including access to academic, sporting, cultural and social activities, and access to comprehensive wellbeing support. ANU is located in the heart of Canberra, our beautiful and vibrant capital city. Canberra’s accessibility, friendliness, and overall quality of life makes it the perfect place to live, study and explore the region. Get a glimpse of a day in the life of an ANU exchange student! details.Description: Bahçeşehir University (BAU) is a private institution in Istanbul, Turkey, with over 24,000 students and around 1,900 staff. Founded in 1998, it has developed a strong international profile, with more than 6,000 international students and over 290 global academic agreements. The university operates multiple campuses in Istanbul and maintains branch campuses in Berlin, Rome, Toronto, and Washington, D.C. BAU is notable for its CO-OP education model, which integrates academic study with professional internships through partnerships with over 2,300 companies. It ranks among the top Turkish universities in international outlook and sustainability. The university is located in central Istanbul, with its main campus along the Bosphorus in Beşiktaş, offering students direct access to one of Europe’s most dynamic urban environments. Istanbul combines historical depth with modern infrastructure, and its extensive public transport network makes commuting between campuses and city districts efficient. The city’s cultural diversity and strategic location between Europe and Asia provide a unique setting for international exchange. A small curiosity: Istanbul is the only city in the world that spans two continents, with the Bosphorus Strait dividing its European and Asian sides.

It is an important base in China for talent training in and research of foreign languages, translation, tourism, and economics and trade.

details.Description: Bielefeld University, established in 1969, is a modern and research-driven institution with around 24,500 students and 14 faculties covering the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, engineering, and medicine. It is known for its interdisciplinary approach and emphasis on unifying research and teaching. The university hosts several renowned research centers and institutes, such as the Center for Interdisciplinary Research and the Cluster of Excellence Cognitive Interaction Technology. Bielefeld’s innovative structure, including its central building where all faculties are under one roof, fosters collaboration and a strong academic community. Located in the city of Bielefeld in the North Rhine-Westphalia region of Germany, the university offers a balanced student experience with both urban and natural surroundings. The campus is situated near the Teutoburg Forest, offering opportunities for outdoor recreation, while the city itself provides cultural venues, cafés, and student-friendly events. With an efficient public transport system and a welcoming atmosphere, Bielefeld is an ideal setting for exchange students looking for a mix of academic excellence and everyday livability.

details.Description: Boğaziçi University, located in Istanbul, is one of Turkey’s most prestigious public universities, known for its strong academic programs and vibrant international community. Established in 1863 as Robert College and transformed into a public university in 1971, Boğaziçi offers a wide range of programs across six faculties, including Arts and Sciences, Economics and Administrative Sciences, Engineering, and Education. Exchange students can choose from a variety of English-taught courses, benefiting from a rigorous academic environment that emphasizes critical thinking, research, and a global perspective. The university’s longstanding tradition of academic excellence and its openness to international collaboration make it an ideal destination for students seeking a high-quality study abroad experience. The university's main campus is situated on a hill overlooking the Bosphorus, providing a stunning backdrop for student life. Istanbul itself is a dynamic metropolis that bridges Europe and Asia, offering a rich blend of history, culture, and modern urban energy. Exchange students will find endless opportunities to explore the city’s historic landmarks, vibrant arts scene, and diverse culinary traditions, all while being part of a lively student community at Boğaziçi.

Mission Boğaziçi University’s mission is to educate individuals who embrace it’s institutional values, who are able to think both creatively and critically, who are independent and egalitarian, who appreciate ethical values, who respect nature and are aware of environmental issues, who are rooted in the local and open to the global, and who can, with their self-confidence and scholarly, social and cultural foundations, successfully take on leadership positions anywhere in the world. details.Description: Ca’ Foscari University of Venice, established in 1868 as Italy’s first business school, has evolved into a comprehensive institution offering a wide array of academic programs. With approximately 20,000 students and eight departments, the university is structured around four main academic areas: Foreign Languages and Literatures, Humanities, Economics, and Sciences. Exchange students have access to a diverse selection of courses, including subjects in international business, cultural studies, environmental science, and linguistics, many of which are offered in English. Ca’ Foscari maintains a strong emphasis on global engagement and intercultural exchange, providing international students with academic experiences deeply connected to the university’s historical strengths in commerce, languages, and cultural heritage. Situated in the heart of Venice, Ca’ Foscari’s campuses are embedded within the city’s iconic canals and historic architecture. The unique urban landscape offers students a learning environment that blends academic life with the artistic, cultural, and maritime traditions of Venice. From exploring local markets and museums to participating in university-organized cultural events, exchange students experience daily life in a city renowned for its beauty, history, and vibrant student atmosphere. The University also offers Italian language courses for international students and a ‘buddy’ program with local students.

details.Description: Established in 1348, Charles University stands as one of the oldest and most esteemed universities in the world. Despite its rich historical legacy, the university maintains a forward-thinking and cosmopolitan approach, making it a modern and prestigious institution of higher education. As the largest and top-rated university in the Czech Republic, Charles University boasts 17 faculties, with 14 of them located in the vibrant city of Prague. The university's commitment to internationalization is evident in its diverse student body, with over 9,000 international students comprising approximately 20% of the total student population. This multicultural environment fosters a lively and dynamic atmosphere within the university. Offering a wide range of courses in multiple languages, including English, German, French, and Czech, Charles University ensures that students from various backgrounds can pursue their academic goals. As an Erasmus student, one can benefit from the support of international associations dedicated to facilitating the integration and orientation process. Additionally, each faculty hosts various clubs and organizations, such as film clubs, choirs, and book clubs, providing students with opportunities to engage in extracurricular activities and explore their diverse interests. Charles University serves as a thriving hub of intellectual growth, cultural exchange, and community engagement, making it a highly sought-after institution for students seeking a comprehensive and enriching educational experience. Prague offers a rich and stimulating environment for student life, combining historical depth with modern infrastructure. The city is compact and well-connected by public transport, including a metro system known for its depth and efficiency. Students can explore medieval streets, vibrant cultural venues, and green spaces throughout the city. A fun fact: Prague is home to the world’s largest castle complex (the Prague Castle) which spans over 70,000 square meters and includes palaces, churches, and historic lanes, making it a central part of the city’s identity and a frequent destination for students and visitors alike.

details.Description:
The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is a leading comprehensive research university.
It has a total of 61 departments under the Faculties of Arts, Business Administration,
Education, Engineering, Law, Medicine, Science, and Social Science. Currently, it has
approximately 21,000 students undertaking undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral
programmes. CUHK is the only university in Hong Kong with a college system. Each undergraduate student
is associated with one of the nine Colleges. The Colleges are responsible for informal
learning, and for academic and cultural immersion for students. CUHK is committed to
general education and whole-person development.

details.GPA for undergraduate admission: 7 CUHK also considers applicants with a lower average, but extra academic recommendations from a professor is required for students with a grade average under 7.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Copy of TOEFL or IELTS test report, taken within the last two years or a written support letter from the home institution's study-abroad office attesting the student's ability to attend courses instructed in English. Minimum TOEFL score of 550 (paper-based) or 80 (internet-based), or IELTS 6 (For undergraduates) or IELTS 6.5 (For postgraduates) or equivalent. Law students must submit a score report: a score of 100 on TOEFL or a score of 7 on IELTS.
details.Restrictions: Undergraduate students should have completed at least two semesters of university studies. Please note that availability of postgraduate-level courses for exchange students is very limited . Graduate students should make sure that they are allowed to take undergraduate courses while on exchange as part of their graduate degree before applying. All English-taught courses are open to exchange students except the following: - Faculty of Medicine courses (except some biomedical sciences and public health courses) - Faculty of Education courses (except some sports science and physical education (SPED) courses taught in English, and physical education (PHED) courses with an X after the course number) - Faculty of Law courses (except Law major students) - MBA courses (except for MBA specific exchange agreements) - Student-orientated teaching (STOT) courses - Courses under the MSc in Advanced Environmental Planning Technologies and MSc in Housing Studies programmes - Core Master of Accountancy courses - Courses under the MSc in Finance, MSc in Management and MSc in Marketing programmes, except students from the exchange partner schools of these programmes, who can take specified courses - FNSC courses under the Food and Nutritional Sciences programme in the School of Life Sciences - Courses in the undergraduate and postgraduate design studios, except for students from the School of Architecture's exchange-partner schools - College General Education (GECC, GEJC, GEMC, GESH, GEUC, GESC) courses - All courses listed here (http://www.oal.cuhk.edu.hk/files/incoming/course_not_open_for_iasp.pdf) (for IASP students) - Any other courses restricted by their offering Departments
details.Course information: Course Information (https://www.oal.cuhk.edu.hk/academics/) Course exceptions document (https://www.oal.cuhk.edu.hk/files/incoming/course_exceptions.pdf) Students can choose courses based on their academic interests or requirements from various disciplines. Detailed course arrangements can be found here (https://www.oal.cuhk.edu.hk/academics/) . Graduate/Post-graduate courses are limited for exchange students.  Consider taking upper-level undergraduate courses instead.  MBA courses are generally not open to exchange students unless they are part of an existing formal MBA exchange agreement. Business courses are highly competitive.  Students are advised to be flexible in their study plans. Students interested in China-related courses can explore courses offered by the Chinese Studies programme.  These courses are taught entirely in English and cover China's cultural past, modern history and contemporary issues.  Details are available on the programme website (https://www.ccs.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/undergraduate-programmes/ba-in-chinese-studies/) . Limited law courses are only available to law major students.  These courses and quota are restricted due to the specialised nature of the programme. Please refer to this document (https://www.oal.cuhk.edu.hk/files/incoming/course_exceptions.pdf) for more information on the specific admission and English requirements.

details.Housing: The Office of Academic Links (OAL) will place exchange students in on-campus accommodations (hostels) where there are plenty of opportunities to integrate with locals through the many formal and informal activities organised by the hostels. On-campus Accommodation • On-campus housing is guaranteed for exchange students. • Accommodation fee for undergraduate students per semester is between HK$8,000 and HK$11,200. • Accommodation fee for postgraduate students per semester is approximately HK$13,500. • Accommodation is shared, normally double or triple occupancy. • Single room options are very limited and only available to students with medical needs and able to provide official medical proof.

details.Description: Chonnam National University (CNU) is a leading national institution founded on the principles of Truth, Creativity, and Service. Since our establishment in 1952, we have cultivated exceptional talent, upholding the values of democracy, human rights, and peace, and driving progress in both our local community and the nation. Today, we stand at a pivotal moment. As we navigate an era of rapid changes—including digital transformation, demographic shifts, and the climate crisis—universities must redefine their roles and responsibilities to meet the challenges of the future. At Chonnam National University, we are committed to leading this transformation. Through cutting-edge technology and innovative interdisciplinary research, we are advancing as a world-class research university while nurturing the next generation of leaders. By sharing knowledge and technology, we strive for mutual growth with our local and global communities. Guided by our motto, Together CNU, we are building a university where dreams are realized, the pursuit of truth is respected, and our contributions make a lasting impact on society. We invite you to join us in shaping the future for Chonnam National University.

details.Description: The Universidad Complutense de Madrid (UCM), founded in 1293, is one of the oldest and most prestigious universities in Spain and Europe. With over 86,000 students and a wide range of academic disciplines, it is also one of the largest traditional (non-distance) universities in Europe. UCM is a public research university with a strong emphasis on academic excellence, social responsibility, and international collaboration. Its two main campuses—Moncloa and Somosaguas—are located in Madrid and offer students access to extensive libraries, research centers, and cultural facilities. The university has a long history of academic innovation and was among the first in the world to award doctoral degrees to women. Madrid, the capital of Spain, offers a dynamic and student-friendly environment with a rich cultural heritage and excellent infrastructure. The city’s extensive public transport system—including metro, buses, and commuter trains—makes it easy for students to navigate between campuses and explore the city. Madrid is known for its world-class museums, lively neighborhoods, and green spaces like Retiro Park. A fun fact: Madrid is one of the highest capital cities in Europe, sitting at 667 meters above sea level, and its name is believed to come from the Arabic word Magerit , meaning “place of abundant water.” This blend of history, accessibility, and vibrant city life makes it an ideal destination for students.

However C1 in Spanish is highly recommended for Master programs, because UCM are not able to guarantee any courses or research in other languages.
details.Restrictions: Only open for BA students. Students registered in a specific faculty at UCM (main faculty) can choose a maximum of two courses in a faculty other than their main faculty; provided that such courses can be pre-approved at UCPH.

details.Description:
Concordia University was founded in 1974 and supports a community of over 50,000 students
per year. The university has two campuses, set approximately 7 kilometres apart: Sir George
Williams Campus is the main campus in the downtown core of Montreal and Loyola Campus in
the residential district of Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. Concordia offers over 300 undergraduate and
100 graduate programs and courses
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: September-December Winter semester : January-April Please note that the spring semester begins very early compared to the spring semester at UCPH. You should only apply for the spring semester, if you do not have exams in January at UCPH.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: TOEFL-test: 90 IELTS-test: 7.0
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 12 credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Study load for graduate students: 9 credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Conversion and levels: Study load is calculated according to the level of the specific course. Please note that not all UCPH Master’s (graduate) programmes allow credit transfer of bachelor (undergraduate) courses into their programmes. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: Restricted courses 2022-23 (https://www.concordia.ca/content/dam/concordia/offices/ci/docs/AY2022_23_restricted_course_list.pdf) 50% of the selected courses must fall within the same Concordia program.

details.Housing: Housing is not guaranteed for international exchange students.

scholarship.

details.Description: Cornell University is the federal land-grant institution of New York State, a private endowed university, a member of the Ivy League, and a partner of the State University of New York. It has been described as the first truly American university because of its founders' revolutionarily egalitarian and practical vision of higher education, and is dedicated to its land-grant mission of outreach and public service. Founded in 1865 by Ezra Cornell and Andrew Dickson White, Cornell was intended to teach and make contributions in all fields of knowledge. These ideals are captured in Cornell's motto, a popular 1865 Ezra Cornell quotation: "I would found an institution where any person can find instruction in any study."
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: Late August to Mid-December Spring semester: Mid/Late January - Mid-May Academic calendar (registrar.cornell.edu/academic-calendar)
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: TOEFL and IELTS are the primary tests accepted. Duolingo is also acceptable. More information for international students is available on the Undergraduate Admissions website (https://admissions.cornell.edu/international-students) . TOEFL iBT or Special Home edition: 100 and up IELTS: 7.5 and up Duolingo: 130 and up
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 12 credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: Evidence of solid academic preparation in general and in the proposed field(s) of study; a minimum of two semesters of continuous full-time university study are needed Note: exchange students tend to be among top of the class of their respective institutions. Academic information: Exchange students accepted at Cornell will be admitted into a major in the college or unit participating in the exchange. It is expected that students applying to the exchange program will be interested in taking the majority of their classes in this college or unit. Enrollment in classes in other colleges at Cornell is possible but cannot be guaranteed. Only students in business degree programs can apply to the Dyson School of Applied Economics and Management or the Nolan School of Hotel Administration as their Home College. Exchange students are unable to take courses in Computer Science (CS). Related subjects may be found in other departments (Electrical and Computer Engineering; Information Science, Systems, and Technology; or Operations Research and Information Engineering). • Studio classes (architecture, art, design, and fashion) are typically not available to students through general exchange agreements. • Senior capstone courses as well as first year writing seminars are not available to exchange students. Graduate programs, and Cornell University degree/certificate programs outside Ithaca, NY are not open to university-wide exchanges.
details.Important links: Cornell University (cornell.edu) Office of Global Learning (globallearning.cornell.edu) Courses (https://courses.cornell.edu/) International Services (international.globallearning.cornell.edu)
details.Housing: Housing is limited and not guaranteed for exchange students. • Fall semester: Finding housing can be very challenging. On-campus housing is not available, and single-semester leases within commuting distance are difficult to secure. • Spring semester: Housing may be available on-campus and is generally easy to find off-campus. • Academic year: Off-campus only Note: Upon nomination to Cornell we encourage students to begin searching for housing. However, students should not commit to housing (financially or otherwise) until they have received admission notification from Cornell and have secured a visa appointment. On-campus housing (living.sas.cornell.edu/live/apply/) Off-campus living (ccengagement.cornell.edu/off-campus-living)
details.Scholarships: Students applying for this university are automatically considered for KU’s Internationalisation scholarship.
details.Additional information: Fall semester applicants: If you want to apply for the fall semester at this university, you need to apply in the first application round (with deadline in November), as this is the only time fall semester spots will be offered Spring semester applicants: If you want to apply for the spring semester at this university, you need to apply in application round 1 (with deadline in November) or in application round 2 (with deadline in February - and only if there are vacant spots) as this is the only application rounds where the spots will be offered.

details.Description: Cergy Paris University is a public Institution and a leading centre of teaching and research. The University is composed of 5 departments: Law, Economy and Management, Languages, Literature and Social Sciences, Science and Technology. The University takes also part in the European exchange program and has adopted the ECTS system (European Credit Transfer System) which allows European students to obtain credits in their university for courses taken abroad. Cergy-Pontoise has been pointed out as a “Model University” several times by the French government. Cergy Paris is situated in the department of the Val-d’Oise in the Paris region. It is a dynamic city which offers a broad spectrum of artistic and cultural events thanks to its numerous theatres, museums and concert halls. From Paris it takes approx. 40 minutes by train to reach the town Cergy-Pontoise.
details.Agreement name: CY Cergy Paris Université - Erasmus - Law
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: Early September to December, incl. exams for English law courses. Exams for law courses taught in French are held in January. Winter semester: From January to May, incl. exams for English law courses. Orientation meetings are arranged in both semesters – attendance is compulsory.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: French is the main language of instruction at Université de Cergy Paris. Law classes are, however, taught in both French and in English. It is possible to take a full study load of 30 ECTS with law courses taught in English. There are no language requirements although some knowledge of French is recommended when you are in a French university.
details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. UCPH encourages our law students to apply for law courses offered on 3rd or 4th year.
details.Important links: See information for incoming exchange students (https://www.cyu.fr/en/international/students/come-in-exchange-program) - scroll down and in the right side of the screen find a document with English course offers. The Faculté de droit (http://www.droitucp.fr/) Cergy Paris University (https://www.u-cergy.fr/fr/index.html) See information about course offers (http://www.droitucp.fr/degrees-and-teaching-programs) . All law courses from ‘the Anglo-American Law Degree’ are open for exchange students and you can also take 2 law courses from the ‘LL.M. taught in English’.
details.Housing: See information on housing service (https://u-cergy.studapart.com/en/)
details.Scholarships: Students applying for this university are automatically nominated for the Erasmus+ scholarship
details.Additional information: See information on the French language Centre (https://www.cyu.fr/clf-centre-de-langue-francaise) See additional information in evaluations or experience reports from former students in Mobility Online or KUnet. Applying for pre-approval of courses: When you have received confirmation from UCPH about an exchange place at CY Cergy Paris Université, you must apply for pre-approval of the courses you intend to take as an exchange student. Usually course descriptions are not available online - but contact the study abroad coordinator at Faculty of Law of UCPH and ask for assistance to obtain course descriptions from Cergy Paris. Be aware that the processing time for applications of pre-approval of courses may take 4-6 weeks in Cph and the pre-approval of your courses have to be completed before you can obtain a signed learning agreement (containing your course titles). Your learning agreement has to be uploaded in your application for admission in late April. When the Faculty of Law in Copenhagen has nominated you for an exchange place at CY Cergy Paris Université, you have to apply for admission within the application deadline which may vary a bit from year to year. Current valid address: CY CERGY PARIS UNIVERSITÉ Incoming Mobility Office Tour des Chênes, 3e Étage, Bureau 318 33 Boulevard du Port 95011 CERGY-PONTOISE CEDEX FRANCE

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: English Language requirements: • TOEFL test with minimum 98 scores on the internet-based test (iBT). or • IELTS test with minimum 7.0 scores Please note that test scores must be less than two years old.
details.Restrictions: Law students must follow a full study load of min. 12 credits which corresponds to 30 ECTS per semester. Be aware that credit requirements may be different for other exchange students at Duke Law School. Observe that attendance in classes is mandatory - very little absence may be permitted approx. max 1-2 times!!
details.Course information: Generally, Duke Law School accepts very few exchange students per semester less than 10 exchange students will not be unusual; exchange students at Duke join approx. 100 international students in the LLM program (who are staying for a whole year program). Exchange students combined with LLM students are then enrolled in courses with American JD students. All students are graded on the same scale. The style of teaching is based on the socratic method, meaning students are actively involved by use of cold calling. The professors expect you to be well prepared for classes, so that you will be ready to answer questions or participate in class discussions, if you get called upon in class. Faculty members will make note of students with excessive absences and may refuse to allow such students to sit for exams. Some courses are not available to LLM or exchange students. Exchange students should therefore have alternative courses selected and approved by their home university in case their first choices are not available. Exchange administrators are encouraged to check with the International Studies department in advance with questions about course content and appropriateness of particular courses for exchange students.

details.Housing: Duke University does not provide on-campus housing. Housing suggestions are, however, made available to students via the Admitted Students Website, for which login and password information is issued after an admission offer is accepted. Apply for housing as soon as possible as it may be difficult to find housing for just one semester compared to LLM students who are renting for a whole year. May also be challenging with the local transportation offers, see reference to former student reports on this page.
details.Scholarships: Students applying for this university are automatically considered for KU’s Internationalisation scholarship.
details.Additional information: Though tuition is waived between the partner universities, students are responsible for educational fees. Bills are issued and normally due before students arrive on campus to begin their program. See info on the estimated fees below: • Health Fee - $484 • Healt Insurance $1,688 • Law Student Activity Fee - $75 • Graduate Student Activity Fee $20 • Graduate Student Services Fee - $12 • Transcript Fee - $120 • Recreation Fee - $187 • Books & Supplies - $729 General living expenses are not included in the figures above. Health Insurance Students with F1 or J1 visas are automatically enrolled in the Duke SMIP (Student Medical Insurance Plan). See additional info on enrollment or waiver proces. (https://students.duke.edu/wellness/studenthealth/insurance/) In addition to a possible mandatory insurance at your host university, UCPH recommends that Danish students on an exchange programme take out an insurance coverage with a Danish insurance company to make sure that you are sufficiently covered especially during your activities and trips outside the campus area of your host university and in case an urgent situation should occur with need of home transportation for DK.

details.Description: École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales (EHESS) is a distinguished graduate-only research institution, founded in 1984 as a grand établissement alongside the Collège de France and Sciences Po. With its main campus in Paris and additional sites in Marseille, Lyon, and Toulouse, EHESS is internationally recognized for its interdisciplinary approach to the social sciences and humanities. The university has been home to some of the most influential thinkers of the 20th century, including Pierre Bourdieu, Claude Lévi-Strauss, and Jacques Derrida. Today, EHESS hosts a diverse student body of approximately 3,000 students from around the world, drawn by its unique academic environment that combines rigorous historical analysis with contemporary research. Situated in central Paris, EHESS offers students an exceptional opportunity to study in one of Europe’s foremost intellectual and cultural capitals. The university’s location places students at the heart of a city renowned for its libraries, archives, museums, and vibrant academic life. Paris provides a stimulating backdrop for scholarly engagement, with countless opportunities to attend public lectures, exhibitions, and cultural events. For students seeking a rich academic experience alongside immersion in a dynamic urban setting, EHESS represents an ideal destination for an exchange semester.

details.Description: The École Normale Supérieure de Lyon (ENS de Lyon) is a highly selective French public institution focused on advanced education and research in the sciences and humanities. It hosts approximately 2,300 students and over 500 faculty and researchers. ENS de Lyon is part of the network of Écoles normales supérieures, known for preparing students for careers in academia and public service. The institution is distinguished by its strong emphasis on research-led teaching and its integration with national research bodies such as CNRS and INRIA. Its compact size and rigorous academic environment foster close interaction between students and researchers, offering a setting that differs from larger, more generalist universities. ENS de Lyon is located in the city of Lyon, France’s third-largest urban area and a major centre for education, culture, and innovation. The university’s campuses are situated in the Gerland district, which is well connected by public transport and close to both the Rhône river and the city’s central areas. Lyon combines historical architecture with modern infrastructure and is known for its role in the humanities, sciences, and gastronomy. The city offers a manageable scale, active student life, and access to cultural institutions, making it a practical and engaging place to spend an exchange semester. Its location in southeastern France also provides convenient links to other European cities and regions.

details.Description: Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), established in 1635, is Hungary's oldest and largest university, renowned for its academic excellence and research contributions. Situated in Budapest, ELTE offers a diverse range of programs across various disciplines, including humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, and law. The university provides courses in English, making it accessible to international students. With a commitment to fostering a dynamic learning environment, ELTE encourages critical thinking, interdisciplinary collaboration, and global perspectives. Students have the opportunity to engage in cutting-edge research and benefit from the expertise of distinguished faculty members. Located in the heart of Budapest, ELTE's campuses offer a blend of historical charm and modern facilities. The city, known for its rich cultural heritage and vibrant atmosphere, provides students with a unique living and learning experience. Budapest boasts a wide array of cultural attractions, including museums, theaters, and historic landmarks, as well as a lively student community. The city's efficient public transportation system ensures easy access to various parts of Budapest, allowing students to explore and immerse themselves in the local culture. Studying at ELTE offers not only academic growth but also the chance to experience life in one of Europe's most captivating cities.

details.Description: Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), established in 1635, is Hungary's oldest and largest university, renowned for its academic excellence and research contributions. Situated in Budapest, ELTE offers a diverse range of programs across various disciplines, including humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, and law. The university provides courses in English, making it accessible to international students. With a commitment to fostering a dynamic learning environment, ELTE encourages critical thinking, interdisciplinary collaboration, and global perspectives. Students have the opportunity to engage in cutting-edge research and benefit from the expertise of distinguished faculty members. Located in the heart of Budapest, ELTE's campuses offer a blend of historical charm and modern facilities. The city, known for its rich cultural heritage and vibrant atmosphere, provides students with a unique living and learning experience. Budapest boasts a wide array of cultural attractions, including museums, theaters, and historic landmarks, as well as a lively student community. The city's efficient public transportation system ensures easy access to various parts of Budapest, allowing students to explore and immerse themselves in the local culture. Studying at ELTE offers not only academic growth but also the chance to experience life in one of Europe's most captivating cities.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: Early September to mid-December, exams not incl. Winter semester: Early February to mid-May, exams not included. See link to academic calendar (https://www.elte.hu/en/academic_calendar?m=73) (the exam periods are mostly directed to the local students)

You can apply for a language confirmation from the Faculty of Law in Copenhagen and the confirmation will be based on your grades in English from your ‘studentereksamen’ or HF diploma. A language confirmation will only be needed after you have been nominated to the exchange programme at Eötvös Loránd University.
details.Restrictions: Exchange programme for both bachelor and master level law students. As a law exchange student, you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. Generally, all law courses have the value of 5 ECTS credits. In order to complete a course, it is required that you attend the class; you can only miss 2 classes in a course during one semester. Courses are accessible for both bachelor and master level exchange students.

details.Description: Erasmus University Rotterdam is a leading international research university known for its strong focus on societal impact and academic excellence. Established in 1913, the university offers a wide range of programs in economics, business, law, social sciences, health, and humanities. It is particularly renowned for its Erasmus School of Economics and Rotterdam School of Management, both of which enjoy global recognition. With a student population of over 30,000, including a large international community, Erasmus University fosters an intellectually stimulating and diverse academic environment. Its interdisciplinary approach and emphasis on real-world relevance make it an ideal destination for students seeking a forward-thinking and globally connected exchange experience. Located in the vibrant city of Rotterdam, the university offers students the opportunity to live and study in one of Europe’s most innovative urban centers. Rotterdam is known for its modern architecture, dynamic cultural scene, and status as a major international port city. The city’s youthful energy, excellent public transport, and wide range of cultural and recreational activities make it especially appealing to students. Whether exploring contemporary art museums, attending music festivals, or enjoying the city’s waterfront, exchange students will find Rotterdam to be a lively and inspiring place to complement their academic journey at Erasmus University.

details.Description: Established in 1855 as the Federal Polytechnical School, ETH Zurich has from the outset been a national centre for education with international appeal, attracting talent from all over the world. Today, ETH Zurich is one of the leading international universities for technology and the natural sciences. It is well known for its excellent education, ground-breaking fundamental research and for implementing its results directly into practice. ETH Zurich has more than 18,500 students from over 110 countries. 21 Nobel Laureates have studied, taught or conducted research at ETH Zurich, underlining the excellent reputation of the university.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: September - February Spring semester: February - September Academic calendar (https://ethz.ch/en/studies/non-degree-courses/exchange/about-the-study-programmes/academic-calendar-and-exam-schedule.html)
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: CEFR certificate: German/English B2 (accepted). C1 (recommended)
details.Restrictions: You should have completed two years of study (120 ECTS) before enrolling at ETH. Please note that some courses are restricted, e.g., in the number of participants and that you cannot register for any courses ending with –AAL. 2/3 of your course credits must be offered by the department you are applying to. 1/3 of your credits can be taken from other departments and / or the University of Zurich. Students are free to combine Bachelor and Master courses, independent of their level of studies at the home university, provided they have the necessary prerequisites to follow the courses. There is not limit as to the amount of MSc courses Bachelor students can take. You will be studying at the Department of Biology (D-BIOL). At D-BIOL, you can choose their semester program between block and concept courses. If you want to write you bachelor’s thesis at ETH Zurich, you must enclose written confirmation from your supervisor at ETH Zurich in your application. Research projects are expected to be full-time and part of your exchange stay. A combination of course work and research project must be discussed with the supervisor. It is not possible to write your thesis project as an exchange student at ETH Zurich.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: B2 - English and/or C1 - German B2 - English corresponds to level B  whereas C1 - German corresponds to level A in the Danish upper secondary school. See detailed description of language levels at the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale) Once UCPH nominate you for exchange, the host university will inform you which kind of documentation they require as proof of your language skills.
details.Study plan: Bachelor’s students: 15 ECTS courses and 15 ECTS research project. Master’s students: 30 ECTS courses or 15 ECTS courses and 15 ECTS research project. Research projects: Before applying for exchange, please make sure the university offers relevant research. Once UCPH has nominated you for the exchange (after the application process at UCPH), you need to find: A supervising professor who will accept you. Please note that this will take some time and work on your behalf (please start as early as possible). Below at 'Important links' find access to additional guidance. A good place to start looking for a suitable project is the ETH department or institute (https://chab.ethz.ch/en/studies/master/pharmsciences.html) you would be interested in joining. Check the information and contact professors you are interested in directly. It is up to the you (both BSc and MSc) to reach an agreement with a professor at ETH for supervision of your project. If one of your professors at your home university has research contacts at ETH Zurich and can recommend a suitable project for you and establish contact with a professor here, this would of course be very helpful. Some projects offered at ETH are also published by SiROP - find research projects at SiROP (https://sirop.org/app/) . You can search for projects through the portal SiROP. It is up to you, and probably also in discussion with your supervisor, how many ECTS you would like to invest in a project. But please note the number of ECTS is either 5, 10, 15 or 20. At the very latest, you must have secured a supervisor by the beginning of the semester. Students who are unable to secure a supervisor will be expected to take courses instead. Please note that each course at ETH awards very few ECTS, so it may be preferable to combine research projects and courses.

details.Scholarships: Financing Students applying for this university have so far been automatically nominated for a SEMP (Swiss-European Mobility Program) grant. Switzerland is currently seeking to join the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 if they will join. As a result, students applying for exchange places in Switzerland will receive either a SEMP grant or an Erasmus Scholarship. The Heyning-Roelli Foundation provides scholarships to talented but financially underprivileged students for travel and subsistence expenses. Please note that these are external funds and do not affect scholarships already granted within SEMP. Information about the conditions and application process for the Heyning-Roelli Foundation. (http://www.heyning-roelli-stiftung.ch/fakten_en_page2.html)

details.Description: Established in 1855 as the Federal Polytechnical School, ETH Zurich has from the outset been a national centre for education with international appeal, attracting talent from all over the world. Today, ETH Zurich is one of the leading international universities for technology and the natural sciences. It is well known for its excellent education, ground-breaking fundamental research and for implementing its results directly into practice. ETH Zurich has more than 18,500 students from over 110 countries. 21 Nobel Laureates have studied, taught or conducted research at ETH Zurich, underlining the excellent reputation of the university.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: September - February Spring semester: February - September Academic calendar (https://ethz.ch/en/studies/non-degree-courses/exchange/about-the-study-programmes/academic-calendar-and-exam-schedule.html)

details.Restrictions: You should have completed two years of study (120 ECTS) before enrolling at ETH. Please note that some courses are restricted, e.g., in the number of participants and that you cannot register for any courses ending with –AAL. 2/3 of your course credits must be offered by the department you are applying to. 1/3 of your credits can be taken from other departments and / or the University of Zurich. Students are free to combine Bachelor and Master courses, independent of their level of studies at the home university, provided they have the necessary prerequisites to follow the courses. There is not limit as to the amount of MSc courses Bachelor students can take. You will be studying at the Department of Physics (D-PHYS). If you want to do a research project or write you bachelor’s thesis at ETH, you must enclose written confirmation from your supervisor at ETH Zurich in your application. Projectwork is expected to be full-time. A combination of course work and a project must be discussed with the supervisor. It is not possible to write your thesis project as an exchange student at ETH Zurich.

details.Additional requirements (academic - deta: Semester Fulfillment Undergraduate students must have completed at least one (1) semester before the application stage at Ewha begins (i.e. before March for exchange in the following Fall Semester, and before September for exchange in the following Spring Semester). Graduate students must have completed at least one (1) semester at graduate-level before the application stage at Ewha begins (i.e. before March for exchange in the following Fall Semester, and before September for exchange in the following Spring Semester). Graduate students must provide official transcript of graduate-level studies (undergraduate level GPA is not considered). This means that graduate students should consider Ewha Womans University for exchange only during the third or fourth semester of their graduate programme.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (:

details.Study load for undergraduate students: 15 credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Study load for graduate students: 9 credits = 30 ECTS - Conversion and levels: Study load is calculated according to the level of the specific course. Please note that not all UCPH Master’s (graduate) programmes allow credit transfer of bachelor (undergraduate) courses into their programmes. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: AVAILABLE COURSES / FACULTIES Undergraduate Level: General courses are available. Restriction may apply to: Art & Design, Music, ELTEC Engineering, Education, Scranton Honors Program, and HOKMA College of General Education. Nursing, Medicine, Pharmacy are not available . Graduate Level: The Graduate School courses are available. Some courses in the Graduate School of International Studies are available. English-taught courses of School of Law are available. Courses in the Graduate School of Business courses are available for graduate students only. The Professional Schools, the Special Graduate Schools are not available , except those mentioned above.

details.Description: Freie Universität Berlin, established in 1948, is one of Germany’s top research universities and a member of the German Excellence Strategy. It has around 33,900 students, including a large international community, and offers over 150 degree programs across the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, and life sciences. The university is known for its strong interdisciplinary approach and global partnerships, with over 400 Erasmus+ agreements and numerous collaborations worldwide. Research is a central part of its mission, supported by institutes like the Otto Suhr Institute for Political Science and the Dahlem Research School for doctoral training. Located in the green and residential district of Dahlem in southwest Berlin, the university offers a peaceful academic setting with easy access to the city’s vibrant culture and public transportation. Students can explore Berlin’s rich history, diverse neighborhoods, and thriving arts and cultural scenes while studying at a campus known for its modern facilities and international outlook. The city’s dynamic atmosphere, combined with Freie Universität’s strong academic reputation, makes it an attractive destination for exchange students.

details.Description: Freie Universität Berlin, established in 1948, is one of Germany’s top research universities and a member of the German Excellence Strategy. It has around 33,900 students, including a large international community, and offers over 150 degree programs across the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, and life sciences. The university is known for its strong interdisciplinary approach and global partnerships, with over 400 Erasmus+ agreements and numerous collaborations worldwide. Research is a central part of its mission, supported by institutes like the Otto Suhr Institute for Political Science and the Dahlem Research School for doctoral training. Located in the green and residential district of Dahlem in southwest Berlin, the university offers a peaceful academic setting with easy access to the city’s vibrant culture and public transportation. Students can explore Berlin’s rich history, diverse neighborhoods, and thriving arts and cultural scenes while studying at a campus known for its modern facilities and international outlook. The city’s dynamic atmosphere, combined with Freie Universität’s strong academic reputation, makes it an attractive destination for exchange students.

details.Description:
Fudan consists of 29 schools and departments, with seventy undergraduate disciplines. The
University confers bachelor's degrees in seventy academic disciplines, and master's degrees
in two hundred and twenty five disciplines (with fifty of them established by the University
itself), and doctoral degrees in twenty-four Level I and one hundred and fifty-three Level II
academic disciplines (with twenty-nine of them established by the University itself). There
are also twenty-five research stations that offer postdoctoral fellowships. Fudan now has an enrollment of 26,792 full-time degree candidates. Another 20,670 are
studying at the schools of Continuing Education and Online Education. Besides, the
University's population of foreign students is 2,812 today.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: An English language proficiency of an academic level is required. However, Danish law students can be exempt from language test requirements, provided that you have a Danish ‘studentereksamensbevis’ or ‘HF’ diploma with English lessons taken at A level. This will correspond to C1 in the CEFR self-assessment grid (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) . After you have been nominated you can then apply for language confirmation where you indicate that a language level of C1 is required. Without a language confirmation of level C1, Fudan University will require that you take a language test with the following minimum test scores: 90 points on the internet-baset TOEFL or 6.5 points on the IELTS.
details.Restrictions: At least two years of previous law studies when law is studied at the undergraduate level or at least one year of previous law studies when law is studied at a graduate level. As stated above, 12 credits correspond to 30 ECTS per semester, please be aware that credit requirements may be different for other exchange students at Fudan School of Law. Exchange students can choose courses for undergraduates if there is any vacancy and at most two courses for LL.M. Program. Generally around late June, the exact course table for the coming fall will be ready and Fudan University will then send an electronic version to exchange students by email.

In addition to your law studies at Fudan University, you will have the possibility of exploring Shanghai, China and the Asian culture. Visa: All non-Chinese citizens must obtain a student visa / residency permit for their study as an exchange student at Fudan Law School. Below 'Reports' please study the travel reports from the former UCPH students who went on student exchange to Fudan University. Although the travel reports may come from students within other student areas, the reports will contail valuable information for all UCPH students.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Chinese Language Program : No language requirements English proficiency: TOEFL IBT above 90 or IELTS score above 6.5 (no items below 6.0) is required. TOEFL MyBest Scores are acceptable. TOEFL/IELTS score should be valid (within two years after test date) at the time of enrollment to Fudan. Chinese proficiency: If you intend to take Chinese-taught courses, you need to be either a native speaker of Chinese or have an HSK level 5 score of 210. HSK score is only necessary if you intend to take Chinese-taught courses. You do NOT need an HSK score if you are a native speaker of Chinese or if you do not intend to take Chinese-taught courses.
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 12 credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Study load for graduate students: 12 credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Conversion and levels: Study load is calculated according to the level of the specific course. Please note that not all UCPH Master’s (graduate) programmes allow credit transfer of bachelor (undergraduate) courses into their programmes. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.

Other restrictions include : MBA courses, LLM courses, medical courses, special programs in faculties (e.g. International Cultural Exchange School), undergraduate courses in medicine. details.Description: The FGV Direito Rio (Fundação Getúlio Vargas Rio de Janeiro Law School) is a Brazilian private law School for higher education founded in 2002 in Rio de Janeiro by the Fundação Getúlio Vargas.
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: Runs from early August to the end of December - an orientation day included. Spring semester: Runs from February to July Each semester has 2 exam weeks. Dates are decided in the beginning of each semester.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: There are no language test requirements. See info on the availability of courses taught in English below at 'course information'. Be aware that all FGV homepage information at Law School is stated in Portuguese (generally with translation options), but still it may be difficult to retrieve all necessary information during an exchange program without any previous knowledge of Portuguese.
details.Study load for graduate students: A full study load of 30 ECTS per semester corresponds to 120 hours in total.
details.Restrictions: Exchange students are generally encouraged to take at least one law course taught in Portuguese, which of course would require sufficient language skills.
details.Course information: FGV has a 5-year law programme at undergraduate level and a two-year law programme at graduate level. A new master degree in Business Law and Arbitration is now being offered. If you want to attend law courses taugth in English then expect to take courses at undergraduate level, as nearly all courses at master level are taught in Portuguese (maybe 1-2 courses in English). Although you are a master level student during your exchange programme, you will also be allowed to register for law courses at both undergraduate and graduate level at FGV. An add and drop period for courses is generally offered at the beginning of each semester. Be aware that credit requirements may be different for other exchange students at FGV Direito Rio. FGV works with hours and not ECTS credits. The courses offered may have a duration of 30, 45 or 60 hours in total (preparation time is not included). A course of 30 hours would e.g. correspond to a course of 7.5 ECTS. FGV may encourage you to take courses from other faculties but in order to take such courses you must obtain a pre-approval for each course in advance from the Study Board in Copenhagen.

FGV does not offer accommodation, but the international office can advise students

details.Scholarships: Students applying for this university are automatically considered for KU’s Internationalisation scholarship.
details.Additional information: The University of FGV is situated in Rio de Janeiro at the southeastern coast of the Atlantic Ocean in Brazil with approximately 6.7 million inhabitants. The University itself is rather small educational institution with approx. 600 students in total at FGV Rio Law. You may expect that several exchange students going to FGV will be able to speak Portuguese - perhaps leaving only a minor group of exchange students being dependent on English courses and conversation in English. As part of the exchange program, you will have the possibility of exploring the huge city or Rio de Janeiro, the amazing scenery, the Brazilian culture and all along improve your academic skills.

details.Description: Goethe Universität Frankfurt am Main is one of Germany’s leading research universities, known for its strong academic tradition and international orientation. Founded in 1914, the university offers a wide range of disciplines across its 16 faculties, with particular strengths in economics, law, social sciences, and natural sciences. It is home to several prestigious research institutes and maintains close ties with the city’s financial and cultural institutions. With a student population of over 45,000, including a significant number of international students, Goethe University fosters a vibrant and diverse academic community. Its commitment to interdisciplinary research and critical inquiry makes it an attractive destination for students seeking a rigorous and globally connected exchange experience. Situated in Frankfurt am Main, Germany’s financial capital and one of Europe’s most cosmopolitan cities, Goethe University offers students a dynamic urban environment rich in professional and cultural opportunities. Frankfurt is known for its impressive skyline, international institutions, and thriving arts scene. The city combines modern infrastructure with historical charm, offering easy access to museums, theaters, and green spaces along the River Main. Its central location in Europe also makes it an ideal base for travel and exploration. For students looking to combine academic excellence with the experience of living in a global metropolis, Goethe Universität Frankfurt am Main presents an outstanding choice for an exchange semester.

details.Description: Goldsmiths was founded in 1891 and has been part of the University of London since 1904 – being a creative powerhouse with a rich academic heritage. Today, Goldsmiths has a close-knit community, with students and staff from around the world who are inventive, imaginative and original. Goldsmiths offers a range of undergraduate and postgraduate study options in the arts, humanities, social sciences, cultural studies, computing, and entrepreneurial business and management, all on a friendly, accessible, single-site campus. At just a 10-minute train ride from London Bridge, it’s easy to access all central London has to offer, while being based in a vibrant and diverse local area.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: For students studying for a single term , a language confirmation from UCPH will be satisfactory. After the nomination process, you will be able to retrieve a language confirmation from UCPH in Mobility Online certifying that you have an English language level equivalent to B2 on the European CEFR (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) .  As a UCPH student you fullfill the requirements of an English level of B2 from your previous studies before your enrolment at UCPH. Generally, the official English language requirement is CEFR Level B2, or for undergraduates an IELTS language test score of 6.0 overall. For postgraduates, IELTS score must be 6.5 overall. You can find a list of English language qualifications on this page (https://www.gold.ac.uk/apply/english-language-requirements/) . Alternative documentation of your language qualifications may also be accepted, see Alternative English Requirements (https://www.gold.ac.uk/apply/english-language-requirements/) and check info below 'Danish STX/HF ...'.

details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . As a result, students applying for exchange places in the UK cannot be guaranteed an Erasmus+ grant at the time of application. Eligibility for Erasmus+ funding will depend on whether the host university joins the programme and concludes an Erasmus+ agreement with the University of Copenhagen. Students nominated to a UK university will be informed of their grant eligibility no later than March 2027.

details.Description: Since 1975, our teaching and research have been shaped by a commitment to social justice, environmental sustainability and inclusive access to education. Today, those ideals are more important than ever. As we enter the second half of Griffith’s first century as a globally recognised university of excellence, we’re building on this legacy by placing purpose, people, partnerships and communities squarely at the centre of what we do. From pioneering research and student entrepreneurship to supporting Indigenous flourishing and expanding access to education through online learning, we’re continuously adding to our history of making a difference in the world around us. With more than 40,000 students, our community spans five campuses across South East Queensland plus our Digital campus. We’re also proud to be home to a global alumni network of over 200,000 graduates. See what it is like studying at Griffith University! (https://youtu.be/4ghHz0zdTS0)

details.Study load for graduate students: 40 credit points = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Conversion and levels: Study load is calculated according to the level of the specific course. details.Description: In today's world where creativity and discoveries are of utmost importance, our place in the world will be determined by the scientists we train. The main aim of graduate education in neuroscience, especially doctoral education, is to train scientists who can conduct research independently. The mission of our institute is to contribute to the production of science and technology in neurological sciences, to train scientists, and to serve as an umbrella for multidisciplinary studies in the field of clinical and basic neurological sciences. Hacettepe University Institute of Neurological Sciences is among the first institutes preferred by students who want to receive doctoral education in the field of neurological sciences in Turkey. Vision of our Institute: To open research and education functions in neurological sciences to national and international interaction and exchange by using the latest technological methods, and to be an internationally recognised and preferred institute.
