details.Description: Established in 1386, the University of Heidelberg holds the distinction of being the oldest university in Germany, embodying a legacy of knowledge and intellectual pursuit that spans centuries. With a community of over 31,000 students, including approximately 6,000 international students, it provides a vibrant and inclusive environment for higher education. Nestled by the picturesque lake Neckar, the campus offers a serene and inspiring backdrop for academic pursuits, fostering a conducive atmosphere for learning and personal growth. Recognized as one of the strongest research universities in Europe, the institution boasts 12 faculties encompassing a diverse range of disciplines. These faculties, such as Biosciences, Chemistry and Earth Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science, Physics and Astronomy, Philosophy, Modern Languages, Theology, Law, Economics and Social Sciences, Behavioral and Cultural Studies, and Medicine, offer comprehensive academic programs that cater to a wide array of interests and career paths. Through a commitment to rigorous research and innovation, the university cultivates an environment that fuels intellectual curiosity and advances knowledge in various fields. Heidelberg is a compact and picturesque city located along the Neckar River in southwestern Germany. Known for its Baroque architecture, cobblestone streets, and vibrant cultural life, the city offers a student-friendly environment with efficient public transport and a strong cycling culture. The city’s historic center is home to cafés, bookstores, and cultural venues, all within walking distance of the university. A fun fact: tucked inside Heidelberg Castle is the world’s largest wine barrel, the Heidelberg Tun, built in 1751 with a capacity of over 219,000 liters—though it was only filled three times due to persistent leaks.

details.Agreement name: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology - Faculty of Science
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Description: HKUST - School of Science The School of Science comprises 5 academic units that offer a wide variety of courses and programs in biological science, chemical science, mathematical science, ocean science and physical science. Exchange students may take a combination of courses across different disciplines, with priority in taking courses offered by the School of Science.
details.Language requirements: Proficient in English , as courses are mainly conducted in English
details.Restrictions: Course information is available at Course Catalog (http://publish.ust.hk/prog_crs/index.html) . Course Restrictions Generally speaking, science exchange students will have priority in taking science courses including chemistry, environmental science, life science, mathematics, ocean science and physics. For courses offered in other Schools, it will be subject to the availability of seats and approval of the course instructor. Due to limited seats, exchange students are unlikely to enroll in chemistry laboratory courses. Course Levels Exchange students are expected to take mainly courses at undergraduate level. Science exchange students are allowed to take postgraduate courses subject to the requirements of the course pre-requisites (if any), the availability of seats and approval of the course instructor. Please note that postgraduate courses for exchange students are limited since most are under the self-financed programs which are not open to exchange students.
details.Important links: HKUST School of Science: Incoming International Exchange Program (https://hkust.edu.hk/) HKUST School of Science (https://hkust.edu.hk/) Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) (https://hkust.edu.hk/)
details.Housing: University-provided Housing Students will be arranged with university accommodation as far as possible. More information is available at https://studyabroad.hkust.edu.hk/inbound/arrival/living-matters/ (https://studyabroad.hkust.edu.hk/inbound/arrival/living-matters/) . Students are required to complete the housing application procedures on or before the deadline designated by the Student Housing and Residential Life Office. More details will be provided in the admission package to exchange students. Self-arranged Accommodation HKUST also provides students with relevant information and advice on self-arranged accommodation, please refer to http://shrl.ust.hk/ (http://shrl.ust.hk/) for details.

details.Description: HKUST - School of Humanities and Social Science (SHSS) School of Humanities and Social Science comprises three divisions – the Division of Humanities (https://huma.ust.hk/) , the Division of Social Science (https://sosc.hkust.edu.hk/) and the Center for Language Education (http://cle.ust.hk/)
details.Academic calendar: HKUST Academic Calendar (https://registry.hkust.edu.hk/resource-library/academic-calendar)
details.GPA for undergraduate admission: No specified requirements. Students are normally expected to have completed 2 years of undergraduate study by the start of the exchange, and be in good academic standing at their home institution.
details.GPA for graduate admission: No specified requirements. Good academic standing
details.Restrictions: Course information Exchange students can select SHSS courses as long as they meet the prerequisite requirements and subject to space availabilities. Some courses may require professor approval for enrollment. Courses offered by SHSS are identified by the following prefixes in the course codes: HUMA , SOSC , SHSS Undergraduate (UG) / Postgraduate (PG) course offering varies by semester. Below past year course is for reference purpose only: Social Science Courses: UG https://prog-crs.hkust.edu.hk/ugcourse/2024-25/SOSC (https://prog-crs.hkust.edu.hk/ugcourse/2024-25/SOSC) PG https://prog-crs.hkust.edu.hk/pgcourse/2024-25/SOSC (https://prog-crs.hkust.edu.hk/pgcourse/2024-25/SOSC) Humanities Courses: UG https://prog-crs.hkust.edu.hk/ugcourse/2024-25/HUMA (https://prog-crs.hkust.edu.hk/ugcourse/2024-25/HUMA) PG https://prog-crs.hkust.edu.hk/pgcourse/2024-25/HUMA (https://prog-crs.hkust.edu.hk/pgcourse/2024-25/HUMA) Language Courses: UG / PG https://cle.hkust.edu.hk/courses (https://cle.hkust.edu.hk/courses) Restrictions - SSMA, MGCS, MALS, MALE, HMMA - Students who are not enrolled in these special programs normally are not allowed to register for these courses. - ACCT, ECON, FINA, ISOM, MARK, MGMT - Due to availabilities and capacity reserved to HKUST business degree seeking students. Business courses at postgraduate (PG) level (i.e. 5000-level or above) are reserved for special business programs and are closed to students who are not in the program. Therefore, exchange students admitted to the School of Humanities and Social Science should NOT plan on taking business courses at PG level. Enrollment to courses outside SHSS (for example, business) is not available.
details.Important links: HKUST SHSS - Inbound Exchange Program Overview (https://shss.hkust.edu.hk/global_experience/exchange_in_overview)
details.Housing: Information on on-campus accommodation can be found at the Student Housing and Residential Life Office (SHLO) (https://shrl.ust.hk/) . Given the limited supply of on-campus housing, PG exchange-in students are advised to arrange off-campus accommodation by themselves. The Off-Campus Housing Section of Student Housing Office (https://offcamphouse.ust.hk/) provides general assistance for students who are looking for off-campus accommodation.

details.Description: Humboldt University of Berlin is a public research university in the central borough of Mitte in Berlin, Germany. It was established by Frederick William III on the initiative of Wilhelm von Humboldt, Johann Gottlieb Fichte and Friedrich Ernst Daniel Schleiermacher as the University of Berlin (Universität zu Berlin) in 1809, and opened in 1810, making it the oldest of Berlin's four universities. HU is divided into nine faculties, including its medical school shared with the Free University of Berlin, has a student enrollment of around 33,000 students, and offers degree programmes in some 189 disciplines from undergraduate to postdoctorate level. Past and present faculty and notable alumni include an impressive 57 Nobel Prize laureates as well as eminent philosophers, sociologists, artists, lawyers, politicians, mathematicians, scientists, and Heads of State; among them are Albert Einstein, Karl Marx, Friedrich Engels, Otto von Bismarck, W. E. B. Du Bois, Angela Davis, Arthur Schopenhauer, Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel, Walter Benjamin, Max Weber, Georg Simmel, Karl Liebknecht, Ernst Cassirer, Heinrich Heine, Max Planck, and the Brothers Grimm.

details.Academic calendar: Winter semester: Mid-October until around Mid-February. Exams are normally held two weeks after the end of the lectures, i.e., until end of Feb or early March. Summer semester: Mid-April until Mid-July. Exams are normally held two weeks after the end of the lectures, i.e., until the end of July or early August An orientation week is held each semester one week before the start of the lectures. details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Be aware that 95% of all law courses/modules are taught in German. In addition, information about timetables, exams, registration processes will only be available in German. Humboldt Universität requires that all incoming exchange students take an online German language test (called the C-Test). After the application round in Cph there will be an application process for Humboldt where this test is taken online with texts to be filled in and parts of reading, understanding, and giving summaries; the C-test is all in writing, no oral part. If your result is less than 50 points, you must apply for an intensive course in German at the Humboldt Universität (HU) language center (Sprachenzentrum) and send the confirmation of this application to HU. Preconditions for the admission will be the passed test (equivalent to level B2 with 50 points) or the intensive course. If you have (almost) no knowledge of German and plan to attend courses exclusively in English , please be aware that the range of courses offered in English at the Faculty of Law is very limited and that in some semesters fewer courses than usual are offered. In this case, it may be difficult to achieve the number of ECTS credits required by your home university if you are required to take law courses. The language centre of Humboldt Universität offers a number of language courses for international students as well as intensive courses before the beginning of each semester (or during the semester).
details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student, you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. SWS-indication – transferred to ECTS value: All Law classes taught in German have an “SWS” indication showing the number of class hours per week. Courses with 2 SWS = 5 ECTS, 4 SWS = 10 ECTS and 6 SWS = 15 ECTS. In some course descriptions you may find LP-values which will also correspond to course ECTS-values. The law programme at Humboldt Universität is not divided into a bachelor and master degree. Therefore, the whole range of elective courses are offered to both so-called 'bachelor' and 'master' students. If the catalogue for the upcoming semester is not online yet, please use the one from the year before, since the courses are, in general, the same. The style of teaching at Humboldt Universität may be characterized as a bit old school with a teacher giving lectures and the students listening and taking notes. Generally, there is very little group work or group presentations, i.e. less active student involvement.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: All bachelor’s courses are taught in German and generally a full exchange programme with courses taught in English cannot be guaranteed - you may need to take courses taught in German. Please observe that there may be different language requirements when applying for a master’s course. Generally, the required level of German language skills is level B2 or C1 on the European self-assessment CEFR-grid (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) . details.Restrictions: Special language and math requirements for the School of Business and Economics The language of instruction of all the department's Master programs is English. The courses at the School of Business and Economics have a strong emphasis on imparting rigorous and quantitative methods of economic analysis and management science. A strong background in Mathematics is essential. Access to admission restricted undergraduate courses: Applicants from EU-Countries as well as from Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway are allowed to apply for a maximum of three admission-restricted (NC) undergraduate courses (Bachelor’s or State Examination courses). Furthermore, these applicants are allowed to indicate (and apply for) an additional non-admission-restricted (non-NC) course of studies in the application. details.Academic calendar: The start date of your exchange period depends on the study plan you will be following abroad. Once you have been nominated for an exchange place, you and the coordinators at the host university will plan where you should start and end your stay. Normally, you will start your exchange in early March (spring semester) or early October (autumn semester).
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: B1 – German B1 German corresponds to B level at Danish upper secondary school. For a more detailed description, see the Council of Europe’s website. (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale)
details.Restrictions: The coordinator at the host university will help organise your first clinical stay. You will be informed of the contents of your first clinical stay before your trip. You cannot arrange your second clinical stay until you have arrived at the host university. So please note that you will not know the content of your second clinical stay until after you have arrived. Even though you do not know the academic content of your entire stay abroad before you leave, you must still follow the normal procedure and apply for an advance transfer of credits. This means that you must apply for an advance transfer of credits at least six weeks before the start of your stay abroad. You must attach a preliminary plan for the second clinical training period when you apply for an advance transfer of credits. Once you know the contents of your second clinical training period after you arrive at Charité, you can apply for another advance transfer of credits.
details.Study plan: Second semester of master’s programme When you spend your second semester at a foreign university, you must follow this study plan: • Five weeks of internal medicine • Five weeks of surgery • Two weeks of anaesthesia Read more about spending the second semester abroad on Study Information. (https://kunet.ku.dk/studie/medicin-ka/Sider/Emne.aspx?topicid=549e18de-2ced-41cc-a674-3e965197799a#1036731_noPictureOnTop_content) Fifth semester on the master’s programme: “International Perspective with a Stay in a Clinic Abroad” When you spend your fifth semester at a foreign university, you must follow the following study plan: •12-14 weeks of elective clinical training Read more about doing the fifth semester abroad on Study Information. (https://kunet.ku.dk/studie/medicin-ka/Sider/Emne.aspx?topicid=549e18de-2ced-41cc-a674-3e965197799a#1036739_noPictureOnTop_content)

details.Additional information: On your exchange in the fifth semester, you have the opportunity to prepare your own study plan based on the specialisations offered by the university hospital. You will need to agree your final study plan with the coordinators at the host university, depending on their capacity and availability.

details.Description: The University of Greenland, known as Ilisimatusarfik, is the leading institution of higher education in Greenland and offers a unique academic experience shaped by Arctic perspectives. It is a small university with around 200 to 300 students. The university offers courses mainly in Greenlandic and Danish, with some courses available in English. The main campus is located in Nuuk. Nuuk is a small yet dynamic city surrounded by dramatic mountains and fjords, offering a blend of traditional Greenlandic culture and modern living. The city is compact and walkable, with short distances between most areas. The natural surroundings provide endless opportunities for outdoor exploration, including hiking, kayaking, and witnessing the northern lights, making it an inspiring place for students seeking both cultural immersion and adventure.

details.Description: As the UK’s only university focusing entirely on science, engineering, medicine and business, Imperial College London is truly unique, and in the QS World University Rankings 2022 came in at number 7. Founded in 1907, Imperial’s expertise now spreads across nine campuses – six medical campuses, the centre for ecology, evolution, and conservation at Silwood Park, and White City Campus, the new 25-acre base for researchers, businesses and healthcare experts to work alongside each other.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: Late September - Mid-December Spring semester: Early January - late March/Late-June Term Dates: Term 1 (Autumn Term) Late September to mid-December Term 2 (Spring Term) Early January to mid-March Term 3 (Summer Term) Late April to late June
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Confirmation from SCIENCE Study Administration
details.Study load: 30 ECTS per semester
details.Restrictions: You should have completed two years of study (120 ECTS) at university level prior to entry to Imperial College. You can only apply to one academic department, and cannot apply to more than one academic department.. Please note that Imperial College does not operate a semester system. The College has a term system. You are advised to study for a full academic year at Imperial College, including research project works. If you only wish to go for one semester, you are advised to go for either the autumn or the spring + summer term. The courses/modules you select, including projects, must be from the appropriate curriculum of the host (admitting) academic department. For example, if you will be applying as an undergraduate then the appropriate curriculum would be the “undergraduate” curriculum. You are advised to select courses from a single year of the undergraduate curriculum Imperial College does not currently publish a single module catalogue (curriculum). A module catalogue (undergraduate curriculum/syllabus) which will refer to the ECTS applicable and other relevant information required by a prospective exchange student can be obtained from the exchange programme co-ordinator for the department to which a prospective exchange student is seeking admission: More information (https://www.imperial.ac.uk/placements/student-exchanges/information-for-student-exchange-partner-universities/) VERY IMPORTANT: Timetables (for courses/modules in a single academic department) are normally confirmed during September, but occasionally not until the beginning of the academic year; therefore it is normally not possible to confirm any programme of study until you have arrived at the College. Expect to have to make modifications to your initial study plan after your arrival. Term Dates: Term 1 (Autumn Term) Late September to mid-December Term 2 (Spring Term) Early January to mid-March Term 3 (Summer Term) Late April to late June

If you decide to study at Imperial College for one semester, you are advised to find your own accommodation.
details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . As a result, students applying for exchange places in the UK cannot be guaranteed an Erasmus+ grant at the time of application. Eligibility for Erasmus+ funding will depend on whether the host university joins the programme and concludes an Erasmus+ agreement with the University of Copenhagen. Students nominated to a UK university will be informed of their grant eligibility no later than March 2027.
details.Additional information: You will be studying at the Department of Life Sciences, which is based on two campuses: South Kensington and Silwood Park.

details.Description: Founded in 1948, Sciences Po Lyon is a public higher education institute specializing in Human and Social Sciences and training future executives in the public and private sectors. The educational model is similar to that of Anglo-Saxon Schools of Public Affairs or School of Government. Their teaching is fueled by a constant quest for excellence and cultivates a multi-disciplinary approach in human and social sciences based on four fundamental disciplines: history, law, political science, and economy. Since 2017, Sciences Po Lyon has operated two campuses: the historical campus in Lyon city centre and a second in Saint-Étienne. International students who visit us for a semester or a full academic year will study on the Lyon campus. With its 1,800 students, Sciences Po Lyon is a higher education institute of a size that enables it to retain a human touch, offering optimal study conditions that can benefit each and every individual student.

details.Description: Institut d'Études Politiques de Toulouse, commonly known as Sciences Po Toulouse, is a selective and prestigious institution specializing in political science, international relations, law, economics, and sociology. Founded in 1948, it is part of the network of Sciences Po institutes across France and is recognized for its rigorous academic programs and strong emphasis on interdisciplinary research. Sciences Po Toulouse offers a dynamic learning environment with a student body of around 1,500, including a growing number of international students. The institution is particularly committed to preparing students for careers in public service, international organizations, and policy-making, while also fostering critical thinking and civic engagement. Located in the vibrant city of Toulouse, Sciences Po offers students a unique blend of academic excellence and quality of life. Toulouse is the fourth-largest city in France and a major center for aerospace, innovation, and higher education. Known for its rich history, lively cultural scene, and welcoming atmosphere, the city provides an ideal setting for student life. With its mix of historic architecture, green spaces, and bustling cafés, Toulouse offers both inspiration and comfort. Exchange students at Sciences Po Toulouse benefit not only from a stimulating academic experience but also from the opportunity to explore a dynamic and youthful city in the heart of southern France.

In general, visiting French universities require a high level of French. Often the lectures are conducted in French even if the language of instruction is suppposed to be in English.
details.Important links: Sciences Po Toulouse | Homepage (https://www.sciencespo-toulouse.fr/en) Sciences Politiques Toulouse - International students (https://www.sciencespo-toulouse.fr/en/international-students) English Track courses (https://www.sciencespo-toulouse.fr/en/courses/university-diploma-in-international-comparative-studies) French Track courses (https://www.sciencespo-toulouse.fr/fr/international/diplome-universitaire-detudes-comparatives-internationales) Academic Calendar (https://www.sciencespo-toulouse.fr/en/calendrier-academique)
details.Housing: Only the International Office of Sciences Po Toulouse can provide university accommodation in one of the CROUS halls of residence. A request must be made during the application process. Monthly rent at a hall of residence in Toulouse will cost approximately €300. We are unable to guarantee a room for each student as the number of rooms is limited. Whether you choose student housing or private accommodation, students should start looking for accommodation as soon as possible. More information here. details.Description: ISCTE – Instituto Universitário de Lisboa, founded in 1972, is a dynamic public research university located in Lisbon’s university district, currently serving around 11,000 students across four schools: Business, Social and Human Sciences, Sociology and Public Policy, and Technology and Architecture. It offers a wide array of bachelor’s, master’s, integrated master's, and PhD programs in fields such as economics, management, sociology, political science, engineering, and architecture. ISCTE is internationally accredited by organizations like AACSB, AMBA, and EUR-ACE, and hosts strong research centers such as BRU-IUL and DINÂMIA’CET-IUL. With robust global partnerships and a multicultural learning environment, it is an attractive choice for students interested in social sciences, business, technology, and interdisciplinary research. Living in Lisbon as an ISCTE student combines the energy of a vibrant capital with the charm of student-centered neighborhoods. The ISCTE Students’ Union organizes sports, cultural events, debates, and a range of academic activities that contribute to a lively campus atmosphere. Students also enjoy Lisbon’s bustling cafés, music festivals, rich cultural scene, and easy access to stunning beaches. Altogether, ISCTE offers a rewarding academic experience set in the warm and dynamic environment of Lisbon.

details.Description: Istanbul Bilgi University, established in 1996, is a leading foundation university in Turkey known for its innovative approach to education and strong international outlook. The university offers programs across various fields, including economics, business, law, communication, engineering, architecture, social sciences, and arts. Exchange students can choose from a wide range of English-taught courses, benefiting from an interdisciplinary academic environment that emphasizes critical thinking, creativity, and real-world application. Bilgi’s strong ties with industry, NGOs, and international partners provide students with opportunities for research, internships, and collaborative projects, making it an attractive destination for those seeking a dynamic academic experience in Istanbul. With campuses located in central parts of Istanbul, including the iconic Santral Istanbul Campus, Bilgi offers students a vibrant learning environment within one of the world’s most historically rich and culturally diverse cities. Exchange students can enjoy exploring Istanbul’s unique blend of ancient landmarks, contemporary art scenes, bustling markets, and diverse culinary traditions. The university’s urban campuses are well-connected to the city’s cultural and social life, allowing students to immerse themselves fully in the dynamic rhythm of Istanbul.

details.Description: Istanbul University is the oldest university in Turkey and one of the ten oldest universities in Europe, with a rich academic heritage dating back to 1453 following the conquest of Constantinople by Sultan Mehmet the Conqueror. Today, the university serves more than 250,000 students across 16 faculties, 17 institutes, and numerous research centers. Exchange students can access a wide range of academic disciplines, including humanities, social sciences, law, economics, science, and medicine, benefiting from the university’s strong academic traditions and its role as a leading institution in Turkish higher education. The university’s central location and large academic community offer an enriching environment for learning and cultural exchange. Located in the heart of Istanbul, the Beyazıt Campus is surrounded by the city’s historical and cultural landmarks, providing students with a unique backdrop for their studies. From the Grand Bazaar and Hagia Sophia to the vibrant neighborhoods along the Bosphorus, students have countless opportunities to explore Istanbul’s rich heritage and dynamic urban life. The city’s blend of Eastern and Western influences, combined with its status as Turkey’s economic and cultural hub, makes it an exciting and immersive destination for international students.

details.Restrictions: As a Study Abroad or Exchange student, you cannot study subjects from both semester and trimester models, only one or the other. Postgraduate : You can enrol in both undergraduate (Levels 1–4) and postgraduate (Level 5) subjects, as long as you meet any subject prerequisites.You must however enrol in at least one Level 5 subject You should avoid selecting subjects that run before the start of your chosen study period as this could create visa issues i.e. a block mode subject or summer course. details.Description: Prospective foreign students of Kangwon National University! Kangwon National University is opening its doors wide for foreign students. As one of the 10 core national universities in Korea, we maintain a high level of quality in education and research, while offering a comprehensive range of majors desired by students. Our dormitory capacity is among the highest in Korea, and KNU is located in the beautiful lakeside city of Chuncheon, which is only 1 hour away from the capital city of Seoul, the center of politics, economy, and culture in Korea. This proximity allows you to enjoy a wide variety of cultural activities. Furthermore, our safe and clean living environment and inexpensive living costs will surely help foreign students live comfortably while studying abroad. Kangwon National University is dedicated to becoming a "prestigious glocal university, continuously developing with the region through value and knowledge creation." We deeply appreciate and encourage your lasting support and interest.

details.Description: Karolinska Institutet is one of Sweden’s most prominent medical universities, internationally recognized for its research and academic excellence in health sciences. With approximately 6,000 students and over 2,000 doctoral candidates, it maintains a focused academic environment supported by around 5,000 employees, including leading researchers and clinicians. The university is unique in that it is responsible for selecting Nobel laureates in Physiology or Medicine, a distinction that underscores its global influence in biomedical research. Its close integration with Stockholm’s healthcare system provides students with direct access to clinical environments and research facilities. Located in the Stockholm region, Karolinska Institutet offers students the opportunity to live and study in one of Europe’s most technologically advanced and environmentally conscious capitals. The city combines efficient public transport, widespread English proficiency, and a strong cultural infrastructure, making it accessible and navigable for international students. Stockholm is built on 14 islands connected by over 50 bridges, and its proximity to forests and waterways allows for outdoor activities year-round. A small curiosity: the city’s metro system is often referred to as the world’s longest art gallery, with installations and sculptures integrated into nearly every station.

The opening of the university also reflected the perceived need for higher education as a vehicle with which to reconstruct the war-ravaged nation and a means of perpetuating the time-honored spirit of the Korean people.

details.Description: KIMEP University is the oldest and the largest North American-style University in Central Asia. It was founded in 1992 by the decree of Nursultan Nazarbayev, the First President of the Republic of Kazakhstan. KIMEP is an independent not-for-profit educational institution serving a multicultural and multinational student body. It is situated in a modern campus in the center of Almaty, the largest city in Kazakhstan.

KIMEP University is a leading, innovative institution in Central Asia that promotes educational excellence through teaching and research. When Kazakhstan became independent in 1991, the authorities realized the pressing need for Western-style education as a means to catalyze and sustain economic and social change. As part of this vision, KIMEP was conceived and founded. From its modest beginnings as a small institution, it has grown into a world-renowned university. KIMEP University has established a tradition of excellence by offering programs of the highest academic quality that follow international standards and best practices. The correspondence of our standards to those in Europe and the United States is underlined by the accreditation of many of our programs by international educational quality assurance agencies. The university prides itself on more than simply providing first-class academic programs. KIMEP University distinguishes itself in its devotion to the well-being and personal development of its students. In stark contrast to many universities in Central Asia, KIMEP University involves representatives from its independent student government in decision-making processes and university committees. This complements the university’s broader commitment to transparency, fairness, and integrity, as well as fosters a sense of empowerment and responsibility among students. The alumni which the university produces are not only highly qualified, but deeply committed to these values, and it is this characteristic that makes them such desirable hires. They are recruited by top local and international firms and organizations, and they can be found in diverse professional roles around the world. KIMEP University has played a critical role in the economic modernization of Kazakhstan. Our alumni include many of Kazakhstan’s political and business leaders. KIMEP University serves as an incubator for future generations of Kazakhstani and regional leaders. As an innovative and adaptive institution, KIMEP University will continue to tailor its services to the needs of its students and to those of the Kazakhstani state and society as a whole.

details.Description: King's is one of the UK's most historic and prestigious universities founded in 1829. With a forward thinking vision and state-of-the-art facilities, King's is renowned for excellence in both its innovative teaching and pioneering research. Based in the heart of central London, and spread across five London campuses, King's is one of the largest multi-faculty institutions in the UK with more than 33,000 students.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Students coming for the full academic year will need to provide a valid language test like IELTS, TOEFL, Pearson or other approved international tests listed on the university website. For a student exchange programme for only one semester without requirement of a Student Visa, you do not need to take a language test. Instead you can retrieve a language confirmation from UCPH in Mobility Online which will certify that you have an English language level equivalent to B2 on the European CEFR (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) . A language confirmation will only be needed after you have been nominated to the exchange programme. Levels 4, 5 and 6 are for Undergraduate students and Level 7 is for Postgraduate Taught students (i.e. Masters). Undergraduate students cannot take Level 7 modules, and Postgraduate students cannot take Levels 4, 5 or 6. Important to note: Only modules that are listed in the Study Abroad online module catalogues are open to Study Abroad students. Not all modules at King's College London can be taken by Study Abroad students. Please only select modules found in our catalogues. Postgraduate students should note that some departments/modules are only available to postgraduate students nominated under a specific departmental exchange.

details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . As a result, students applying for exchange places in the UK cannot be guaranteed an Erasmus+ grant at the time of application. details.Description: Leiden University, founded in 1575, is the oldest university in the Netherlands and one of Europe’s leading research institutions. It serves nearly 34,000 students from over 120 nationalities and employs more than 6,400 staff members. The university is spread across two cities—Leiden and The Hague—and is home to 32 research institutes that focus on interdisciplinary collaboration across fields such as law, life sciences, artificial intelligence, and global governance. With a strong emphasis on academic freedom and integrity, Leiden University integrates research and teaching, encouraging students to engage with complex societal challenges in a global context. The city of Leiden offers a rich and student-friendly environment, combining historical charm with modern amenities. Known for its picturesque canals, vibrant cultural scene, and compact layout, Leiden is easy to navigate—most places are just a short bike ride away. The city hosts numerous festivals, museums, and events throughout the year, and is well-connected to other Dutch cities like Amsterdam and The Hague. A fun fact: Leiden is the birthplace of Rembrandt van Rijn and also home to the world’s oldest university observatory, established in 1633—making it a city where art and science have long flourished side by side.

details.Description: Leiden University, founded in 1575, is the oldest university in the Netherlands and one of Europe’s leading research institutions. It serves nearly 34,000 students from over 120 nationalities and employs more than 6,400 staff members. The university is spread across two cities—Leiden and The Hague—and is home to 32 research institutes that focus on interdisciplinary collaboration across fields such as law, life sciences, artificial intelligence, and global governance. With a strong emphasis on academic freedom and integrity, Leiden University integrates research and teaching, encouraging students to engage with complex societal challenges in a global context. The city of Leiden offers a rich and student-friendly environment, combining historical charm with modern amenities. Known for its picturesque canals, vibrant cultural scene, and compact layout, Leiden is easy to navigate—most places are just a short bike ride away. The city hosts numerous festivals, museums, and events throughout the year, and is well-connected to other Dutch cities like Amsterdam and The Hague. A fun fact: Leiden is the birthplace of Rembrandt van Rijn and also home to the world’s oldest university observatory, established in 1633—making it a city where art and science have long flourished side by side.

details.Description: Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU Munich) is one of Europe’s foremost research universities, with a legacy of academic excellence dating back to its founding in 1472. LMU offers a broad spectrum of disciplines, ranging from the humanities and social sciences to medicine and natural sciences, and is consistently ranked among the top universities in Germany and internationally. Its programs are deeply rooted in cutting-edge research, and students benefit from close interaction with leading scholars and access to world-class facilities. With a strong international profile and a student body of over 50,000, LMU provides a stimulating academic environment that encourages intellectual curiosity and interdisciplinary collaboration. Located in the heart of Munich, LMU offers students the opportunity to study in one of Germany’s most attractive and culturally rich cities. Munich is known for its high quality of life, vibrant arts scene, and proximity to the Alps, making it an ideal setting for both academic and personal growth. The city combines historic charm with modern innovation, and students can enjoy everything from museums and music festivals to outdoor activities and international cuisine. An exchange semester at LMU Munich promises not only academic enrichment but also a rewarding experience in one of Europe’s most welcoming and dynamic urban environments.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: By the time you start studying at LMU , you must have the language level B2 according to the Common European Framework of Reference (at least B1 for your application). Some departments have higher requirements. German : Good German language skills are important in order to study at LMU. Even though some departments offer modules in English, most courses at a bachelor's level are offered in German. On commencing your studies at LMU you should have acquired level B2 language skills. English: The same requirement applies if you plan to take courses in English. A list of departments that offer English language courses can be found under choosing courses (https://www.lmu.de/en/study/all-degrees-and-programs/programs-for-international-visiting-students/erasmus-and-lmuexchange/choosing-courses/) . The faculty / department will review your application on an individual basis. Please note, that you do not have to prove your German skills if you only take classes in English.
details.Restrictions: BA and MA students can apply for this agreement. The Institute for European Ethnology and Cultural Analysis at LMU Munich offers the complete range of academic subjects in European Ethnology, extending from the analysis of cultural phenomena on our doorstep to the investigation of cultural phenomena in other European societies, and including the processes of Europeanization, transnationalization, and migration, as well as cultural comparison. Incoming Erasmus students can also choose English courses from other institutes (for example, from Sociology, Cultural Anthropology, English Studies). Additional restrictions: Erasmus students must choose at least 60% of their course modules in the field of study defined in the bilateral agreement. Students should take the other 40% of their course modules in no more than two other fields of study. The Faculties of Business Administration, Medicine, Dentistry, Veterinary Medicine, Pharmacy do not accept students outside of their own inter-Institutional agreements. Likewise, places cannot be guaranteed in Sociology and English taught Politics courses.Therefore, all exchange students can choose courses in a maximum of three study areas. If you have no previous knowledge in a given subject area, you can only attend introductory courses in that subject area. If you are studying in a bachelor's program, you are generally not allowed to take master's courses (LMU will discuss exceptions to this rule internally)

details.Description: Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU Munich) is one of Europe’s foremost research universities, with a legacy of academic excellence dating back to its founding in 1472. LMU offers a broad spectrum of disciplines, ranging from the humanities and social sciences to medicine and natural sciences, and is consistently ranked among the top universities in Germany and internationally. Its programs are deeply rooted in cutting-edge research, and students benefit from close interaction with leading scholars and access to world-class facilities. With a strong international profile and a student body of over 50,000, LMU provides a stimulating academic environment that encourages intellectual curiosity and interdisciplinary collaboration. Located in the heart of Munich, LMU offers students the opportunity to study in one of Germany’s most attractive and culturally rich cities. Munich is known for its high quality of life, vibrant arts scene, and proximity to the Alps, making it an ideal setting for both academic and personal growth. The city combines historic charm with modern innovation, and students can enjoy everything from museums and music festivals to outdoor activities and international cuisine. An exchange semester at LMU Munich promises not only academic enrichment but also a rewarding experience in one of Europe’s most welcoming and dynamic urban environments.

Some departments have higher requirements. German : Good German language skills are important in order to study at LMU. Even though some departments offer modules in English, most courses at a bachelor's level are offered in German. On commencing your studies at LMU you should have acquired level B2 language skills. English: The same requirement applies if you plan to take courses in English. A list of departments that offer English language courses can be found under choosing courses (https://www.lmu.de/en/study/all-degrees-and-programs/programs-for-international-visiting-students/erasmus-and-lmuexchange/choosing-courses/) . The faculty / department will review your application on an individual basis. Please note, that you do not have to prove your German skills if you only take classes in English.
details.Restrictions: Erasmus students must choose at least 60% of their course modules in the field of study defined in the bilateral agreement. Students should take the other 40% of their course modules in no more than two other fields of study. The Faculties of Business Administration, Medicine, Dentistry, Veterinary Medicine, Pharmacy do not accept students outside of their own inter-Institutional agreements. Likewise, places cannot be guaranteed in Sociology and English taught Politics courses. Therefore, all exchange students can choose courses in a maximum of three study areas. If you have no previous knowledge in a given subject area, you can only attend introductory courses in that subject area. If you are studying in a bachelor's program, you are generally not allowed to take master's courses (LMU will discuss exceptions to this rule internally)

details.Description: Luiss University, officially Libera Università Internazionale degli Studi Sociali Guido Carli, is a renowned private university in Rome specializing in the social sciences. Established in 1974, Luiss offers academic programs across four main departments: Economics and Finance, Business and Management, Law, and Political Science. The university emphasizes a practical and interdisciplinary approach to learning, closely connected with Italy’s business community and public institutions. Exchange students have access to a broad selection of English-taught courses, with opportunities to engage in case studies, project work, and interactive seminars designed to mirror real-world challenges. A favorable student-to-faculty ratio ensures personalized learning and active academic engagement. Located in Rome’s elegant Parioli and Trieste neighborhoods, Luiss University provides a campus environment within one of Europe’s most historic and dynamic cities. Students can easily explore Rome’s rich cultural life, with museums, galleries, markets, and iconic landmarks just a short distance from campus. The university fosters a vibrant student community through various academic and cultural events, allowing exchange students to immerse themselves in both Italian university life and the unique urban energy of Rome.

details.Description: Luleå University of Technology, located in the Arctic Region, has four campuses and over a hundred education programs. The university serves around 18,000 students. It offers programmes and courses in Swedish as the primary language of instruction, but it also has a growing number of courses in English. The city of Luleå sits in Sweden’s far north and provides a distinctive Nordic student experience. The main campus lies within reach of the central city, and everyday necessities are accessible by local transit and cycling when the weather allows. Beyond the urban amenities you’ll find dramatic natural surroundings: forests, coastlines and snow in winter. For an exchange student willing to embrace the climate, Luleå offers both solid academic life and a memorable location.

details.Description: Lund University is one of Scandinavia’s oldest and largest institutions, with a student population of over 45,000. It is internationally recognized for its research output and participation in major EU projects places it among the leading research universities in northern Europe. Its historical foundation in 1666 and continued emphasis on academic freedom distinguish it from other institutions. The university offers courses taught in both English and Swedish across a wide range of disciplines, making it highly accessible to students from all over the world. details.Description: Maastricht University was founded in 1976, making it the second youngest of the thirteen Dutch universities. Maastricht University, the European university of the Netherlands, has nearly 22,000 students and 5,000 staff. We are young, interdisciplinary and socially engaged, which is evident in everything we do. Despite our relatively recent establishment, we have already built a strong reputation through our excellent research and education, and by connecting science with regional, European and global challenges. We rank among the best young universities in the world.

details.Restrictions: Course switches are not possible after the course registration deadline(s). Reason for this is that Maastricht University uses the Problem-Based Learning system. A lot of planning goes into finding enough rooms and teachers/tutors, and to make sure each tutorial group is about the same size (average group size is 15 students).
details.Course information: In the SBE online exchange course database (https://code.unimaas.nl/Code/Selection?intCalendarID=32&intBAMA=3&intFacultyID=26) , you can find all information you need about SBE’s bachelor’s and master’s courses, such as the course coordinator(s), learning outcomes and competences, the number of ECTS credits, literature, and any prerequisites. At Maastricht they offer Problem-Based Learning (PBL) with a different, more interactive way of learning compared to traditional university education. You will not have to spend hours listening to lectures, although there are some, usually at the start of the study period. Instead, per course you will attend a two-hour tutorial group meeting, twice a week. These meetings form the core part of the study programme and are the driving force for learning. Within the tutorial groups (with 8 to 15 students), problems are presented and researched as cases.

details.Additional information: Maastricht, the oldest city in the Netherlands, gained international fame as the 'birthplace of the European Union' by hosting of the European Summit in 1991, and as the city where the Treaty of Maastricht was signed in 1992. Maastricht University is highly regarded in Europe for its unique teaching style and high-quality research. In fact, it’s School of Business and Economics (SBE) has been awarded three prestigious accreditations, resulting in the so-called Triple Crown accreditation. A buddy programme is available for all incoming exchange students.

details.Description: Macquarie University is recognised globally for its pre-eminence in key research disciplines, as well as producing graduates who are among the most sought-after professionals in the world. Since our foundation in 1964, we have aspired to be a different type of university: one unbound by ivory towers and sandstone walls. Rather, we are focused on fostering collaboration between students, academics, industry and society, encouraging all to traverse the boundaries of their own perspectives and effect change. The campus is located in the heart of Australia’s largest high-tech precinct, only 18 minutes from downtown Sydney. Like a miniature city, Macquarie has a vast array of amenities on campus including a bookshop, a bar and several cafés. Take a tour of Macquarie University (https://youtu.be/UnwtlW_x9v0?si=ma8xDs7oR-Ni96hv)

details.Description: Malmö University is a relatively young institution, established in 1998, with a student population of around 24,000 and approximately 1,800 staff. It is known for its focus on urban studies, sustainability, and social innovation, and maintains strong connections with the surrounding community and regional industries. The university emphasizes interdisciplinary collaboration and internationalization, with a high proportion of students and faculty from outside Sweden. Its central location within Malmö allows for close integration with the city’s public services, cultural institutions, and business networks. The university is located in Malmö, Sweden’s third-largest city, situated at the southern tip of the country and directly connected to Copenhagen via the Öresund Bridge. Malmö is compact, bike-friendly, and known for its diversity, with over 170 nationalities represented in the population. The city offers a mix of modern architecture, coastal parks, and historical sites, all within walking distance of the university. A small curiosity: Malmö’s Turning Torso is the tallest building in Scandinavia and was the first twisted skyscraper in the world.

details.Language requirements: McGill's Law program is offered in a bilingual, English & French, environment. The majority of courses at McGill are offered in English, thus the ability to communicate in English is a requirement. At the Faculty of Law, reading of complex substantive texts in French and English are assigned in many upper-year law courses, irrespective of the language of instruction of the course. In certain courses in particular, such as private law courses, students will be assigned readings in French. While examination questions are set in the language in which a course is given, any examination may contain extensive passages in either French or English. details.Description: Meiji University was founded in January 1881 as the Meiji Law School by a group of young lawyers barely in their 30's: Tatsuo Kishimoto, Kozo Miyagi, and Misao Yashiro. The three founded the Meiji Law School in their fervent hope to "foster bright capable youths who would lead a modern civil society in Japan". Meiji University ranks solidly among the best universities in Japan, currently consisting of 10 undergraduate schools, 12 graduate schools and four professional graduate schools.

details.Description: The university was founded in 1958 and has now grown into an ecosystem of campuses, educations centers and partnerships spanning the globe. details.Description: Mykolas Romeris University (MRU) was founded in 1990 as a non-profit public university located in the urban setting of the large city of Vilnius. The University’s is highly recognized for its’ outstanding Law School and it is no. 1 in the area of Law among all Lithuania’s universities according to “QS World University Rankings by Subject 2020”.  In the students’ opinion, the University MRU is also placed no. 1 among all Lithuania’s universities (“Reitingai” magazine, 2020).
details.Academic calendar: Autumn semester: Late August to the end of December - with exams in January. Spring semester: Late January to the end of May - with exams in June. An introductory week is held each semester – see additional information on introductory week (https://www.mruni.eu/en/university/internationalization/erasmus-and-exchange-studies-incoming/) if you scroll down.

details.Study load: As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad.
details.Restrictions: Students may take courses from both – bachelor and master cycles. Just keep in mind that master cycle courses may have prerequisites outlined in the course descriptions. If you do not meet these prerequisites, it may be too difficult to study the courses.

details.Description:
Established in 1996, NUPACE, the Nagoya University Program for Academic
Exchange, constitutes both a frontrunner and intrinsic element of our continued endeavor to
internationalize. NUPACE will afford you the opportunity to simultaneously enjoy a quality academic
curriculum, discover Japan and, most importantly, to acquire a fundamentally international
approach to life.
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Academic calendar: Autumn Semester : October – February Spring Semester : April – August Transcript issuance : A digital copy will be sent to the student approximately six weeks after the completion of the exchange.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: English proficiency test: Non-native English speakers wishing to participate in the English-language curriculum should possess one of the following scores: TOEFL iBT 79, IELTS 6.0, TOEIC 780, CEFR B2, or CET-6 485. Students from Scandinavia, Germany, Austria, The Netherlands, Hong Kong and Singapore are exempt from this requirement, as are students who have an English language education background. Japanese Language Proficiency Test (JLPT): Students intending to take regular university courses instructed in Japanese must possess level N1/level 1 of the Japanese Language Proficiency Test (JLPT), or the equivalent.
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 14 credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Study load for graduate students: 8 credits = 30 ECTS Please note that not all UCPH Master’s (graduate) programmes allow credit transfer of bachelor (undergraduate) courses into their programmes. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: NUPACE Special Undergraduate and Special Graduate Students majoring in Chemistry or Physics are generally not permitted to enrol in G30 courses with laboratory content.
details.Course information: With over 800 courses taught in English, (and many more in Japanese), students participating in NUPACE have a variety of study options open to them. Provided that they meet the academic and linguistic requirements of the classes in question, students may devise semester/year-based course loads from, 1) the wide-ranging spectrum of English-taught courses, offered both by the individual Schools and Institute of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ILAS), 2) Japanese language courses, and 3) regular courses taught in Japanese. Lists/syllabi of courses English-taught courses: https://nupace.iee.nagoya-u.ac.jp/en/academic/overview.html (https://nupace.iee.nagoya-u.ac.jp/en/academic/overview.html) Regular Japanese-taught courses for students with JLPT N1: https://syllabus.adm.nagoya-u.ac.jp/ (https://syllabus.adm.nagoya-u.ac.jp/)
details.Important links: Inbound exchange programme website (NUPACE): https://nupace.iee.nagoya-u.ac.jp/en/ (https://nupace.iee.nagoya-u.ac.jp/en/) NUPACE > Application Information: https://nupace.iee.nagoya-u.ac.jp/en/apply/index.html (https://nupace.iee.nagoya-u.ac.jp/en/apply/index.html) NUPACE > Application Procedures: https://nupace.iee.nagoya-u.ac.jp/en/apply/procedures.html (https://nupace.iee.nagoya-u.ac.jp/en/apply/procedures.html)
details.Housing: Type of accommodation offered : In principle, single rooms in student dormitories located within a short commute to the university, either on foot or by subway. University housing fees: 25,000-45,000 JPY per month, including utilities. Application method: No procedures necessary; NUPACE will apply for housing on the student’s behalf.
details.Scholarships:
Students applying for this university are automatically considered for KU’s Internationalisation
scholarship.
details.Additional information:
Nagoya University has opened six undergraduate and seven graduate degree programmes
taught entirely in English, known as the “Nagoya University Global 30 International
Programmes”, or simply “G30 Programmes”. Courses comprising the G30 programmes are, in
principle, open to exchange students, and a large number of NUPACE students are taking
advantage of the opportunity to register for them. Website for G30 programmes (http://admissions.g30.nagoya-u.ac.jp/en/Program/)

details.Description: Nanzan University offers 8 Faculties and 18 Departments, 6 Graduate Schools and 14 Programs, as well as Center for Japanese Studies. Small-size Classes enable students to be active in class and easy to get attention and valuable advice from professors. The Center for Japanese Studies is renowned as a leader in the field of Japanese language education for more than 45 years. Nanzan University has approximately 10,000 students, including over 300 international students. We continue to explore internationalization that is congruent with our educational motto “For Human Dignity. International students of undergraduate and graduate programs are eligible for 50 % tuition fee exemption. A variety of scholarships are also available for students, which will lessen the burden the school life expenses. Nagoya City in Aichi Prefecture is in the center of Japan, a convenient location from which to visit many other places. It has often played an important role in Japan’s history and some remarkable traditions and customs are still alive today. At the same time, there are many spots in Aichi where you can experience modern Japanese culture, making it possible to witness two cultures from different time eras. The region is also the hub of Japanese manufacturing industries.
details.Academic calendar: Fall: September - December Spring: January - May For more information about the academic calender, see here: https://www.nanzan-u.ac.jp/English/academics/cjs/calendar.html (https://www.nanzan-u.ac.jp/English/academics/cjs/calendar.html)
details.Minimum GPA for admission: GPA For students going on mandatory stay For students going on a mandatory stay there are no GPA requirements. GPA for all other students All other students must have a cumulative grade point average of 7.0 on the Danish grading scale. If you are appointed a spot for this agreement with a GPA higher than 7.0 but your GPA gets scaled down to a lower GPA than 7.0 in the period until the host universitys application deadline, your application may be rejected by the host university and your exchange stay will not be possible.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: In accordance to Nanzan University's webpage you need to have a level of Japanese or English ability sufficient to undergo education at Nanzan University. You can download an official English language proficiency statement with reference to CEFR B2 in Mobility Online if you get a spot for this agreement.
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 14 credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2027-2028 and onwards. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Study load for graduate students: 8 credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2027-2028 and onwards. - Conversion and levels: Study load is calculated according to the level of the specific course. Please note that not all UCPH Master’s (graduate) programmes allow credit transfer of bachelor (undergraduate) courses into their programmes. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: The spots for this agreement are preferentially allocated to students who are going on a mandatory study abroad stay. Any remaining spots will be allocated to applicants who are planning an ordinary exchange. Therefore, you cannot rely on the calculation of available spots as stated in the fact sheet.
details.Important links: https://www.nanzan-u.ac.jp/English/academics/cjs/ (https://www.nanzan-u.ac.jp/English/academics/cjs/)
details.Housing: The CJS students will be given the following three housing options. Dormitory (Your specific dormitory preference will not be accepted.) Homestay* Self-arranged For more information on accommodations, please see below. Accommodation (https://www.nanzan-u.ac.jp/English/studentlife/accommodation/) Note: Students should make an accommodation choice carefully. Once an application is submitted, students cannot make a change request on accommodation and move into another housing after enrollment. In other words, the students who apply for two semesters from fall to spring will stay in the same accommodation for the entire period. Students who selected a dorm on application will be placed with one of the following dorms based upon application information. Janssen International Residence Foyer Nanzan Rainbow House Kikusumi Ryo Students will be noticed of the results of their housing assignment around two months before the program starts. *Nanzan commissions the arrangement of homestay to an arrangement company. Matching information will be finalized and notified to students after notification of housing assignment results.

details.Description: The Faculty of Law offers courses of general legal education and specialization courses at an undergraduate and postgraduate level. The educational process on an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary level is not confined within the University of Athens, but is realized in cooperation with famous higher education institutions in Greece and abroad. Graduates of The Faculty of Law excel in all fields of science and research; engage in significant professional activity in both Greece and the international scientific world; contribute to the political life and have played a significant role in the construction of the modern Greek state.

details.Description: National Chengchi University (NCCU) was founded in 1927, and for more than 9 decades of re-formation and development, we have been upholding our motto, “Harmony, Independence, Balance and Preeminence”, We continue to refine our teaching methods and research in order to nurture talents for our country and the world. We currently have 12 colleges excelling in the Liberal Arts, Law, Commerce, Science, Foreign Languages, Social Sciences, Communication, International Affairs, Education, Innovation, Informatics, Global Banking and Finance. We have 34 departments, one undeclared major in the College of Communication, 43 master's programs and 34 doctoral programs. Additionally, NCCU offers 12 on-the-job Master’s Programs, and also 7 distinguished International Master's Programs and International Doctoral Program. NCCU also has 10 university-level research centers：the Institute of International Relations, Election Study Center, Center for the Third Sector, Center for Creativity and Innovation Studies, Taiwan Studies Center, Center for China Studies, Humanities Research Center, Center for Aboriginal Studies, Center for Mind, Brain and Learning and Center for the Study of Chinese Religions. In addition, NCCU forms an educational system from pre-school level to the Doctoral program with its affiliated institutions, including a high school, an experimental elementary school and a kindergarten.

details.Description:
Characterized by both tradition and innovation, National Taiwan Normal University (NTNU) has
long been recognized as one of Taiwan’s elite institutions of higher education. Founded in 1922,
NTNU was formerly an institution dedicated to teacher education. The university later evolved
into a comprehensive university that provides students and scholars with opportunities to study
and conduct research in a wide range of fields. Throughout its long history, NTNU has always
been committed to academic excellence and this is reflected in the many influential educators
and researchers that have studied at NTNU over the years.

details.Description: The National University of Singapore Faculty of Law is widely regarded as Asia’s leading law school. Staffed by an outstanding permanent faculty diverse in origin and qualifications, NUS Law is dedicated to building a vibrant community and creating an environment that facilitates critical thinking and reflection on the fundamental legal issues confronting our interconnected world. Located in Singapore, which for more than a century has been a commercial hub at the crossroads of Asia, NUS Law is very much Asia’s Global Law School. Since 1957 our curriculum has been infused with perspectives from other jurisdictions and disciplines. This tradition has accelerated in recent years, providing a legal education that is comparative, international, and multi-disciplinary. The Law School hosts many visiting faculty and students from every continent, offering a lively, cosmopolitan atmosphere both inside and outside the classroom. The aim is to provide a liberal education that enables our graduates to think critically and creatively, as globally-oriented lawyers with a strong sense of their role in society.
details.Agreement name: National University of Singapore (NUS) - Faculty of Law
details.Academic calendar: Semester 1: Early/mid-August – Dec. (incl. exams) A orientation programme is held before the start of sem. 1. Semester 2: Early/mid-Jan. – mid-May (incl. exams) Special Term: May – August. See additional information in the academic calendar (https://www.nus.edu.sg/education#academic-calendar)
details.GPA for undergraduate admission: N/A [Not open for student exchange during bachelor law programme at UCPH].
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: As part of the exchange agreement between the National University of Singapore and the University of Copenhagen, Danish law students are exempt from language test requirements as exchange students. A language confirmation is, however, required to confirm that you have sufficient language qualifications. The confirmation will be based on your grades in English from your ‘studentereksamen’ or HF diploma. A language confirmation will only be needed after you have been nominated to the exchange programme, where you can retrieve it in Mobility Online.
details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad.
details.Course information: Study level: Our LLB degree is a 4-year honours programme where upper year students (year 3 and 4) will read electives. Incoming exchange students can choose the same electives that our upper year students read. These electives are also opened to our Masters students though masters students will be marked on different marking scheme. In general, the exchange programme at NUS is catered for undergraduate students. Most courses (level 1xxx to level 4xxx) that are open to incoming exchange students are at the undergraduate level in NUS context. Graduate level courses are categorized level 5XXX to 6XXX. Teaching style: At NUS you may anticipate class attendance, active class participation, mid-terms and other assignments which will all form part of your final assessment alongside the actual exam; thorough preparations will be required and it may seem quite different from UCPH that assessment procedures are ongoing throughout the whole semester.
details.Important links: See course descriptions (https://nusmods.com/courses?sem[0]=3&sem[1]=1&level[0]=1000&level[1]=2000&level[2]=3000&level[3]=4000&fac[0]=Law) - change the sorting for sem. 2 See info course selection tips (https://nus.edu.sg/registrar/docs/info/prospective-students---non-graduating/ng-courses.pdf) See info for incoming exchange students (https://www.nus.edu.sg/gro/global-programmes/student-exchange/incoming-exchangers) See info on clubs and interest groups (https://law.nus.edu.sg/student-life-support/student-activities/clubs-interest-groups/) The Faculty of Law (https://law.nus.edu.sg/) The National University of Singapore (https://nus.edu.sg/)
details.Housing: All non-graduating students are eligible to apply for on-campus housing, although not guaranteed placement given the limited supply of accommodation at NUS. Primary consideration will be given to exchange students reading undergraduate courses in NUS. A application process will take place after you have accepted by NUS as an exchange student. See additional info on accommodation (https://osa.nus.edu.sg/accommodation/hostel-options/) .
details.Scholarships: Students applying for this university are automatically considered for KU’s Internationalisation scholarship.
details.Additional information: Additional costs: Although tuition fee is waived for exchange students, you are still responsible for paying: Student Service fee S$ 66.44 Health Service fee S$ 132.50 Subject to later changes, see the fee info (https://nus.edu.sg/registrar/administrative-policies-procedures/non-graduating/non-graduating-fees) . Insurance: In addition to a possible mandatory insurance at your host university, UCHP recommends that Danish students on an exchange programme take out an insurance coverage with a Danish insurance company to make sure that you are sufficiently covered especially when talking about possible need for home transportation to DK or possible coverage during your activities and trips outside the campus area of your host university. Info on visa produres: After your registration at NUS - they will inform you about visa procedures.

details.Description:
NUS started out as a modest medical school in 1905, founded by a determined group of
businessmen led by Tan Jiak Kim, to serve the needs of the local community. Today, we are
Singapore’s flagship university consistently ranked among the top two universities in Asia and
top 25 in the world. NUS consists of 3 Campuses: Kent Ridge, Bukit Timah and Outram. 12 Undergraduate Schools, 4 Graduate Schools, 26 University‐level Research Institutes and
Centres. 52 Bachelor's degrees, 28 Double majors, 27 Concurrent degrees, 35 Joint degrees, 71 Double degrees.144 Master's degrees, Doctoral degrees, Graduate diplomas 28000 Undergraduates, 10000 Graduate students, 2400 Faculty and 3200 Research Staff.
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Academic calendar: NUS semester 1 (Fall): August - December NUS semester 2 (Spring): January - May
details.GPA for undergraduate admission: 7 (Danish grading scale) with no grades below 4. Students with grades below 7 may find it difficult to secure modules.
details.GPA for graduate admission: N/A - the agreement is only open to BA students
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: As English is the main language of instruction at the University (except for Asian/European studies where a good command of the respective Asian/European language is a pre-requisite), you must be proficient in the English language in order to benefit from your studies at NUS. If you are applying to read modules from NUS Faculty of Law as part of your university-wide exchange, you are required to submit either the TOEFL (iBT 100) or IELTS (6.5) results.
details.Restrictions: The exchange programme at NUS is for undergraduate students and only open for students enrolled in a bachelor's degree programme at UCPH. Students must have completed at least 2 semesters (one full year) at the time of application to NUS (usually April for exchange in Fall semesters and September for exchange in Spring semesters). Modules that are open to incoming exchange students are at the undergraduate level in NUS context (level 1000 to 4000). Undergraduate exchange students should consider level 1000 to 3000 modules. Level 4000 modules are mostly reserved for NUS graduating students. Modules of level 5000 and above are graduate modules and are not available to exchange students. Make sure you have read through information about the available and restricted courses at NUS (https://www.nus.edu.sg/registrar/prospective-students/non-graduating/coursework) . Computer Science courses are very popular and access to these is extremely limited. Please plan for courses other than Computer Science. Modules from the Colleges/Faculties/Schools/Institutes/Departments below are NOT open to any non-Graduating applicants/exchange students: • Faculty of Dentistry • Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine (module codes that do not start with LSM only) • Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health (Graduate modules only) • Alice Lee Centre for Nursing Studies • Institute of Systems Science • All modules in NUS self-funded programmes
