details.Description: Founded in 1831, New York University is one of the largest private universities in the United States. The University, which includes 18 schools, colleges and institutes, occupies five major centers in New York City. There are more than 50,000 students enrolled in all of the schools. The center of NYU is the Washington Square campus in the heart of Greenwich Village. One of the city's most creative and energetic communities, the Village is a historic neighborhood that has attracted generations of writers, musicians, artists, and intellectuals. Beyond the Village, New York City becomes an extension of the University's campus. In addition to its Manhattan locations, the University is also located in Brooklyn with the second oldest school of engineering and technology in the country, and has numerous research facilities.
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: August- December Spring Semester: January-May Please note that the spring semester begins very early compared to the spring semester at UCPH. You should only apply for the spring semester, if you do not have exams in January at UCPH.
details.GPA for graduate admission: Above 9 (Danish scale) - please note that when applying for graduate level in the US you have to fulfill the grade requirement from the department at your host university. Each department has their own grade requirement for graduate level students - and it is often very high - at least above 9  but more often between 10 and 12.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Duo-Lingo: 135 and above ( only for applicants for undergraduate (BA) level ) or TOEFL-test: 100 (with no less than 22 on any section) if taken before January 21, 2026 or 5 or above (overall score and subscores) if taken on or after Jan. 21, 2026 IELTS-test: 7.5 (with no less than 6.0 on any section) The following undergraduate students are exempted from submitting an English Language Proficiency test: ● The student is enrolled in a degree program where the official language of instruction is 100% in English. ● A national from a majority native English speaking country (Americas, United Kingdom, Australia, Ireland etc…). Passport is required. ● Home University is based in a majority native English speaking country (Americas, United Kingdom, Australia, Ireland etc…). Passport is required. Each NYU Graduate school and Faculty has different English proficiency exemption requirements.
details.Restrictions: NYU does not accept Economics students at graduate level Available NYU Schools & Faculties Open to Exchange Students through the NYU International Exchange Program: — Undergraduate Students Undergraduate exchange students are not assigned to specific schools or faculties. Undergraduate exchange students have access to all undergraduate courses offered at NYU, provided that they meet the course’s requirements and space is available. Please refer to the Course Registration, Availability and Restrictions section for more details. Graduate Students* Graduate exchange students may apply to the faculties below, and their application must be accepted by the department to which they are applying. In reviewing the application, departments will be evaluating students based on academic achievement, as well as the applicant’s academic fit with the department in terms of past coursework taken and research interests. ● Graduate School of Arts and Science (GSAS) (select departments) ● Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development (select departments) ● Silver School of Social Work (all departments) ● Tisch School of the Arts (Department of Cinema Studies and Performance Studies, Fall semester only) It is very hard to get accepted to NYU as a graduate student. Most departments require a GPA of 12 (Danish scale) as well as extracurricular activities in order to accept an exchange student at graduate level.

Residence halls offered to exchange students vary from apartment-style with shared kitchen areas to traditional hall style, although most will be placed in apartment-style housing. Please note that housing is not guaranteed, and NYU is better able to accommodate exchange student housing requests in the Spring semester. For more information about on campus housing options, please visit NYU’s On Campus Living website. (nyu.edu/life/living-at-nyu/on-campus-living.html)

Be aware that credit requirements may be different for other exchange students at New York University. Exchange students are not eligible to participate in clinics or clinic seminars.
details.Course information: See link to course descriptions on https://its.law.nyu.edu/courses (https://its.law.nyu.edu/courses) See info on the study levels at NYU (https://www.law.nyu.edu/students/roadmap/overview) Course Enrollment and Registration Exchange students will have the same opportunities as our LL.M. students when registering for classes; demand for courses may exceed their availability so they cannot be guaranteed. Instructions for registering will be sent along with the letter of admission. In the fall semester, students participating in the exchange program are strongly encouraged to enroll in “Introduction to U.S. Law” (worth 2 credits). The course is held during the week prior to the start of the fall semester. In the spring semester (January to May), students participating in the exchange program are also strongly encouraged to enroll in a section of Graduate Lawyering. In the past, this course has been offered on an intensive basis during the week before spring semester courses begin.

details.Additional information: General Information New York University School of Law is the preeminent global law school featuring innovative teaching, research, and intellectual and professional development in a uniquely collegial environment. The essence of the Law School experience is the close interaction between our faculty and students. Creating and nurturing a stimulating intellectual environment is central to the educational philosophy of the Law School, and these characteristics hold high appeal for both students and faculty. NYU School of Law offers more than 200 rich and diverse courses and programs on issues that permeate all aspects of law in the 21st century. This extensive curriculum broadens perspectives and opens new ways of seeing and understanding, not only the law, but the world around us. NYU Law creates a vibrant community through our rigorous academic programs, including business, constitutional, criminal, environmental, innovation, interdisciplinary, international, procedure, public interest and tax law, as well as innovative programs, such as our renowned clinics and our groundbreaking lawyering program. For more information click here (https://www.law.nyu.edu/areasofstudy) . Located in Greenwich Village, New York City, NYU School of Law is a vibrant part of this metropolis.

details.Description: Newcastle University was founded in 1834 to educate the pioneers of the industrial revolution. Teaching was then, and is still, at the heart of the University: at Newcastle they educate for life, to develop and nurture successive generations of creative practitioners, clinicians, scientists, engineering and educationalists, and set them on the path to make their own mark on society.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: Mid-September to late January. Spring semester: Early January to mid-June See additional information in the academic calendar (https://www.ncl.ac.uk/regulations/docs/term-dates/#currentandfutureyears) Terms show the teaching period, whereas semesters also include the assessment/exam period.
details.Minimum GPA for admission: The host university has no minimum GPA requirement.
details.Language requirements: A good knowledge of English is essential for studying at Newcastle University as an exchange student. A language test is not necessary but a language confirmation is required confirming that you have sufficient language qualifications corresponding to min. level B2 in the self-assessment CEFR-grid (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) . After the application process at UCPH, you can apply for a language confirmation from the Faculty of Law in Copenhagen. The language confirmation will be based on your grades in English from your Danish ‘studentereksamen’ or ‘HF’ diploma. An official language text is only required as part of the visa procedures, if your stay exceeds 6 months.
details.Study load: 30 ECTS = 60 credits As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS/60 credits per semester while you are abroad.
details.Course information: Law courses/module at undergraduate level: All modules (courses) are listed on the module catalogue (find active link below at 'Important links') , within which students can search by School, but student should be aware that anything listed as ‘Inactive’ are not offered, and there are some modules which are not available to incoming exchange students.  For example, LAW2100 is specific to our outgoing exchange students and LAW1000 is not credit-bearing. Master level courses: Exchange students may be able to select LL.M. level modules (find active link below at 'Important links') while studying at Newcastle Law School with permission of the LL.M. Degree Programme Director and the relevant module coordinator. Whole year modules with alternative assessment in Dec/Jan. Many modules are year-long, but the majority of these offer an assessment in semester 1.  For any students who are sitting a module assessed by a January examination who do not expect to return to Newcastle after Christmas, we do try to support alternative methods of assessment. This should be raised with the Exchange Coordinator when the students choose their modules so an alternative form of assessment can be looked into. Student exchange to Newcastle is only open in the autumn semesters due to very limited course/module offers in spring semesters.
details.Important links: See course/module catalogue (https://www.ncl.ac.uk/mobility/experience-newcastle/module-catalogue/) below Humanities and Social Sciences - select 'Law'. See information on Master level degrees (https://www.ncl.ac.uk/law/study/masters/) Homepage of Newcastle Law School (https://www.ncl.ac.uk/nuls/) See information for International and EU students (https://www.ncl.ac.uk/international/) See info on Newcastle University Sport (https://www.ncl.ac.uk/sport/) See info on Meet and Greet Service (https://www.ncl.ac.uk/student-welcome/whenyouarrive/internationalwelcome/#airportmeetandgreetservice)
details.Housing: Housing is difficult to find for students coming for one semester. In Newcastle, we are happy to announce that we have secured an additional city-centre student accommodation site and hope to be able to offer rooms to part-year students this year. See additional info on https://www.ncl.ac.uk/accommodation/ (https://www.ncl.ac.uk/accommodation/)
details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . As a result, students applying for exchange places in the UK cannot be guaranteed an Erasmus+ grant at the time of application. Eligibility for Erasmus+ funding will depend on whether the host university joins the programme and concludes an Erasmus+ agreement with the University of Copenhagen. Students nominated to a UK university will be informed of their grant eligibility no later than March 2027.
details.Additional information: When The Faculty of Law in Copenhagen has nominated you for an exchange place at Newcastle University, you have to apply for admission within the application deadlines which may vary a bit from year to year. After the application procedures you will receive information from Newcastle University about visa procedures. There may be differences in the requirements for a stay of 6 months' duration compared to a stay beyond that period. Warning - if you go on student exchange in the last semester of your master degree, a transcript delay may postpone the completion of your master degree! Generally, at British universities official transcripts are delayed with approx. 3-4 months into the next semester due to an audit for a Board of Examiners. In urgent cases, UCPH try to obtain confirmation on the validity of a provisional transcript – but we cannot give you any guarantee in advance.

details.Description: The Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (NCU) was founded in 1945. It is one of the largest universities in Poland, currently comprising 16 faculties. It provides graduate and postgraduate courses for almost 21,500 students, employing more than 400 staff and offering education in over 100 fields of study and 55 postgraduate courses. NCU has state-of-the-art research infrastructure including the National Laboratory of Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics (FAMO), the Center for Quantum Optics and the Interdisciplinary Center for Modern Technologies to name but a few, as well as modern teaching facilities comprising, among others, Collegium Humanisticum and the brand-new University Sports Centre. The Centre for Astronomy in Piwnice near Toruń houses a unique 32-meter radio telescope. Spitsbergen (in the Arctic Sea) is home to NCU Polar Station.
details.Academic calendar: Winter semester: October – February Spring semester: February – June Academic calendar (https://www.umk.pl/en/erasmus/students/)

details.Restrictions: The language of instruction at NCU is mainly Polish; Erasmus+ students may find a number of modules in foreign languages at particular faculties (mainly in English, German, French). If you wish to find out more about special courses in foreign languages, please contact your Faculty Coordinator at NCU. BSc students are allowed to follow MSc courses if they fulfill the course prerequisites (some courses require a bachelor’s degree). Exchange students are allowed to choose the courses from the different faculties/departments without any restrictions. However, it is important that you get the approval of your major coordinator (e.g., at Physics) and the coordinator at a respective faculty (e.g. at Mathematics). In the fields of study such as physics, there is a possibility for incoming students to carry out research projects in foreign languages.

details.Description: North Carolina State University is a pre-eminent research enterprise that excels in science, technology, engineering, math, design, the humanities and social sciences, textiles and veterinary medicine. With more than 35,000 students and nearly 8,000 faculty and staff, NC State University transforms lives and provides leadership for social, economic, and technological development across North Carolina and around the world. Approximately 4,800 international students are currently enrolled at NC State, and the international students and faculty represent over 120 countries. The university is within two hours of the Atlantic Ocean, and within three hours of the Blue Ridge Mountains. The area offers numerous opportunities for hiking, camping, surfing, boating and various other activities.

details.Description: Established in 1870, the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences (NIH) is a public university located in Oslo, Norway. The NIH faculty has a broad international network of research collaborators as well as more than 1600 students. NIH offers a unique learning opportunity for exchange students through a beautifully scenic campus, world-class facilities, rich campus culture, a variety of English-led classes, and diverse student activity groups all of which are available to exchange students.

details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: August – December Spring semester: January – June Important dates (https://www.nih.no/english/studies/exchange/practical-information/important-dates.html)

details.Restrictions: Courses are offered in course packages. The courses in the different packages are in the same field in sport sciences, and no conflicts in scheduling and exams will occur. Students must choose one of the course packages when completing the application. It is not possible to choose courses from different course packages. details.Description: The Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) is Norway’s largest university, with about 43,500 students in total, including a significant number of international students. It has campuses in three cities: Trondheim (its main site), Gjøvik, and Ålesund. NTNU offers a wide variety of programmes across many disciplines: science, technology, engineering, health sciences, humanities, social sciences, etc. Many master’s programmes are taught entirely in English, making it quite accessible for exchange students who don’t want to speak Norwegian. The location and surroundings of NTNU are a major part of its appeal. Trondheim, where the main campus is located, is a lively student city with a strong blend of history, culture, and nature. You get to enjoy river-side areas, a scenic fjord, forests nearby, islands, and plenty of opportunities for outdoor activities like hiking, skiing, or kayaking. The campuses themselves are fairly well integrated into the city, and public transport is good.

details.Description: Örebro is situated a two hours’ drive west from Stockholm, in the heart of Sweden: Örebro is the 6th largest town in Sweden with a population of 150,000. It is a town with a historic atmosphere that is enhanced by the winter darkness, and it stands out in a colorful bloom in the spring. Close to nature, bike-friendly and full of culture – Örebro possesses qualities of both a larger city and a classic Swedish small town. The School of Law in Örebro is combined with Psychology and Social Work studies. This exciting blend facilitates interaction, exchange of competencies and skills, and collaboration beyond subject boundaries. We are host to a number of strong research environments with prominent researchers, who are also involved in teaching at all levels. As an exchange student at Örebro University, you will be a part of a modern, broad-based University with an ambitious vision - to lead towards a knowledge-driven society. You will also be invited to take part in a one-of-a-kind three week long orientation programme offering a variety of activities
details.Academic calendar: Each semester: An orientation programme with social activities for 3-4 weeks. details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student, you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad.
details.Course information: See link to course descriptions below at 'Important links'. Higher education in Sweden is divided into three cycles: first cycle, second cycle and third cycle. The courses offered in English for exchange students are: •First cycle (Bachelor level) •Second cycle (Master level) The level and prerequisites of each course state how many credits the student is required to have achieved within the subject before being admitted to the course. The prerequisites should be carefully considered when selecting a course. The majority of law courses offered at Örebro University have the value of 15 ECTS; courses with other ECTS values may also be available. At Swedish universities, courses and modules are mainly studied one at a time. For example, a student takes a full-time course of 15 ECTS for five weeks, which also includes examination. When the course is completed, the student takes up the next course.

details.Description:
Although officially founded in 1931 as Japan's 6th imperial university, you may be interested
to learn that Osaka University's roots reach back to 1838 and Tekijuku, a private "place of
learning" founded by OGATA Koan. Today, Osaka University has four campuses: Suita, Toyonaka, Minoh, and Nakanoshima.
Furthermore, the university boasts 11 undergraduate schools, 16 graduate schools, and 29
centers and institutes for research. It is clearly one of Japan's outstanding comprehensive
universities.

details.Description: Osnabrück University is a mid-sized public university in northwestern Germany, with a student population of around 14,000 and a staff of approximately 1,200 academic employees. It is known for its interdisciplinary research and strong collaboration between faculties, particularly in the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. The university places a strong emphasis on international cooperation and offers a welcoming environment for exchange students. One of its distinctive features is the close integration of research and teaching, supported by a compact campus structure that fosters interaction across disciplines. The university is located in the city of Osnabrück, a historic and student-friendly city in Lower Saxony. With a population of just over 160,000, Osnabrück offers a manageable and affordable urban environment, while still providing a rich cultural life, green surroundings, and good public transport. The city has a strong academic and youthful character, shaped in part by its university community. Its location between the Teutoburg Forest and the Wiehen Hills also makes it attractive for students who enjoy outdoor activities alongside their studies.

They will be trained in studying migration, migration-related diversity and processes of inclusion as contested issues and objects of regulation that are observed, defined, structured and ‘produced’ by various actors, institutions, discourses, and practices – and also by migration research itself. Specific foci within the programme include: the institutional structures, policies and actors of migration regimes as regulatory systems in a cross-national and historical perspective the history of modern migration refugee migration (regimes) gender and migration the spatial dimension of migration (regimes) academic knowledge production on migration

details.Description: Panteion University of Social and Political Sciences, founded in 1927, is one of Greece’s oldest and most respected institutions dedicated exclusively to the social sciences. With around 19,000 students, it offers a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programs across departments such as Political Science, Sociology, Psychology, International and European Studies, Communication, Public Administration, and Economic and Regional Development. The university is known for its interdisciplinary academic approach, strong emphasis on research, and its role in shaping social and political thought in Greece. Situated in the Kallithea district of Athens, Panteion benefits from a central urban location with easy access to cultural landmarks, parks, and the city’s vibrant everyday life. The university is well connected to the rest of Athens via public transport, making it simple to explore both the historical and modern sides of the city. Students often enjoy the nearby neighborhoods filled with local cafés, bookshops, and outdoor spaces, all contributing to a lively and engaging study abroad experience.

details.Description: Pompeu Fabra University (UPF), founded in 1990, is a modern public university located in the heart of Barcelona. It serves a student population of around 12,000 and is known for its strong focus on research, innovation, and internationalization. UPF offers programmes across social sciences, humanities, communication, health, and life sciences, and maintains a high level of academic performance and global engagement. The university emphasizes interdisciplinary learning and is closely connected to local and international research networks. Its compact urban campuses foster a dynamic and accessible academic environment. Barcelona provides an ideal setting for student life, combining Mediterranean climate, rich cultural heritage, and excellent public transport. The city is known for its architecture, beaches, and vibrant neighborhoods, all easily reachable by metro, tram, or bike. Students benefit from a wide range of cultural events, cafés, and outdoor activities throughout the year. A fun fact: Barcelona is home to one of the few beaches in the world that was artificially created for the Olympics—before 1992, the city had no real beach culture. Today, it’s a central part of student life and a symbol of the city’s transformation.

details.Description: Pusan National University (PNU) is a prestigious national university located in Busan, the second largest city in Korea and a gateway to the Eurasian continent. It was established as Korea’s first national university on May 15, 1946, and now has the status of Korea’s best national university. Pusan National University has fulfilled its mission as a regional hub university, actively engaged in the past 70 years of successful industrialization and democratization in South Korea. As 2019 marks the 73rd anniversary of its foundation, the university focuses on strengthening its research and educational capacities as Korea’s best national university. It aims to become a global research-oriented university with this overarching vision: “a university guided by the future of students and a university loved by the people.” Four separate specialized campuses with strong research and education infrastructure Pusan National University has four multi-campuses located in the southeast region of the Korean peninsula. The Busan Campus has great history and traditions.

The university has more than 32,000 students. The Mile End campus is home to most of the academic Schools and offers shops, cafés, restaurants, a gym and the 24-hour library. There’s plenty of green and outdoor space, but you’re only minutes away from Central London’s bustling streets.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Generally, a language test is required – see options for exemption below. In order to fulfil the entry requirements you need to take one of the language tests stated below: •A TOEFL iBT: 100 overall score (only internet-based TOEFL tests are accepted) with 24 in Writing, 18 in Reading, 17 in Listening and 20 in Speaking. •An IELTS: 7.0 points overall score with 6.5 in Writing, 5.5 in Reading, Listening and Speaking. You can also see the language requirements stated on Queen Mary’s homepage (https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/englishlanguagerequirements/undergraduate/) . Exception possible with a Danish diploma and sufficient grades You can obtain an exemption from the language requirements if you have a Danish STX/HF/HHX or HTX diploma or certificate with examination grades in English in oral and written English at 10. If your diploma contains only one exam e.g. in written English – then your in-class assessment grade [årskarakter] in oral English will also be taken into account and must contain a grade at 10 or above. And vice versa, if your diploma contains only one exam in oral English – then your in-class assessment grade from your written exam in English will also be taken into account and must contain a grade at 10 or above. Be aware that your transcript/diploma must not be dated any earlier than 5 years prior to the start date of the exchange. An institutional language confirmation stating that the student achieved a certain level will not be sufficient. During the admission procedures, Queen Mary must receive a scan of the diploma/certificate displaying the original marks of 10 or above.

details.Description: Law has been studied and taught at Queens since 1845. The years since have seen many changes and challenges for the legal profession in Belfast. Legal and political developments have drawn a great deal of interest to law throughout the United Kingdom and Ireland, as well as to the distinctive aspects of the Northern Irish legal system. In more recent years the School has had an increased focus on European, international and comparative law. The School of Law is situated in a modern state of the art building from 2016. It features world class facilities to support an innovative culture of learning.

details.Description: ESADE is a global academic institution known for the quality of its education, its international outlook, and its focus on holistic personal development. ESADE has strong ties to the business world ESADE Law School is Spain’s top private university for studying law and one of the most innovative law schools in the world. With more than thirty years of history, ESADE Law School is synonymous with excellence, an international focus, academic expertise and permanent connection with the professional world.

Danish law exchange students are, however, exempt for providing any language documentation.
details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. In the spring semester, you may find a selection of law courses taught in English but be aware of a more limited course selection compared to the autumn semester – also due to timetable overlaps.
details.Course information: Law courses have typically the value of 3, 4 or 5 ECTS making it quite common to register for approximately eight courses in total to reach 30 ECTS. Usually, course descriptions for the following academic year  become available in June. The first 2 weeks after arrival, it is generally possible to add and drop courses. The majority of courses are taught in seminar classes with mandatory attendance where active participation may be included in the final grade for some of the courses. You may expect less group work and less reading. The exams are mostly closed book and written by hand. Below at 'Important links' you will find access to law course offers. After admission you will obtain admission to the intranet called mySADE.

details.Description: Reykjavik University is a modern and innovative institution which has around 3,500 students, creating a close and collaborative learning environment. The university offers a wide range of courses taught in English, particularly at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Its main campus is located in central Reykjavik, designed with open spaces and modern facilities that encourage creativity and cooperation among students. Reykjavik, the capital of Iceland, is a small yet lively city surrounded by breathtaking natural scenery. It is known for being safe, friendly, with well-planned paths and compact neighborhoods that make daily life convenient. The city offers a rich cultural scene with music, art, and festivals throughout the year, as well as cozy cafes and geothermal pools that reflect the local lifestyle. Just outside the city, students can enjoy stunning landscapes such as volcanic fields, waterfalls, and coastal views, making Reykjavik an ideal place to combine academic studies with outdoor adventure.

details.Description: Riga Graduate School of Law (RGSL) is a specialized law school located in Riga, Latvia. RGSL offers interdisciplinary bachelor and masters programmes in law, allowing engaged and curious students to combine their law studies with courses in business, international relations, finance and diplomacy.

On bachelor level (one semester would then be comprised of 3 modules × 6 weeks each, with exams at the end of each module). On Masters level - 2 weeks foundation courses, then 8 weeks long study modules (2 modules per semester).

details.Description: The history of Ritsumeikan dates back to 1869 when Prince Kinmochi Saionji, an eminent international statesman of modern Japan, founded "Ritsumeikan" as a private academy on the site of the Kyoto Imperial Palace. Today, Ritsumeikan University offers a wide range of courses in advanced studies at its Kinugasa Campus in Kyoto, Biwako‐Kusatsu Campus (BKC) in Shiga and Osaka‐Ibaraki Campus (OIC) in Osaka. The Study in Kyoto Program (SKP) brings together students from around the world. It offers numerous courses in Japanese language and culture, utilizing the extensive historical and cultural resources of the ancient city of Kyoto. The program also offers courses in English regarding both Japan‐related and business subjects. Kyoto, the capital of Japan from 794 to 1868, is an ideal place for study, being a city with one of the highest concentrations of academic institutions in Japan. Kyoto is home to some of Japan's most important World Heritage Sites such as the Ryoanji, Ninnaji and Kinkakuji (Golden Pavilion) Temples, which are located right at the doorstep of Ritsumeikan University. It enjoys a harmonious blend of the ancient and the modern, thus giving students the unique opportunity to experience all aspects of Japanese society. By studying in SKP at Ritsumeikan University, students are able to take advantage of the rich academic and cultural environment of this city, leading to a truly fruitful and memorable study experience in Japan.

details.Description: RWTH Aachen University (Rheinisch-Westfälische Technische Hochschule Aachen) is the largest university of technology in Germany and one of the most renowned in Europe. Every year, numerous international students and scientists come to the university to benefit from its high quality courses and excellent facilities, both of which are recognised at an international level. With its 260 institutes in nine faculties, RWTH Aachen is among the leading European scientific and research institutions. details.Additional requirements (academic - deta: Semester Fulfillment All applicants must currently be enrolled in at least second semester (= have already completed at least one semester) at SNU's application stage (i.e. before March for exchange in the following Fall Semester, and before September for exchange in the following Spring Semester). SNU cannot accept graduate exchange students who did not complete at least one semester of their graduate program once SNU's application period starts. details.Description: The Sigmund Freud University (SFU) was founded in 2003 with the aim of transforming psychotherapy into psychotherapy science, based on an academic foundation. The campus is located in Vienna. Sigmund Freud University pioneered the study of Psychotherapy Science as an academic degree. This program approaches Psychotherapy by emphasizing research activities, practical training, and academic exchange among different psychotherapy schools. Sigmund Freud University is one of the only academic institutions in the world, where Psychotherapy is taught at an undergraduate level.

details.Description:
Located on British Columbia's west coast Simon Fraser University opened in 1965 with 2,500
students. The university is now boasting more than 37,000 students and three campuses:
Burnaby Campus, Surrey Campus and Vancouver Campus. The Burnaby- and the Surrey Campus
are both approximately 40 min from downtown Vancouver, but can be easily reached with the
famous Expo Line. SFU is the first Canadian member of the National Collegiate Athletic Association, the world’s

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Students applying for undergraduate level at SFU: Documents accepted: Official Transcript which states the language of instruction is English, or a letter if currently studying in a degree program in which the principal language of instruction is English at an institution where the principal language of instruction is not English (only relevant for students at master's level at UCPH as all BA programs are Danish) or - Completion of a three-unit post-secondary level course taught in English with a passing grade. Documents accepted: Official Transcript which states the language of instruction for the course is English, or a statement from the Exchange Coordinator stating that they have successfully completed at least one English-taught course or - TOEFL-test: 88 (minimum score of 20 in each category) or - IELTS-test: 6.5 with no part les than 6.0 Students applying for Graduate level at SFU: -Documents accepted: Official Transcript which states the language of instruction is English, or a letter if currently studying in a degree program in which the principal language of instruction is English at an institution where the principal language of instruction is not English (only relevant for students at master's level at UCPH as all BA programs are Danish) or - Have completed a degree at an institution where the principal language of instruction was English, or a degree program in which the principal language of instruction was English (in an institution where the principal language of instruction was not English). Documents accepted: Previous degree official transcript stating the language of instruction was English, or letter from institution stating that degree was English-taught or - TOEFL-test: overall score of 93 or better with a minimum score of 20 in each of the four components or Duolingo English Test (DET) with an overall minimum score of 125, with a minimum of 105 in each section or - IELTS-test: 7.0 (with no part less than 6.5)

details.Restrictions: Restrictions and Considerations (http://www.sfu.ca/students/exchange/academic-information/restricted-subjects-and-courses.html) For students who wants to apply for graduate studies at SFU: The vast majority of exchange students at SFU are admitted as undergraduates. At Simon Fraser University, undergraduate degrees are generally four years in length. This means that many exchange students who are graduate students at their home universities may actually be better suited to take undergraduate Upper-Division courses (300 and 400 level) at SFU, especially if they are in the first year of their graduate degrees.  Note that being admitted as a graduate student may impact which SFU Residence building for which you are eligible. Graduate students will only be able to apply for courses from one department, and this is the department to which we will request students to be admitted. While you can request courses from additional departments, access cannot be guaranteed. There are many specialized and cohort-based graduate programs at SFU, which exchange students may not be able to access.

details.Description: SMU was established on 29 July 2000 and is located in the Downtown area of Singapore. It has a city campus with a total enrolment of about 10,000 undergraduate and postgraduate students and comprises six schools offering undergraduate, graduate and PhD programmes in business administration, business analytics, financial services, accountancy, economics, information systems management, law and the social sciences.   The university has over 30 research institutes and centres of excellence, and customised corporate training and lifelong learning for individuals are available through the university's professional and executive development programmes. SMU comprises six schools: - School of Accountancy - Lee Kong Chian School of Business - School of Economics - School of Information Systems - School of Law - School of Social Sciences SMU has an emphasis on generating rigorous, high‐impact, and relevant multi‐disciplinary research that addresses Asian issues of global relevance, SMU faculty collaborate with leading international researchers and universities from USA, Europe, China and India as well as with partners in the business community and public sector, through its research institutes, centres and labs. SMU’s city campus is a state‐of‐the‐art facility located in the heart of downtown Singapore, fostering strategic linkages with business, government and the wider community.

details.Restrictions: Please note that this exchange programme is for undergraduate students as it will not be possible to take graduate courses at SMU Eligibility 1. Applicants must have completed at least one academic year of undergraduate studies 2. Applicants must continue to be a registered undergraduate in their home university throughout the period of study at SMU 3. Applicants must fulfil the English language proficiency requirement by SMU. Course enrolment is conducted via a bidding exercise in July (Term 1) and December (Term 2) each year. Only undergraduate courses from a prescribed list are applicable to exchange and visiting students (Course Codes 001‐499). Students will be allocated e$100 dollars (one‐time only), for bidding of all their courses. This empowers them to draw up their own timetable based on their recommended study plan (subject to constraints of curriculum requirements and the supply and demand of classes). Details and instructions related to course bidding together with the list of courses offered, shall be made available to students between two to four weeks before the course bidding exercise. It is important that students understand the information, policies and procedures to ensure a smooth bidding process. Demand could be high for some courses, e.g. fundamental freshmen courses. Students are encouraged to be pro‐active and flexible in their study plans to optimise their bidding opportunities.

details.Description: Sorbonne Nouvelle University (Université Sorbonne Nouvelle – Paris 3) is a public institution within the Sorbonne group, specialising in the humanities and social sciences. It hosts approximately 18,000 students and employs over 1,300 academic and administrative staff. The university is known for its strong international orientation and its commitment to interdisciplinary research. As part of the European University Alliance UNA Europa, Sorbonne Nouvelle contributes to collaborative academic initiatives across the continent. Its structure supports close engagement between students and faculty, and its programmes are designed to foster analytical thinking and academic independence. The university is located in Paris, with its main campus situated in the 12th arrondissement near Place de la Nation. This area offers good transport connections and access to a range of cultural and everyday amenities. Paris itself is home to numerous academic institutions, libraries, and research centres, making it a central location for higher education in Europe. The city’s historical significance, public infrastructure, and international character provide a stimulating environment for students. An exchange semester at Sorbonne Nouvelle offers the opportunity to study in a major European capital while engaging with a diverse academic and social landscape.

details.Description: Sorbonne University, a prestigious and globally renowned academic institution, stands as a multidisciplinary and research-driven university. Firmly rooted in the heart of Paris, its historical roots trace back to 1257, making it one of the oldest universities in Europe. With its three faculties encompassing Arts & Humanities, Medicine, and Science and Engineering, the university is dedicated to nurturing student excellence and addressing the scientific complexities of the modern era. Serving as a beacon of higher education and research, Sorbonne University holds a distinguished position within the French academic landscape. Furthermore, Sorbonne is a part of 4EU+ Alliance with the purpose of laying the foundation for an innovative European university model. Sorbonne is fully committed to engage with both its students and partners on an international scale. The university believes that internalization and innovation go hand in hand. In terms of student life, Sorbonne offers more than 80 sporting and artistic activities which are free to join as students off the university.
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Academic calendar: https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/education/study-sorbonne-university/degree-seeking-students/practical-information (https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/education/study-sorbonne-university/degree-seeking-students/practical-information) Autumn semester: Mid September – January 31 Winter semester: End of January – June 30 Inbound Erasmus students must come a week earlier to go to an Erasmus meeting, get their student card and the general information about their stay and to enroll in their chosen courses.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: For students taking courses at the Faculty of Lettres (Humanities): A French language certificate (minimum level B2) is required: Official tests such as DALF, DELF, TCF, Alliance Française, official language level certificate from a teacher or a French language training institute are accepted. OLS certificates are also accepted as proof of French language proficiency, on one condition: It must be accompanied by a letter from a professor confirming the student's language level. For students taking courses at the Faculty of Science and Engineering: As an exception: Undergraduate applicants wishing to join the Physics Department must demonstrate a minimum C1 level through a recognized language test such as TCF, DELF or DALF. For other study areas with The Faculty of Science and Engineering no official test is required. However, we recommend a minimum B2 level in either English or French, depending on the language of the selected courses. Generally, UCPH strongly recommends the higher level C1 (advanced proficiency in French) when studying at Sorbonne University - to make sure that you can cope sufficiently in courses taught in French. Almost all courses and exams are in held French. In English, it is rarely possible to find a full study load of 30 ECTS. If you are studying at their Faculty of Science and Engineering, there may be a chance of finding enough courses in English, though experience tells us that this is not always the case.
details.Restrictions: The Master students can take BA and MA level courses, but the Bachelor students can only take BA level courses. If BA students are interested in a MA level course, they must ask the academic coordinator and the professor of the MA course if they can take this course. Most courses are taught in French, with the exception of certain language departments where courses are taught in both the learned language and French. It is very unlikely that student can find a full study load in English and must therefore be very proficient in French. You must be able to get a pre-approval of 30 ECTS from UCPH per semester. Restrictions for UCPH-students: - Political Science-students (Statskundskab) at BA-level cannot find courses at Sorbonne for their semester 5 - There are no courses in Economics at Sorbonne - There are no courses in Law at Sorbonne
details.Course information: On this exchange agreement you may look for interesting study areas with the two faculties below: Faculté de Lettres/Faculty of Arts and Humanities - discover the Schools and departments (https://lettres.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/faculty-arts-languages-literature-and-humanities/schools-and-departments) Course catalogue for Faculty of Arts and Humanities: https://moodle-lettres-24.sorbonne-universite.fr/course/view.php?id=403#section-1 (https://moodle-lettres-24.sorbonne-universite.fr/course/view.php?id=403#section-1) . When you have chosen e.g. 'lettres' then press 'Tout dépliér' as it may give you access to additional info. Incoming Erasmus students must take at least 50% of their workload inside their main department. The rest of their workload can be made up of courses from other departments within this Faculty. Questions to Faculty of Humanities can be sent to; lettres-erasmus-inri@sorbonne-universite.fr (mailto:lettres-erasmus-inri@sorbonne-universite.fr) Faculté des Sciences et IngénieriFaculty of Science & Engineering - se info on study areas (https://sciences.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/study/our-programmes-0/programs-french) . Course catalogue for Faculty of Science & Engineering: https://sciences.sorbonne-universite.fr/formation-sciences/offre-de-formation (https://sciences.sorbonne-universite.fr/formation-sciences/offre-de-formation) and list of English courses at FSI can be found here; https://sciences.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/study/our-programmes (https://sciences.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/study/our-programmes) Questions to Faculty of Science and Engineering; sciences-dfipve-mobilite-in@sorbonne-universite.fr (mailto:sciences-dfipve-mobilite-in@sorbonne-universite.fr) Later on at the nomination process, you must be assigned to a specific department and study area within the specific faculty. Be aware that Sorbonne has different campuses all over the city, so remember to check the transportation time if you take classes in different campuses the same day.
details.Important links: Information for exchange students (https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/education/study-sorbonne-university/exchange-students) See study areas within the Faculty of Arts and Humanities: https://formations-lettres.sorbonne-universite.fr//fr/index.html (https://formations-lettres.sorbonne-universite.fr//fr/index.html) Practical information: https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/education/study-sorbonne-university/degree-seeking-students/practical-information (https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/education/study-sorbonne-university/degree-seeking-students/practical-information) Sorbonne University’s official website: https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en (https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en)
details.Housing: Sorbonne University does offer some accommodation for exchange students; however, it is important to note that they do not guarantee accommodation, so international students are recommend to look for private housing when possible. Students receive information about housing when nominated for Erasmus. Consider Fondation Danoise in Cité Universitaire. Accommodation in general is very expensive in Paris, and difficult to find.

details.Academic calendar:
You decide when you want to start your clinical exchange.
Once you have been nominated for an exchange place, you and the coordinators at the host university will plan exactly when you should start and end your stay.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: B2 – French B2 – French corresponds to A level at Danish upper secondary school. See the CEFR-scale on the Council of Europe’s website. (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale)
details.Study plan: Fifth semester on the master’s programme: International Perspective with a Stay in a Clinic Abroad When you spend your fifth semester at a foreign university, you must follow the following study plan: 12-14 weeks of elective clinical training Read more about doing the fifth semester abroad on Study Information. (https://kunet.ku.dk/studie/medicin-ka/Sider/Emne.aspx?topicid=549e18de-2ced-41cc-a674-3e965197799a#1036739_noPictureOnTop_content)
details.Course information: On your exchange in the fifth semester, you have the opportunity to prepare your own study plan based on the specialisations offered by the university hospital. You will need to agree your final study plan with the coordinators at the host university, depending on their capacity and availability. Clinical rotations at Sorbonne University: The clinical rotations at Sorbonne University last one month. This means that you must participate in three rotations during your exchange. Find more information about the clinical rotations on offer. (https://sante.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/international/incoming/internship-medicine-students) ECTS credits for clinical rotations: Each clinical rotation (each lasting one month) equates to 3 ECTS credits. In order to obtain advance approval of the transfer of credits, you must do a minimum of 12 weeks of clinical training. It is therefore essential that you do three rotations, which will make up the 12 weeks. On this basis you will be granted pre-approval of your credits.

details.Description: Stellenbosch University is a public research university situated in the town of Stellenbosch, South Africa. Other nearby universities are the University of Cape Town and University of the Western Cape. Stellenbosch University (SU) is home to an academic community of 29 000 students (including 4 000 foreign students from 100 countries) as well as 3 000 permanent staff members (including 1 000 academics) on five campuses. The main campus in the picturesque university town of Stellenbosch in the heart of the Western Cape winelands is quite an attraction for students. Stellenbosch is situated about 50 km from Cape Town and just 30 km from Cape Town International Airport. SU has ten faculties: AgriSciences, Economic and Management Sciences, Medicine and Health Sciences, Engineering, Military Sciences, Arts and Social Sciences, Science, Education, Law and Theology.

details.Academic calendar: Semester 1: January to June Semester 2: July to December Academic Calendar (sun.ac.za) (https://www.sun.ac.za/english/dates)
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: English B2 ( Self-assessment CEFR-grid (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) ) Courses are offered in English, Afrikaans or the T-option (a combination of English and Afrikaans in the same class with notes available in English). The language of instruction will be indicated in relevant department’s website and the yearbook of the relevant faculty. Please familiarize yourself with the language of instruction when choosing courses.
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 60 NQF credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Study load for graduate students: 60 NQF credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Conversion and levels: Study load is calculated according to the level of the specific course. Please note that not all UCPH Master’s (graduate) programmes allow credit transfer of bachelor (undergraduate) courses into their programmes. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: Exchange students will receive a full tuition fee waiver, but will be required to pay the Exchange Administrative Fee (EAF), which is applicable to all exchange students: Fees: Partner institutions (sun.ac.za) (https://www.sun.ac.za/english/SUInternational/international-students/fees/fees-partner-institutions) Exchange students cannot take courses at the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences, the Faculty of Military Science, the Department of Accounting and Stellenbosch Business School. Please note that approval for any study area is dependent on academic background and acceptance by department. Students are expected to be present during the entire exam period as no exams will be allowed to be taken at home; for this reason it is extremely important that students book their return flight no earlier than the end of the 2nd exam period. Semester students require a study visa. Students apply for a visa after being accepted to Stellenbosch University. Exchange students are required to have a health insurance that meets certain requirements.

details.Description: Stockholm University, established in 1878 as a college and granted university status in 1960, is a renowned public research university located in Stockholm, Sweden. With its rich history and academic excellence, the university attracts over 33,000 students, making it one of the largest universities in Scandinavia. The university comprises four faculties offering a wide range of academic programs. Situated in the world's first national urban park, the campus blends seamlessly with nature, architecture, and modern art, providing a unique and inspiring learning environment. The main campus, Frescati, is conveniently located near an underground railway station, facilitating easy access for students. Stockholm is spread across islands connected by bridges, offering picturesque views of waterways, parks and historic architecture. It’s an easy city to navigate on foot with a lively cultural scene including museums, concerts, cafes and festivals. The surroundings offer easy access to forests, lakes and the Stockholm Archipelago with thousands of islands just a short boat trip away.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: Late August to mid-January Winter semester: Mid-January to early June Each semester is divided into 4 parts: Period 1 (A and B) and Period 2 (C and D). See more information in the academic calendar (https://www.su.se/english/education/during-your-studies/term-dates) .
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Language of instruction: Swedish and English. Students whose mother tongue is not English are recommended to have at least a level of B2-C1 in the self-assessment CEFR-grid (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) or equivalent to an overall IELTS score of 6.5 or TOEFL score of 100 internet-based. Stockholm University does, however, not require any test results or any language documentation.
details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student, you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. Generally, all law courses have the value of 15 ECTS. Be aware that most law courses offered to exchange students are taught at graduate level. You must have studied min. 120 ECTS in law (i.e. 2 years of full-time studies) and preferably more before the exchange programme. All courses have mandatory active attendance. This is means that students are expected to attend their classes well-prepared and ready to actively discuss the contents of the day’s lecture/seminar/etc. For optimal class dynamics it is therefore very important that you are ready for this style of teaching.

details.Additional information: The Faculty of Law at Stockholm University is the biggest Law Faculty in Sweden, both in number of researchers and in number of students. Virtually all fields of law are represented at the Faculty of Law. Stockholm offers a full range of educational possibilities in law and is ranked among the top 100 law schools in the world. Founded in 1893, Stockholm University’s Department of Law maintains the tradition of high-quality legal education with a focus on putting theory into practice and taking full advantage of the expertise found in an innovative, dynamic capital city. We offer three LLM programs in English. These internationally focused master’s programs are some of the most highly regarded and highly competitive programs at the university and have a strong, international reputation. Exchange programme for both bachelor and master level law students. When The Faculty of Law in Copenhagen has nominated you for an exchange place at Stockholm University, you have to apply for admission within the application deadlines which may vary a bit from year to year.

The university is highly ranked in Asia and is also the oldest in East Asia. Focuses on both
traditions and innovation. Very interested in global collaboration and outlook and known for its
strong academic profile. The university is divided into two campuses: Humanities and social
sciences in central Seoul, natural sciences in Suwon. The university has 26,000 Bachelor’s degree
students and 8,000 Master’s degree students

Not required for students who meet at least one of the following: 1) Native speakers 2) Students other than those choosing Business Administration majors in SKKU 3) Applicants from institutions in which English is the primary language of instruction (Students must submit an official letter from the home university confirming the above statement.)
details.Restrictions: Not all courses are open to exchange students as they require special application eligibility or completion of prerequisite courses. The number of English courses may be limited for some undergraduate majors. The following fields of study are restricted and not open to exchange students: Graduate Schools: - Special Graduate Schools - Graduate School of Medicine - Graduate School of Pharmacy - Specialty Graduate Schools (SKK Graduate School of Business, SKK Graduate School of China, Graduate School of Law, Graduate School of Governance, Graduate School of Education, Graduate School of TESOL/Translation) Undergraduate Schools: - School of Medicine - School of Pharmacy - Public Affairs - Law - College of Art (open, but very few courses conducted in English. Theatre is not open for exchange students) Note! Exchange students are classified as bachelor's degree students in the SKKU system, and they must follow a separate method for enrolling in graduate school classes, which will be announced around SKKU's course registration period. Please note that English-taught graduate-level classes are limited.

details.Additional information:
SKKU offers more than 7,000 courses throughout the academic year in every field and level
of study. Currently, over 30% of courses are conducted in foreign languages, primarily
English. The reason for this is twofold: first to provide a chance for SKKU students to improve
their global competence and language capabilities, and secondly to provide a larger selection
of classes for international students who are not fluent in Korean. SKKU is actively recruiting
renowned foreign professors while providing a series of retraining programs for Korean
faculty aimed at enhancing language and lecture skills

details.Description: Sungkyunkwan University was founded at the beginning of the Joseon Dynasty in 1398 as the highest national educational institute in the early years of the Joseon Dynasty in Korea. As the oldest university in East Asia, it has fostered leaders of our society for over 600 years. 'SKKU's main ideology, 수기치인 (修己治人) pronounced 'Su-Gi-Chi-In', teaches that SKKU students strive to perfect themselves as leaders and contribute to our society. This ideology is the fundamental principle by which SKKU brought up leaders of our society for over 600 years, thus contributing to evolution of our society. Sungkyunkwan University, continuously strives to integrate its founding tradition philosophy with the modern technology in order with a view to cultivating global graduate’ s talents who will lead the 21st century. Old Sungkyunkwan was founded over 600 years ago by royal decree to promote education the scholarship in Confucianism. As nation's highest educational institution, Old Sungkyunkwan went through vicissitudes with the country it served over the centuries. Though a long history alone cannot guarantee the excellence of an institution, the rich culture, is surely a unique and valuable asset of the university. What the university has achieved in the past fifty years meets and exceeds that of the preceding history. We take pride in the university's innovative spirit; as a result of the long efforts to place natural sciences on an equal footing with our strong foundation in humanities, we now operate two campuses: the Humanities and Social Sciences Campus and the Natural Sciences Campus. Based on a highly successful partnership with Samsung which has generously funded several core initiatives, the university has been rapidly developing and prospering since 1996.
details.Grade requirements: Students must have a cumulative grade point average of 6.5 on the Danish grading scale. If you are appointed a spot for this agreement with a GPA higher than 6.5 but your GPA gets scaled down to a lower GPA than 6.5 in the period until the host universitys application deadline, there is a risk that your application will be rejected by the host university and your exchange stay will not be possible.

Any remaining spots may be allocated to applicants who are planning an ordinary exchange. Therefore, you cannot rely on the calculation of available spots as stated in the fact sheet.
details.Course information: For students going on mandatory stay It is your responsibility to sign up for courses that are restricted to be credit transferred to the courses related to your mandatory stay as stated in your curricula. If you need help to find courses that can be credit transferred in accordance to the requirements of your mandatory stay please reach out to the student guidance counselor at your department. For graduate students: Exchange students are classified as bachelor's degree students in the SKKU system, and they must follow a separate method for enrolling in graduate school classes, which will be announced around SKKU's course registration period. Please note that English-taught graduate-level classes are limited.

details.Description:
Sungshin University was founded in 1936 with the the following educational mottos: Sungshin
(act with sincerity and faith), Jishin (strive for new knowledge and Jadong (be independent).
Today Sungshin University is comprised of 13 undergraduate colleges, 5 graduate schools and
approximately 13.000 students enrolled. Sungshin is a women university but male exchange
students are welcome. Male students are also enrolled at the graduate schools.

details.Description: Looking for an unforgettable exchange experience that blends academic rigor with cultural discovery? Tajik National University (TNU) in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, invites international students to step into a world where tradition meets innovation. Why Choose TNU? Academic Diversity : With over 20 faculties ranging from law and economics to natural sciences and international relations, TNU offers a broad spectrum of courses tailored to global learners. Cultural Immersion : Experience Tajikistan’s rich heritage, stunning landscapes, and warm hospitality. From ancient Silk Road history to vibrant local festivals, every day is a cultural adventure. Affordable & Accessible : Enjoy a high-quality education and low cost of living in one of Central Asia’s most welcoming capitals. Language & Learning : Courses are offered in Tajik and Russian, with growing support for English-speaking students. It’s a great opportunity to expand your linguistic horizons. Strategic Location : Nestled between China, Afghanistan, and Uzbekistan, Tajikistan is a gateway to exploring the diverse cultures of Central Asia.

details.Restrictions: You are expected to take at least 60% of your courses at TUM Informatics. If you wish to attend courses at other departments, be aware of prerequisites and matching timetables. Bachelor students with at least 2 years (120 ECTS) of prior studies in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a similar subject can take courses at Master level. This means (in order to take English taught courses) you need to meet the following minimum requirements : Programming, Algorithms, Data Structures, Mathematics, Software Engineering. Preferably : Data Bases, Computer Architecture, Operating Systems, Networks, Automata, Formal Languages Please note that IN5xxx, IN8xxx and xxHNxxxx modules are not open for exchange students. In case you want to pursue a thesis during your exchange stay at TUM Informatics, you have to follow the regular TUM rules for thesis on bachelor's and master's level. You are expected to stay for a year if you wish pursue your thesis in the second semester At IN.TUM a Bachelor’s Thesis has usually 15 ECTS (duration of four months) or 25 ECTS (duration of 5 months). A Master’s Thesis lasts 6 months and has 30 ECTS. A thesis has to be registered and submitted in time and according to our rules. You must comply with scheduled exam dates and times which usually to take place between February and March (winter semester) and between July and September (summer semester). Resits/Retakes at TUM Informatics are offered for some but not all lectures. Resits take place in late September/October (registration in September) for summer semester, and late March/April for winter semester (registration in March). Students enrolled at TUM during the current semester can take the resits of the upcoming retake-period.

details.Description: Tohoku University, founded in 1907, is one of Japan’s top national research institutions and has a long-standing reputation for academic excellence and innovation. Exchange students can choose from a wide range of courses taught in English across fields such as materials science, engineering, political science, and the humanities. The university also offers opportunities in business-related subjects through its School of Economics and Management, where students can explore topics like finance, international business, and marketing from both theoretical and applied perspectives. Tohoku is known for its research-first philosophy and interdisciplinary approach, and students benefit from small class sizes and close interaction with faculty. Located in Sendai, a lively city often called Japan’s “City of Trees,” Tohoku University offers an inviting academic environment within a vibrant, student-friendly setting. The city is surrounded by mountains and coastline, making it easy to enjoy nature year-round, while still offering the convenience and culture of a modern urban center. Parks, cafés, art spaces, and festivals help create an engaging atmosphere, and student clubs across academic and cultural interests provide an excellent way for exchange students to connect with peers and get involved in university life.

details.Description:
Tokai University is a private university established by Dr. Shigeyoshi Matsumae in1942. "Tokai"
of "Tokai University" refers to the sea to the east of Asia, namely the Pacific Ocean, and
symbolizes the desire to foster a rich spirit and broad perspectives. Tokai University consists of 7
campuses in Sapporo, Takanawa, Yoyogi, Shonan, Isehara, Shimizu and Kumamoto, which are
comprised of 19 schools and colleges made up of 75 departments, majors, and programs. Its
graduate schools offer 17 programs. The total student population is approximately 30,000. The
founding spirit and objectives of Tokai University are to contribute to human society, to foster
active, talented people and to arouse interest in our earth and a sense of responsibility for the
future of mankind. Tokai University's educational guidelines ground these objectives by offering
a sound and reliable way of thinking as a basis for living and cultivating the richness of
humanity. Tokai University maintains academic exchange agreements with more than 120
universities/organizations in approx. 40 countries. A wide range of international exchange
activities are being actively pursued, from those on the academic front involving students,
researchers, joint-research projects, and the exchange of academic resources, to cultural and
athletic exchanges. There are about 960 international students on campus. Tokai University has
five offices abroad: Denmark, Austria, USA (junior college in Hawaii), Korea and Thailand. Tokai
University has since its beginning maintained close ties to Denmark and Danish educational
culture: Link (https://www.u-tokai.ac.jp/english/about/founder.html)

details.Scholarships:
The student selected for an exchange place on this agreement has to actively apply for the grant from Heiwa Nakajima Foundation. The selected student will receive information about the application procedure. The Heiwa Nakajima Foundation aims to provide a stable and successive environment giving foreign students majoring in Japanese language studies the opportunity to study in Japan. Applicants must be undergraduate students majoring in Japanese language studies as a compulsory subject and must study in Japan for a period of one year. Applicants must maintain their enrollment as undergraduate students at their home universities
throughout their study in Japan. The scholarship is a monthly stipend of 120,000 yen, preparation and travel expenses will be covered as determined by the Foundation. In addition, students are automatically considered for KU’s Internationalisation scholarship.
details.Additional information: Tokai University offers one student from Japan Studies at University of Copenhagen the opportunity to study at Tokai University for a full year (fall + spring) with the support from the Heiwa Nakajima Foundation.

details.Description: Université Toulouse Capitole is a prominent French public university specializing in law, economics, management, and political science. With roots dating back to the 13th century, the university has evolved into a modern institution known for its academic rigor and international outlook. It hosts several renowned research centers and offers a wide range of graduate and postgraduate programs, many of which are taught in English. The university attracts a diverse student body, including a growing number of international students, and maintains strong partnerships with institutions across Europe and beyond. Its commitment to interdisciplinary research and professional development makes it an excellent choice for students seeking both academic depth and career-oriented training. Located in the heart of Toulouse, Université Toulouse Capitole offers students the chance to study in one of France’s most dynamic and student-friendly cities. Toulouse is known for its vibrant cultural life, historical charm, and strong presence in the aerospace and technology sectors. The city combines a rich architectural heritage with a youthful energy, making it an ideal environment for both academic focus and social engagement. Students can enjoy a wide range of cultural events, outdoor activities, and a welcoming atmosphere that supports both learning and personal growth. An exchange semester at Toulouse Capitole promises not only academic enrichment but also a memorable experience in one of southern France’s most attractive urban settings.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Toulouse requires level B2 in French or English according to the European CEFR-scale (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) depending on the language taught in your courses (be aware that it may be difficult to find enough courses taught in English). After the application process in Copenhagen - you must send language cerficates for one or both languages when you apply for admission. French language requirements: DELF : Diplôme d’Études en Langue Française : B2 DALF : Diplôme Approfondi de Langue Française TCF : Test de Connaissance du Français : 450 English language requirements: CAMBRIDGE – FCE, CAE, CPE IELTS (Academic module) overall 6 TOEFL iBT: 79 TOEIC: 785 Duolingo English Test: minimum score 115 TOEFL ITP  - is not accepted! In general, visiting French universities requires a high level of French. Often the lectures are conducted in French even if the language of instruction is suppposed to be in English.

details.Restrictions: Bachelor courses are all taught in French with just a few exceptions.
details.Course information: Master's courses may also be open to bachelor exchange students if you have a strong background in the relevant economics subjects. Therefore, please review the course prerequisites carefully. At master level, please check the ECTS-values on courses taught in English, as it may become very challenging with lots of courses with low ECTS values around 10-11 courses may expected especially in the autumn semster. In the first year of the Master’s programme, the first semester is structured as follows: 3 core modules of 30 hours each, incl. 10.5 hours of tutorials and problem sets that require a significant amount of independent study and are worth approximately 5 to 6 ECTS. 3 half-modules with 15 hours of lectures and 6 hours of tutorials, representing half the workload of the core modules and therefore worth 2.5 ECTS. Optional modules without tutorials and usually without problem sets or mid-term exams, they are introductory courses which therefore require relatively little independent study. These are worth 2 ECTS credits. As part of the core lectures (CM), you attend Tutorials (Travaux Dirigés’ TD). In TD classes, the education may be interactive with problem sets, presentations, assignments, group work etc. – an educational style familiar to the teaching methods in Copenhagen. Be aware of a very high workload in these classes.

details.Description: Trinity College Dublin, founded in 1592 by royal charter, is Ireland’s oldest and most prestigious university and the sole college of the University of Dublin. Located on a 47-acre historic campus in the heart of Dublin, it serves around 22,000 undergraduate and postgraduate students across three faculties: Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences; Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics; and Health Sciences. Trinity is internationally recognized for academic excellence and offers a broad range of programs across disciplines such as business, law, engineering, science, and the arts. The university fosters independent intellectual inquiry, interdisciplinary collaboration, and creativity, and is consistently ranked as Ireland’s leading university and among the top 100 globally in various fields. Trinity is committed to research excellence and societal impact, with world-class interdisciplinary research centres focused on areas like sustainable development, global health, artificial intelligence, and biodiversity. The university hosts a diverse and international academic community, with students and staff from over 120 countries. Trinity encourages a broad-based education, allowing students to explore subjects outside their primary field of study and develop critical thinking skills. With strong links to global industries and institutions, and a location in Dublin’s innovation and cultural hub, Trinity offers an education that is both academically rigorous and closely connected to real-world opportunities.
