details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: As part of the exchange agreement between Trinity College in Dublin and the University of Copenhagen, Danish law students are exempt from language test requirements as exchange students. A language confirmation is, however, required confirming that you have sufficient language qualifications. You can apply for a language confirmation from the Faculty of Law in Copenhagen and the confirmation will be based on your grades in English from your ‘studentereksamen’ or HF diploma. A language confirmation will only be needed after you have been nominated to the exchange programme at Trinity College.
details.Restrictions: Law modules from the LL.M. master programme will not be accessible for exchange students.
details.Course information: Modules/courses on offer to Erasmus law students are from the four years of the LL.B programme, i.e. undergraduate modules. The exchange programme is open for both bachelor and master law students, although only undergraduate courses/modules are available to visiting exchange students. As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad and generally the law modules have a value of 5 or 10 ECTS. We recommend that you take third and/or fourth year modules during your exchange programme at Trinity College. Scroll down - to see modules/courses available to Law Visiting Students (https://www.tcd.ie/law/programmes/undergraduate/modules/#VisitingLaw) •Freshman level refers to first and second year modules – they are core law modules compulsory for all Irish Law students. They are taught in large group settings of up to 200 students. •Sophister level refers to third and fourth year modules – they are elective law modules, specialising in different field of Law, that are optional for third and fourth year Law students. They can be small classes of 30 students up to 100 students. The teaching style at Trinity College is characterized by a great deal of lectures – still with some space for follow-up questions. With course offers exclusively at undergraduate level, the study level especially for master students may seem slightly easier compared to UCPH. As a former law student stated “Trinity had a very good academic programme and I did feel that the level was high at certain times, but I would say that all in all I could relax more during my courses than I would be able to back home.” Please note that some law modules may not available to exchange students.

details.Additional information: Trinity School of Law is Ireland’s oldest and most internationally renowned law school, established in 1740. With a distinguished team of professors and lecturers, many of whom are the leading experts in their fields of study, the School of Law attracts students of the highest calibre. There are over 700 students registered at undergraduate level and 180 students at postgraduate level. The School of Law is ideally situated on the historic campus of Trinity College Dublin in the heart of Dublin city, close to the courts and government buildings. Exchange students can experience the vibrant cultural life of the capital city while studying in one of Ireland’s most famous tourist attractions.

details.Description: Trinity College Dublin, founded in 1592 by royal charter, is Ireland’s oldest and most prestigious university and the sole college of the University of Dublin. Located on a 47-acre historic campus in the heart of Dublin, it serves around 22,000 undergraduate and postgraduate students across three faculties: Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences; Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics; and Health Sciences. Trinity is internationally recognized for academic excellence and offers a broad range of programs across disciplines such as business, law, engineering, science, and the arts. The university fosters independent intellectual inquiry, interdisciplinary collaboration, and creativity, and is consistently ranked as Ireland’s leading university and among the top 100 globally in various fields. Trinity is committed to research excellence and societal impact, with world-class interdisciplinary research centres focused on areas like sustainable development, global health, artificial intelligence, and biodiversity. The university hosts a diverse and international academic community, with students and staff from over 120 countries. Trinity encourages a broad-based education, allowing students to explore subjects outside their primary field of study and develop critical thinking skills. With strong links to global industries and institutions, and a location in Dublin’s innovation and cultural hub, Trinity offers an education that is both academically rigorous and closely connected to real-world opportunities.

details.Description: TU Dortmund University is a forward-looking institution that combines strong academic foundations with innovative research across a wide range of disciplines. Established over 50 years ago, the university has developed a distinctive profile with 17 departments spanning engineering, natural sciences, social sciences, and cultural studies. With approximately 30,000 students and a dedicated faculty of over 300 professors, TU Dortmund fosters a collaborative and interdisciplinary academic environment. The Department of Social Sciences, founded in 2020, is particularly notable for its integration of sociological research, didactics, and the Social Research Center (sfs), making it an exciting destination for students interested in contemporary societal challenges and applied research. Located in the Ruhr region, TU Dortmund offers students the chance to study in one of Germany’s most dynamic and evolving urban areas. Dortmund is a city with a rich industrial heritage that has successfully transformed into a center for technology, culture, and education. Students benefit from a lively cultural scene, green spaces, and a welcoming atmosphere, all within reach of major cities like Düsseldorf and Cologne. The university’s campus is well-connected and designed to support both academic and social life, making it an ideal setting for exchange students seeking a balanced and enriching experience in Germany.

details.Description: For more than 200 years, founded in 1815, TU Wien has been a place of research, teaching and learning in the service of progress. TU Wien is among the most successful technical universities in Europe and is Austria’s largest scientific-technical research and educational institution. The TU Wien is divided into eight faculties with a total of 52 institutes responsible for teaching as well as research.
details.Academic calendar: Winter semester: October – February Spring semester: March – September Academic calendar (https://www.tuwien.at/en/studies/admission/academic-calendar)

details.Restrictions: It is possible for 3rd year BSc students to follow MSc courses provided they have the pre-requisites. You may choose courses from different fields and faculties, if the places are available, and you have the prerequisites or have the equivalent knowledge necessary to enroll. Only 5% of all offered courses are taught in English. Students at Bachelor level should have excellent command in German. Structure of Bachelor's and Master’s Thesis Work at TU Wien: You may write your thesis (Bachelor: 10-12 ECTS and Master: 30 ECTS) as a part of your exchange to TU Wien. This requires a minimum of 4-5 months’ stay in Vienna. You must find a supervisor who agrees to work with you on your topic and give you written confirmation about that before you arrive in Vienna. Without such a written confirmation in advance, you will not be able to do your BSc/MSc thesis work at TU Wien as an exchange student.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: All Tulane Law School courses are taught in English. Students should be studying law fluently in English, both orally and in writing. Tulane Law School requires a confirmation from the University of Copenhagen that certifies that the student’s language qualifications are sufficient. A language confirmation will, however, only be needed after you have been nominated to the exchange programme. At that stage, you will be able to retrieve a language confirmation from UCPH in Mobility Online. Without a language confirmation from the University of Copenhagen, Tulane requires a TOEFL or an IELTS language test with specific requirements. Subject to later changes.
details.Restrictions: Law students must follow a full study load of min. 12 credits which corresponds to 30 ECTS per semester. Be aware that credit requirements may be different for other exchange students at Tulane University Law School.
details.Course information: See former course descriptions (https://law.tulane.edu/course-descriptions) . Exchange students can take any course offered by the Law School, subject to the prerequisites for any given course, except for certain clinical and skills-related courses. Exchange students take classes with JD and LLM students. Most quotas are waived for exchange students, although spring semester students should enroll prior to arrival to make sure that space is still available. The style of teaching is based on the socratic method, meaning students are actively involved by use of cold calling. However, the cold calling is used much more in 1 level classes than in higher class electives. The professors expect you to have read the cases, and that you will be ready to present them and answer questions if you get called upon in class. Special consideration may, however, be taken to exchange students who rarely experience cold calling.

details.Description: In 1955, thanks to the whole-hearted efforts of Taiwanese educators and Christians, Tunghai University was established in Taichung City , a great place for a university thanks to its geographic beauty and convenience. To serve the foreign staff of the university, the Chinese Language Centre was established in 1970, the first such centre in central Taiwan . The CLC is nestled within beautiful trees, flowers, and bird songs, making it an excellent place for learning Chinese. Through Tunghai international education has steadily promoted and Chinese education become common gradually, more and more international students and expatriates choose Tunghai University to have culture and academic exchange. The Chinese Language Centre in Tunghai provides courses of Chinese learning not only to international students, but also expatriates. To face the variety of instruction patterns in recent society­- “No limitation in classes, no boundary on learning.”

details.Description: UiT is a large, multi-campus university in Northern Norway, with around 17,000 students, globally recognised as a leading centre for Arctic research. It offers a broad spectrum of programmes across its eight faculties covering most disciplines. While Norwegian is the main language of instruction, many courses especially at the master’s level are taught in English. The city of Tromsø is often described as really special: you’re surrounded by dramatic Arctic scenery, with fjords, mountains, and islands all nearby, and you get phenomena like the Midnight Sun in summer and Northern Lights in winter. Tromsø is reasonably walkable, especially in the city centre with decent public transit. Importantly, the setting encourages a lot of outdoor activity, both in winter and summer, so if you enjoy nature, you’ll have plenty of options for hiking, skiing, boating, and exploring both urban and wild landscapes.

details.Restrictions: You can only choose courses within your study field, at the department or faculty specified in the exchange agreement. Therefore, it is not possible to mix courses from different fields of study or degree programs, nor across different campuses. Bachelor students can only register for bachelor courses, but master students are allowed to register for both bachelor and master courses. You must fulfill the prerequisites for each course. Course levels: each module starts with 3 abbreviation letters (for example, KJE for chemistry, BIO for biology, PSY for psychology) and 4 numerical digits in the catalogues. The modules with the numerical digits 1000 - 2000 are for bachelor's degree students . The modules with the numerical digits 2000 - 300 are for master's students - it means you must have completed your bachelor's degree or 180 ECTS at your home university to be able to choose these modules. Enrollment at UiT offers the possibility to study at University Center in Svalbard (UNIS) (http://www.unis.no/) – however, you will need to apply to both UiT, AND you must apply directly to UNIS. You must follow both application procedures in detail and both UiT and UNIS require that you attach certified copies of official transcripts to document your grades and student status. UiT as a back-up plan: If you are interested in studying at UNIS, you should be aware that UNIS usually has more applicants than places for exchange students and every semester there are students who are not offered admission. It is therefore recommended that you consider applying for courses at UiT as well as UNIS. That way you will have the option to attend UiT as a second choice if your application is rejected at UNIS.

details.Partner institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
details.Description: UiT is a large, multi-campus university in Northern Norway, with around 17,000 students, globally recognised as a leading centre for Arctic research. It offers a broad spectrum of programmes across its eight faculties covering most disciplines. While Norwegian is the main language of instruction, many courses especially at the master’s level are taught in English. The city of Tromsø is often described as really special: you’re surrounded by dramatic Arctic scenery, with fjords, mountains, and islands all nearby, and you get phenomena like the Midnight Sun in summer and Northern Lights in winter. Tromsø is reasonably walkable, especially in the city centre with decent public transit. Importantly, the setting encourages a lot of outdoor activity, both in winter and summer, so if you enjoy nature, you’ll have plenty of options for hiking, skiing, boating, and exploring both urban and wild landscapes.

These courses are only reserved for students admitted to the NOMPEL programme.

details.Description: The Umeå University is one of Sweden’s leading comprehensive universities, with over 40 000 students enrolled. It offers a large number of programmes and courses taught in English, making it an attractive option for exchange students. The university is known for its strong research and for fostering an open and collaborative academic environment. The city of Umeå provides a friendly and accessible setting for student life, with a compact and walkable central area where cafés, shops and cultural venues are easily reachable from campus. details.Description: The Universidad de Extremadura (UEx), founded in 1973, is a public university serving the autonomous community of Extremadura in western Spain. It has a student population of over 20,000 and operates across four campuses located in Badajoz, Cáceres, Mérida, and Plasencia. UEx offers a wide range of academic disciplines and is known for its commitment to regional development through education, research, and innovation. The university maintains strong ties with local institutions and industries, and its facilities include libraries, laboratories, research centers, and sports complexes. Its structure and mission reflect a focus on accessibility, community engagement, and practical learning. Extremadura offers a distinctive setting for student life, with a mix of historical towns, natural landscapes, and cultural traditions. The region is less crowded than other parts of Spain, making it ideal for students seeking a quieter and more immersive experience. Public transport connects the university campuses with surrounding cities and countryside, and students can explore UNESCO World Heritage sites, Roman ruins, and medieval architecture. A fun fact: Extremadura is the birthplace of many Spanish conquistadors, and cities like Medellín and Trujillo in Latin America are named after towns in the region. This historical legacy adds a unique dimension to studying in Extremadura.

details.Description: The University of La Laguna, founded in 1792, is the oldest university in the Canary Islands and one of the most established in Spain. It serves a student population of around 20,000 and offers a broad range of academic disciplines across its faculties. The university is recognized for its commitment to research, particularly in areas related to marine sciences, astrophysics, and regional development. It maintains strong connections with local and international research networks and emphasizes practical learning and community engagement. The campus environment combines historic buildings with modern facilities, supporting both academic and extracurricular activities. Located in San Cristóbal de La Laguna on the island of Tenerife, the university offers students a unique setting that blends historical heritage with a subtropical climate. The city is a UNESCO World Heritage site, known for its colonial architecture and vibrant student life. Public transport connects the campus with nearby beaches, mountains, and the island’s capital, Santa Cruz. A fun fact: Tenerife is home to Mount Teide, the highest peak in Spain and one of the world’s largest volcanoes, offering students opportunities for outdoor exploration alongside their studies.

details.Description: The Universidad de Salamanca, founded in 1218, is the oldest university in Spain and one of the oldest in Europe. It serves a student population of around 30,000 and offers a comprehensive range of academic disciplines across its faculties. The university is renowned for its historical significance, academic excellence, and contributions to Spanish language and culture. It maintains a strong research profile and international presence, attracting students and scholars from around the world. The campus features a blend of historic architecture and modern facilities, providing a unique academic environment. Salamanca is a vibrant university city in western Spain, known for its well-preserved medieval center and lively student atmosphere. The city is compact and walkable, with efficient public transport and a wide range of cultural events, cafés, and festivals. Students can explore historic landmarks, including the famous Plaza Mayor and the university’s ornate façade. A fun fact: Salamanca’s university is home to the “frog on the skull” carving, a symbol of good luck for students who find it on the university’s façade—a tradition that continues to attract visitors and students alike.

details.Description: The Universidade Católica Portuguesa (UCP), established in 1967, is a prominent private university in Portugal with a strong academic and research profile. It operates across four campuses—Lisbon, Porto, Braga, and Viseu—and hosts over 20,000 students, including more than 3,800 international students from 110 nationalities. UCP employs over 1,100 faculty members and maintains 15 research units with nearly 1,500 researchers. The university is known for its interdisciplinary research, international partnerships, and commitment to social responsibility. A distinctive feature of UCP is its status as a concordat university, meaning it operates under a special agreement with the Vatican, which sets it apart from most other institutions in Portugal. Lisbon, where UCP’s headquarters are located, offers a rich cultural and historical setting for students. The city combines centuries-old architecture with a vibrant modern lifestyle, and is well-connected by public transport, including its iconic yellow trams. Students can enjoy a wide range of cultural activities, from museums and music festivals to traditional Portuguese cuisine. A fun fact: Lisbon’s classic trams are actually based on American streetcars from the early 20th century and were once referred to locally as “Americanos”. This blend of global influences and local traditions makes Lisbon a compelling destination for students seeking both academic and cultural enrichment.

After the application process at UCPH, you can therefore apply for a language confirmation from the Faculty of Law in Copenhagen. The language confirmation will be based on your grades in English from your Danish ‘studentereksamen’ or ‘HF’ diploma. Language requirements for courses taught in portuguese You can also take courses in Portuguese and it is recommended that you have language qualifications corresponding to minimum A2 in Portuguese, cf. on the CEFR-grid (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) .

details.Course information: Generally, the law courses or seminars have low ECTS-values of 3 or 4 ECTS requiring approximately eight (8) law courses in total to reach 30 ECTS per semester. Teaching style at Universidade Católica Portuguesa has a tendency to focus on active student participation via handouts, group discussions and oral presentations. Generally you may expect less reading material for classes compared to UCPH. Class presence is mandatory and students must attend at least 2/3 of the classes, otherwise it will be considered as a fail; be also aware that the level of participation may count towards the final grade in some classes. There are different kinds of exams like take-home exams, essays etc. and also written exams of 2-hours duration written by hand. The majority of law courses taught in English are offered at bachelor level. As a bachelor exchange student you must have completed at least 2 years of law studies at University level in order to attend undergraduate level courses at Universidade Catolica Portuguesa. details.Description: The Universidade de Lisboa (ULisboa), established in its current form in 2013 through the merger of two major institutions, is the largest university in Portugal. It hosts over 50,000 students and comprises 18 schools covering a wide range of disciplines. ULisboa is recognized for its commitment to interdisciplinary research and innovation, with strong international collaborations and a focus on addressing global challenges. Its research agenda is closely aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, and the university actively promotes knowledge transfer and societal impact through partnerships with public and private sectors. Located in the heart of Lisbon, ULisboa offers students access to a city rich in history, culture, and modern amenities. Lisbon is one of Europe’s oldest continuously inhabited cities, with a legacy that includes Roman galleries, Moorish architecture, and earthquake-resistant urban planning dating back to the 18th century. The city is known for its iconic yellow trams, vibrant neighborhoods, and a growing reputation as a hub for startups and digital innovation. A fun fact: Lisbon’s classic trams are modeled after American streetcars from Harlem and New Orleans, and were once locally referred to as “Americanos”.  This blend of tradition and modernity makes Lisbon a compelling destination for students seeking both academic and cultural enrichment.

details.Description:
The Federal University of Rio de Janeiro – UFRJ has three campi: Cidade
Universitária, Praia Vermellha and Macaé, comprising institutes, schools,
faculties and supplementary units, which include seven museums, among
which we can highlight the National Museum, eight university hospitals,
and the third largest ocean basin in the world for research on offshore oil
exploration. The university has partnerships with several national and multinational
enterprises, some of which have facilities on the very UFRJ campi. It is the
case of Petrobras, whose biggest research center is located on Cidade
Universitária campus. Following a global trend, the UFRJ establishes and
maintains cooperative relationships with institutions from all continents,
which now amounts to over 200 international institutions all over the
world.

This must be documented on their transcript by the time of applying to the host university. First-year master's students are considered to meet this requirement based on their completed bachelor's degree.

details.Description: Universidade NOVA de Lisboa, founded in 1973, is a dynamic public university recognized for its innovative spirit and strong international profile. NOVA has grown into one of Portugal’s leading institutions, with around 20,000 students enrolled across nine academic units that cover disciplines ranging from social sciences, humanities, law, and business to science, technology, medicine, and public health. Its schools and faculties consistently rank among the best in Portugal and Europe, known for combining high-quality teaching with research that addresses contemporary challenges. NOVA’s commitment to creating and sharing scientific, cultural, and artistic knowledge, along with training that is deeply anchored in research, reflects its mission to contribute actively to the social and economic development of the communities it serves. Studying in Lisbon offers students the chance to live in a vibrant European capital known for its mild climate, historical neighborhoods, and rich cultural life. NOVA’s various campuses are well integrated into the city, providing modern facilities and fostering an environment that encourages collaboration, creativity, and global perspectives. With Lisbon’s welcoming atmosphere and excellent quality of life, students at NOVA enjoy both rigorous academic experiences and the benefits of living in a lively, cosmopolitan setting.

details.Description: The Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB), established in 1968, is a leading public university in Spain known for its strong research orientation and international outlook. It serves a student population of over 35,000 and offers a wide range of academic disciplines across its faculties. UAB is recognized for its interdisciplinary approach, innovative teaching methods, and close collaboration with research institutes and industry partners. The university’s main campus is designed as a self-contained academic community, providing students with access to modern facilities, libraries, and support services in a single location. Located just outside Barcelona, UAB offers students the advantages of a campus environment while being close to one of Europe’s most dynamic cities. Barcelona is known for its rich cultural life, Mediterranean climate, and excellent public transport, making it easy for students to commute between the campus and the city. The region offers a mix of historic sites, beaches, and vibrant neighborhoods, providing a diverse and stimulating setting for student life.

details.Description: The University of Hamburg is one of Germany’s largest and most diverse universities, with around 43,000 students and over 5,000 academic staff. It is a leading institution in northern Germany for both research and teaching, and is part of the German Excellence Strategy. The university is known for its strong interdisciplinary approach and its commitment to sustainability and social responsibility. With more than 180 degree programs and a wide range of research centers, it offers students access to a broad academic environment. A defining feature of the University of Hamburg is its close integration with major research institutions in the region, including several Max Planck and Helmholtz institutes. Situated in Germany’s second-largest city, the University of Hamburg offers students the chance to live in a vibrant, international urban setting. Hamburg is a major port city with a strong cultural scene, a dynamic economy, and a high standard of living. Its many parks, waterways, and neighborhoods provide a varied and accessible environment for student life. The city is well-connected by public transport and offers a wide range of activities outside the classroom, from music and art to sports and volunteering. For students looking to combine academic development with urban exploration, Hamburg presents a compelling option.

details.Description: Université Côte d’Azur is a public research university located in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur region of southern France. It brings together over 18,000 students and more than 2,000 academic and administrative staff across multiple campuses and research centres. The university is part of the European University Alliance Ulysseus and has been recognized as an Initiative of Excellence (IDEX) by the French government, highlighting its commitment to high-level research and innovation. Its structure integrates several academic institutions and research bodies, fostering collaboration across disciplines and supporting a strong international orientation. The university is based in Nice and the surrounding area, offering students access to both urban and coastal environments. Nice is a mid-sized city on the Mediterranean coast, known for its cultural heritage, public transport infrastructure, and proximity to Italy and Monaco. The region combines academic resources with a high quality of life, including access to museums, libraries, and outdoor activities. For students seeking a well-connected and diverse setting for their exchange semester, Université Côte d’Azur offers a practical and engaging environment in one of France’s most internationally oriented regions.

details.Description: Université de Neuchâtel is a public university in western Switzerland with a student body of approximately 4,000 and a staff of around 1,200. It offers a compact academic environment with four faculties and a strong emphasis on research, particularly in law, economics, and natural sciences. The university is known for its bilingual setting (French and English), which supports international collaboration and mobility. Its manageable size allows for close interaction between students and faculty, and its location in the French-speaking part of Switzerland provides access to cross-border academic networks. The university is located in the city of Neuchâtel, situated on the shores of Lake Neuchâtel and surrounded by the Jura mountains. The city is known for its watchmaking heritage and offers a mix of historical architecture and natural landscapes. Neuchâtel is walkable, well-connected by rail, and offers a calm setting for study with access to outdoor activities year-round. A small curiosity: the lake next to the city is the largest entirely within Swiss borders, and its water is so clear that it’s used as a benchmark for measuring lake transparency across Europe.

details.Description: Université Libre de Bruxelles was founded in 1834 and offers education in all disciplines at all levels. It has 11 faculties and 30,000 students where around 30% are foreign students. ‘The Université libre de Bruxelles bases its teachings and research on the principle of free inquiry. details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student, you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad.
details.Course information: At Université Libre de Bruxelles, all courses are worth 5 or 10 ECTS. Catalogue of courses: BA courses (https://www.ulb.be/fr/programme/ba-droi#programme) and MA courses (https://www.ulb.be/fr/programme/ma-droi)) At the first class of all your courses, you must ask the professor individually for permission to follow his or her course. Generally, the majority of professors want international students in their course, but a few may turn you down. Within the first 2-3 weeks, you have, however, the opportunity to try out courses before finally choosing which ones you wish to follow. The majority of courses are taught as lectures, and in most classes oral participation at lectures count towards your final grade. You can also choose to follow "Travaux Pratiques" (TP) in most courses, which are similar to seminar classes in Denmark. These are optional (for most courses), and an opportunity to go more in depth with the syllabus You can look for additional information in travel reports in KUnet (https://kunet.ku.dk/studie/sider/RedirectToTopic.aspx?topicId=6c9c7e02-d3bb-4735-8e65-33a2cfb91209) and in Reports in Mobility online from Université Libre de Bruxelles.

details.Description: Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne is one of France’s leading public universities, with a strong academic tradition rooted in the historic Sorbonne. It serves over 40,000 students and employs more than 1,400 academic and administrative staff. The university is known for its focus on humanities, social sciences, law, and economics, and maintains active research centres across these fields. It plays a central role in French academic life and contributes to international research networks. Its structure supports a broad academic offering while maintaining close links to national institutions and cultural organisations, making it a distinctive institution within the French higher education system. The university is located in central Paris, with sites spread across several historic buildings in the Latin Quarter and other parts of the city. This location places students in direct contact with the intellectual and cultural life of the capital, with access to libraries, archives, museums, and public institutions. Paris offers a wide range of academic and cultural resources, as well as efficient transport connections to other regions and countries. For students considering an exchange semester, Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne provides an opportunity to study in a city closely tied to European academic and cultural history.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Courses are mostly taught in French. Students are expected to proove a language level of B2 (see info in the self-assessment CEFR-grid (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) ) in the language of instruction. After the application process at UCPH, you must prove your language skills by a language certificate or a letter from a French language teacher or a language test like DELF / DALF , TCF . In general, visiting French universities requires a high level of French. Some courses may be offered in English, but often the lectures are conducted in French even if the language of instruction is suppposed to be in English.
details.Course information: Students can find courses/modules open to exchange students in their host department/study area. See the course/module catalogue (https://international.pantheonsorbonne.fr/en/join-paris-1-pantheon-sorbonne/exchange-student/module-catalogue) . See additional info on course/module offers (https://welcome.pantheonsorbonne.fr/en/apply-and-study) In each department, an academic advisor is in charge of helping incoming exchange students with any questions related to courses. Lectures take place in lecture theatres, often called “amphis”, sometimes with as many as 1,000 students present. Seminars and Practicals Seminars (TD) and practical exercises (TP) are small-group classes that take place in classrooms or laboratories, exploring lecture topics in greater depth.

details.Description: Considered as France's first Law University, Université Paris II Panthéon-Assas is dedicated to upholding the tradition from which it arose, preserving, yet ever-striving to raise its level of excellence in the following fields of study and research: Private Law and Criminal Science, Public Law, Political Science, Roman Law, History of Law, Economics, Management, Information and Communication Sciences. Attentive to students' needs, the university provides various numerical services, tutorials, an ever-growing and comprehensive library database, course and professional counselling services, and a selection of extracurricular athletic and cultural activities all acting in concert to complete and harmonize each student's university experience. The University headquarters are situated in Paris, 5th district, at Place du Panthéon. The majority of law courses will take place at the Centre Assas, a campus in the heart of Paris, next to the Jardin du Luxembourg.

details.Academic calendar:
Fall semester: End of September to December. Exams January to February. Winter semester: End of January to May.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: As an exchange student at Panthéon-Assas you are expected to have language qualifications in French at minimum level B2 in the self-assessment CEFR-grid (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) . Generally, language expectations are high for law exchange students at this university – especially at the final exams. Therefore, if your French language qualifications origin exclusively from your Danish ‘Studentereksamen’ or ‘HF’ degree, UCPH would strongly recommend that you try to improve your language skills before you start on the exchange programme. No official language documentation is, however, required. The majority of law courses are taught in French. In addition, a few law courses are taught in English - see additional info below at 'Restrictions' and ‘course information’).
details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. Be aware that you will probably not be able to choose sufficient law courses which are taught in English; despite promising information on the homepage of Panthéon-Assas. The courses offered in English are often a mixture of law and social science courses; the latter may not always be pre-approved at UCPH. Therefore, your language level in French must be sufficiently high enabling you to take law courses taught in French.
details.Course information: You can choose all courses from 1st to 3rd year at the Licence programme equivalent to bachelor level and 4th year courses at Master 1. The majority of courses are offered as lectures called ‘cours magistraux’ (CM) and generally they have a duration of three (3) hours. Educational material such as text books are not used at lectures, instead students must take notes from the lecturers' presentations and use these when preparing for the final exams. In addition to ordinary lectures (CM), you can take two classes called ‘Travaux Dirigés’ (TD). In TD classes education with be interactive with presentations, assignments, group work etc. – an educational style familiar to the teaching methods in Copenhagen. Be aware of a very high workload in these classes. Some courses in law and political science are taught in English. The majority of these courses are taught on 1st or 2nd year at bachelor level. Generally, UCHP recommends that you choose courses preferably from 3rd year law studies and onwards, which require a sufficient language level in French, jf. info at 'Restrictions' above.

details.Description: University College Cork (UCC) is one of Ireland’s leading universities, known for its strong academic reputation and commitment to research and innovation. It serves a diverse student body of over 24,000 and offers a wide range of disciplines across its faculties. UCC places a strong emphasis on sustainability, international collaboration, and student-centered learning. The university integrates research with teaching and encourages students to engage with real-world challenges through interdisciplinary approaches and community partnerships. Its campus combines historic architecture with modern facilities, creating a balanced environment for academic and personal development. Cork, located in the south of Ireland, is a lively and welcoming city with a rich cultural heritage and a strong student presence. The city is compact and easy to navigate, with good public transport and a wide range of cafés, music venues, and cultural events. Students can explore nearby coastal areas, historic sites, and scenic countryside, all within easy reach. A fun fact: Cork is home to one of the world’s largest natural harbours and also produces a significant share of the world’s Tic Tacs.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: Early/mid-Sep. to the end of Nov. Exams in December. Winter semester: Mid-Jan. to mid/late April. Exams in late April to early/mid May. See additional information on Key semester dates (https://www.ucc.ie/en/student-records/key-dates/) All students are expected to attend an introductory orientation programme which is held at the beginning of each semester.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: A good knowledge of English is essential in order to be able to understand lectures, text books and to work with the English language sufficiently well. UCC does not require students to provide English language certificates.
details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. In the course descriptions in the UCC Book of Modules below, you can see that credit values of courses in Ireland correspond to ECTS values in Europe, i.e. 5 credits in Cork equals 5 ECTS in Denmark. Courses are called modules in Ireland. Info on module numbers: The first two characters in a module indicate the subject area of the module e.g. LW1104 where LW indicates it is a law module. The third character indicates the year or level (in this case a First Year or Level One module), and the remaining three characters 112 identify the particular module within the subject area. The teaching style at University College Cork is characterized by a great deal of lectures and some classroom education. Generally in lectures, there may be little room for discussions or questions. Therefore, if you have any preferences, check out the type of education in advance. Since Ireland is a common law country, doctrines and principles may be different in specific areas, however, with some similarities to the Danish equivalents. The teaching at UCC may be more focused on learning why the law is as it is, how the law works and critically assessing this. Compared to UCPH with case-based education with focus on learning how to apply the law.

details.Description: University College Dublin, founded in 1854, is Ireland’s largest university and one of Europe’s leading research-intensive institutions. With over 39,000 students, including a vibrant international community, UCD offers a broad academic portfolio across six colleges in disciplines such as business, social sciences, law, science, engineering, medicine, agriculture, and the humanities. The university places strong emphasis on academic excellence, interdisciplinary learning, and real-world application of knowledge. Courses are taught by leading researchers, and exchange students are welcomed into a dynamic and inclusive academic environment. UCD’s modern campus provides state-of-the-art facilities, world-class libraries, and numerous research centres that support an active and engaged learning experience. Located just south of Dublin city centre, UCD’s Belfield campus combines the convenience of urban living with the calm of a self-contained, green setting. Dublin is a lively and welcoming capital known for its cultural richness, literary history, and friendly atmosphere. Exchange students at UCD benefit not only from a high-quality education but also from easy access to music, theatre, museums, cafés, and nature. The city’s excellent public transport and international connectivity make it a great base for travel and exploration. Living and studying in Dublin offers a well-balanced student experience that blends academic challenge with social and cultural discovery.

With over 39,000 students, including a vibrant international community, UCD offers a broad academic portfolio across six colleges in disciplines such as business, social sciences, law, science, engineering, medicine, agriculture, and the humanities. The university places strong emphasis on academic excellence, interdisciplinary learning, and real-world application of knowledge. Courses are taught by leading researchers, and exchange students are welcomed into a dynamic and inclusive academic environment. UCD’s modern campus provides state-of-the-art facilities, world-class libraries, and numerous research centres that support an active and engaged learning experience. Located just south of Dublin city centre, UCD’s Belfield campus combines the convenience of urban living with the calm of a self-contained, green setting. Dublin is a lively and welcoming capital known for its cultural richness, literary history, and friendly atmosphere. Exchange students at UCD benefit not only from a high-quality education but also from easy access to music, theatre, museums, cafés, and nature. The city’s excellent public transport and international connectivity make it a great base for travel and exploration. Living and studying in Dublin offers a well-balanced student experience that blends academic challenge with social and cultural discovery.

details.Restrictions: You can only take courses within the College of Science, which gives you a choice across several schools. Most credits should be in the your subject area, for example 20 credits out of 30. Level 1 to 3 are undergraduate modules and level 4 are postgraduate modules. Modules with “SCI”, “NUin” or “Conversion” (“Conv”) in their title are not available to exchange students. In some Schools, certain level 4 modules may be open to undergraduate and exchange students and in some they are not. In case of doubt, email incoming.erasmus@ucd.ie There are also courses recommended for exchange students, which are open to students from any discipline. You MUST arrive in UCD in time for the start of classes. Those who do not do so may have their admission cancelled by UCD.

details.Description: The University of A Coruña, established in 1989, is a public institution located in the region of Galicia in northwestern Spain. It serves a student population of around 20,000 and offers a wide range of academic disciplines across its faculties. The university is recognized for its commitment to research, particularly in fields such as engineering, environmental sciences, and social sciences. It maintains strong connections with local industries and international partners, emphasizing practical learning and innovation. The campus environment combines modern facilities with access to research centers and student support services. A Coruña is a coastal city known for its maritime heritage, lively atmosphere, and student-friendly environment. The city offers efficient public transport, a walkable center, and easy access to beaches and green spaces. Students can enjoy a variety of cultural events, local cuisine, and historic landmarks such as the Tower of Hercules, a Roman lighthouse and UNESCO World Heritage site. A fun fact: The Tower of Hercules is the oldest working lighthouse in the world, and its image is featured on the city’s coat of arms.

details.Description: Established in 1874, the University of Adelaide is Australia's third oldest university. Adelaide has over 27,000 registered students, around 9,000 of whom are international. By every measure, the University of Adelaide—a member of Australia’s prestigious Group of Eight research-intensive universities—stands tall among the world’s leading institutions of learning and innovation. Considered one of the top 1% of Universities worldwide, we count among our distinguished alumni: five Nobel Laureates; over 100 Rhodes Scholars, including Australia’s first Indigenous recipient; and Australia’s first female prime minister and Supreme Court judge. We occupy a unique position among Australian cities, Adelaide is friendly and offers a real sense of community. Its size and sense of comfort means it provides an atmosphere conducive to study. You want beaches? Festivals? Proximity to beautiful Australian nature and the Outback? Adelaide has all of this - and more! (https://youtu.be/GtH4z-7ixPI?si=5nualIZV-_KPhLbX)

details.Description: The University of Agder is a modern, dynamic university in southern Norway with about 14,000 students, spread mainly over two campuses in Kristiansand and Grimstad. While many of the undergraduate courses are taught in Norwegian, there is a solid selection of Master’s‐level and exchange courses in English. The Grimstad campus is especially noted for its engineering, technology, and applied sciences orientation, with modern facilities, while Kristiansand is larger, more central, and offers greater diversity in programme choice. The cities where UiA is based Kristiansand and Grimstad combine the charms of Southern Norway’s coastal landscape with good student amenities and fairly easy living. Kristiansand is the larger city, with a compact centre, decent public transit, green areas, and recreational options close by: forests, beaches, hiking, and water sports. Many services, cafés, shops, and cultural venues are within walking distance if you live in or near the city centre or close to campus, which makes day-to-day life convenient. Grimstad is smaller and the distance from campus to town is short.

details.Description: Akureyri, a city with significant influence on the development of Northern Iceland, has emerged as a vibrant center of learning. Despite its remote location, trade and export, particularly of seafood products, have facilitated connections with the outside world. With a population of around 17,000, Akureyri is the largest community outside the Reykjavik area. The establishment of the University of Akureyri in 1987 solidified the city's reputation as an educational hub. The University of Akureyri, home to approximately 2,000 students, boasts two campuses. Alongside academic facilities, the university campus offers a cafeteria, a wellness and exercise center, and a 24/7 accessible library. Embrace the enriching educational opportunities and the lively atmosphere of Akureyri as you embark on your academic journey at the University of Akureyri. .

details.Description: The University of Almería, established in 1993, is a public university located on Spain’s southeastern Mediterranean coast. It serves around 13,000 students and offers a broad range of academic disciplines, with particular strengths in agricultural sciences, environmental studies, and biotechnology. The university is recognized for its research and innovation in sustainable agriculture and greenhouse technology, reflecting the region’s economic focus. Its modern campus provides students with advanced facilities, research centers, and a supportive academic environment. Almería is a coastal city known for its sunny climate, beaches, and distinctive desert landscapes. The city offers a relaxed, student-friendly atmosphere, efficient public transport, and easy access to both the Mediterranean Sea and nearby natural parks. Students can enjoy cultural events, outdoor activities, and local cuisine. A fun fact: Almería’s Tabernas Desert is the only true desert in mainland Europe and has served as the filming location for numerous classic Western movies.

details.Description: The University of Amsterdam (UvA) is one of Europe’s top research universities, known for its academic excellence, broad disciplinary offerings, and strong international orientation. Founded in 1632, UvA offers a wide range of programs across seven faculties, including humanities, social and behavioral sciences, economics and business, law, and science. With over 40,000 students, including a large international cohort, the university fosters a vibrant and diverse academic community. UvA is particularly recognized for its research-led teaching, interdisciplinary collaboration, and commitment to addressing global challenges through innovative scholarship. Located in the heart of Amsterdam, the university offers students the opportunity to study in one of the most culturally rich and globally connected cities in Europe. Amsterdam is known for its historic canals, world-class museums, and dynamic urban life. The city’s compact layout, excellent public transport, and welcoming atmosphere make it ideal for student living. Whether exploring the city’s artistic heritage, engaging in public debates, or enjoying its lively cafés and green spaces, exchange students at UvA will find themselves in an inspiring environment that supports both academic growth and personal discovery.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: See info on English Language test requirements (https://www.uva.nl/en/programmes/exchange/law/application-and-admission/application-and-admission.html?origin=cQrBgcZsRZO%2F6Pm0Q%2F1d8w#Course-registration) . For courses at bachelor level, Amsterdam requires that your English language qualifications correspond to B2 on the CEFR-list (https://europass.cedefop.europa.eu/resources/european-language-levels-cefr) . After the application process at UCPH you can retrieve a language confirmation at level B2 in English from Mobility Online. The selection of bachelor law courses taught in English can some times be limited. Therefore, bachelor law students can also obtain access to master level courses but be aware that English at level C1 will be required by a language test result or by the excemption stated below. For courses at master level, Amsterdam requires that your English qualifications correspond to C1 on the CEFR-list (https://europass.cedefop.europa.eu/resources/european-language-levels-cefr) . Danish students can be exempted from the language test requirements if you have studied English at level “A” and achieved a passing grade at your exam for the Danish ‘studentereksamen’. With documentation of the above-mentioned criterium, you can contact International Education in Copenhagen and ask for a language confirmation (please state that language level C1 is required). NB: the request for a statement of English C1 proficiency will soon be integrated to Mobility Online.
details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. Exchange Students must have completed at least 120 ECTS before their semester at the Amsterdam Law School.
details.Course information: Find links to bachelor and master courses for exchange students (https://coursecatalogue.uva.nl/xmlpages/page/2024-2025-en/search-programme/programme/8095) The different law programmes in Amsterdam: The Faculty offers three bachelors programmes (two specialised and one general) and approx. 18 masters (LLM) programmes. You may freely choose between LLB courses and LLM courses, but be aware that the majority of courses taught in English are offered at master level. The teaching style at UvA may seem a bit different compared to UCPH with greater expectations on regular attendance and active interaction between teachers and students. Expect a high workload of reading material for each course with weekly assignments which may count towards the final grade. As the semester is divided into two or three blocks, the courses are short and intensive. Master-courses being part of a Master study-programme can be extra challenging. See additional info in Reports (https://kunet.ku.dk/studie/sider/RedirectToTopic.aspx?topicId=6c9c7e02-d3bb-4735-8e65-33a2cfb91209) from UCPH students who previously went on student exchange to Amsterdam.

details.Housing: To make the allocation of housing as fair as possible for all students, we work with a lottery system. Applications from non-EU students will be treated with priority on the condition that the student has met the deadline (though subject to availability). There is a small time window for each semester in which students can apply for housing. All applicants will be assigned a random place on the waiting list. For more information, take a look at the Housing page (https://www.uva.nl/en/education/practical-information/housing/housing.html) . NB: The university of Amsterdam cannot guarantee exchange students with housing so please look for housing on the private market at your earliest convenience.

An exchange in the 1st semester is a better option for MSc exchange students.

details.Restrictions: Exchange students nominated to the Faculty of Science are expected to take their courses at the Faculty of Science. Exchange students can apply for a maximum of two courses at another department or faculty. Please note that placement at other departments is difficult and cannot be guaranteed. BSc-students are not allowed to follow master courses. It is therefore recommended that you follow one of the Minors offered at the Faculty of Science (https://coursecatalogue.uva.nl/xmlpages/page/2024-2025-en/search-course) . These are pre-packaged selections of related courses that fulfill the 30 ECTS requirement. There are fewer English taught courses offered in semester 2. If there is not a full semester load of courses offered in your own study field, you can choose additional Interdisciplinary courses or courses in Scientific Programming, both at bachelor level. Erasmus students who want to take courses at the UvA have to be in Amsterdam when the courses start. You will not be allowed to take a course if you have missed the first class(es).

details.Description: The University of Antwerp (Dutch: Universiteit Antwerpen) is a major Belgian university located in the city of Antwerp. It was founded in 2003 after the merger of three smaller universities. The University of Antwerp has about 20,000 students, which makes it the third largest university in Flanders. The six campuses are located all over the city of Antwerp, from the historic city center to the green belt to the south of the city. The language of instruction in Flanders is Dutch. Hence the university offers courses in Dutch, but all faculties also offer courses in English.

details.Description: The University of Antwerp (Dutch: Universiteit Antwerpen) is a major Belgian university located in the city of Antwerp. It was founded in 2003 after the merger of three smaller universities. The University of Antwerp has about 20,000 students, which makes it the third largest university in Flanders. The six campuses are located all over the city of Antwerp, from the historic city center to the green belt to the south of the city. The language of instruction in Flanders is Dutch. Hence the university offers courses in Dutch, but all faculties also offer courses in English.

details.Description: Founded in 1883, Auckland is the country’s largest university with over 40,000 students, nearly 10,000 of whom graduate annually. The main campus is in the heart of Auckland city and we have four specialist campuses. The University of Auckland is New Zealand’s world-ranked university. The University of Auckland is the only New Zealand university ranked in the top 200 in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings, in the top 100 in the QS World University Rankings, and with the maximum rating of Five Stars Plus in the QS Stars University Ratings. The University is also the highest ranked New Zealand university in the Shanghai Jiao Tong Academic Ranking of World Universities. Auckland’s harbour setting, magnificent beaches and verdant bush make it a great place to study and work, while the University’s close proximity to New Zealand’s major business city enables staff and students to rub shoulders with leading practitioners in their field. For example, medical students work alongside leading specialists at Auckland City Hospital while the Faculty of Law is within walking distance of the courts and major legal firms. The Business School has a close relationship with leading Auckland companies and academics from our Faculty of Engineering, School of Population Health and School of Architecture and Planning serve on think-tanks helping to shape the city’s future. Discover more about living in Auckland (https://www.auckland.ac.nz/en/on-campus/life-on-campus/living-in-auckland.html)

details.Study load for undergraduate students: 60 points = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Study load for graduate students: 60 points = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Conversion and levels: Study load is calculated according to the level of the specific course. details.Description: The University of Barcelona, founded in 1450, is one of Spain’s largest and most prestigious public universities. It serves a student population of over 60,000 and offers a comprehensive range of academic disciplines across its faculties. The university is recognized for its strong research output, international collaborations, and commitment to academic excellence. Its campuses are integrated into the city, combining historic buildings with modern facilities and providing students with access to extensive libraries, research centers, and support services. Barcelona offers a dynamic setting for student life, with a Mediterranean climate, rich cultural heritage, and efficient public transport. The city is known for its architecture, beaches, and vibrant neighborhoods, making it easy for students to balance academic pursuits with leisure and cultural activities. A fun fact: Barcelona’s main campus is located near the Eixample district, famous for its grid layout and iconic works by architect Antoni Gaudí, including the Sagrada Família and Casa Batlló.

details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . As a result, students applying for exchange places in the UK cannot be guaranteed an Erasmus+ grant at the time of application. Eligibility for Erasmus+ funding will depend on whether the host university joins the programme and concludes an Erasmus+ agreement with the University of Copenhagen. Students nominated to a UK university will be informed of their grant eligibility no later than March 2027. You can apply for the SUND Outgoing Mobility grant, if you have not received UCPH Internationalisation Scholarship.

details.Description: After the decision for its founding in 1972, the University of Bayreuth began teaching and studying in 1975. The University of Bayreuth has about 13,300 students and 1,650 academic staff (260 of them professors) on the campus in Bayreuth and at satellite campus in Kulmbach. This makes it one of the largest employers in the region. The university is located in Bayreuth, an 800-year-old city in the north of Bavaria, home to 73,000 residents

details.Description: The University of Bergamo, founded in 1968, is a public university known for its strong connection to the local territory and close collaboration with businesses and institutions. The university offers a diverse range of academic programs across its seven departments, including Economics, Engineering, Foreign Languages, Humanities, Law, Education, and Human and Social Sciences. Exchange students have the opportunity to attend courses taught in both Italian and English, particularly in areas like business, economics, engineering, and languages. The university promotes an interdisciplinary approach, blending theoretical study with practical experiences through workshops, research projects, and partnerships with local industries. Bergamo itself is a charming city in northern Italy, located at the foothills of the Alps and just a short distance from Milan. The city’s rich medieval heritage, vibrant cultural scene, and compact size make it an ideal setting for international students seeking an immersive and accessible study abroad experience. Students can enjoy a lively atmosphere with festivals, concerts, and university events, while also having easy access to nature, mountain activities, and major urban hubs in the Lombardy region.

details.Description: The University of Bergen is a public research university located on Norway’s west coast. Established in 1946, it is one of the country’s leading academic institutions, serving around 20,000 students across six faculties. The university offers a wide range of study programmes and is known for its strong focus on interdisciplinary research, particularly in marine sciences, climate studies, and global health. Bergen, Norway’s second-largest city, offers a unique setting for student life, surrounded by mountains and fjords, making it an ideal place for students who enjoy outdoor activities alongside their studies. The city is compact and walkable, with reliable public transport. Bergen is also known for its rich cultural heritage, vibrant music scene, and historic waterfront district, Bryggen, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

details.Restrictions: The University of Bergen (UiB) offers two different categories of courses to international exchange students: Open courses: - May be taken across different faculties and departments. - Faculty approval is not required. - Previous knowledge may be required (check course requirements). - Registration must be done after admission have been granted (June/December). - May have limited capacity. Restricted courses: - Admission cannot be guaranteed. Faculty approval is required. - Previous knowledge and relevant academic background is required (check course requirements). - Limited capacity. - Qualified students nominated on an exchange agreement in the relevant subject area will be prioritized. You can take courses at more than one faculty, provided that you meet the required/recommended previous knowledge. The relevant faculty/department will consider whether you can be accepted to restricted courses during the application process, or if you can be granted admission later. UNIS – the University Centre in Svalbard If ou want to apply for courses at UNIS, you must apply for admission to both UNIS and UiB. You must follow both application procedures in detail and both UiB and UNIS require that you upload copies of official transcripts to document your grades and student status. UiB as a back-up plan: UNIS has limited enrollment capacity. We therefore recommend that you consider applying for courses at UiB as well as UNIS, that way you will have the option to come to UiB as a second choice. If you want UiB as your second choice, remember to choose both courses at UiB and the option UNIS in UiB's application form.

details.Additional information: The University of Bergen (UiB) is an internationally recognised research university. Academic diversity and high quality are fundamental for us. UiB is the most cited university in Norway. There are seven faculties at UiB and there are close to 18,500 students at the university, along with more than 4,000 faculty and staff. Around 2,000 international students study at UiB. The Department of Earth Science embodies research and research-based education – within central geological and geophysical disciplines, specifically marine geoscience, petroleum, climate and earthquake seismology. The research is conducted on land and sea all over the globe.

Bergen is also known for its rich cultural heritage, vibrant music scene, and historic waterfront district, Bryggen, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

details.Description: The University of Bern, founded in 1834, is one of Switzerland’s leading comprehensive universities, enrolling around 19,000 students across eight faculties and offering a wide spectrum of programs in the humanities, natural sciences, law, economics, medicine, and social sciences. With a strong focus on interdisciplinary research, sustainability, and global cooperation, the university ranks among the top 120–200 universities worldwide, depending on the field. It is particularly renowned for cutting-edge research in climate science, space, and health. Students benefit from close links to governmental institutions and international organizations located in Bern, providing unique opportunities for internships, networking, and real-world projects. Living in Bern as a student means enjoying all the advantages of Switzerland’s picturesque capital city. With its UNESCO-listed medieval Old Town, lively café culture, and riverside spots along the Aare for swimming or relaxing, Bern combines a laid-back atmosphere with rich cultural offerings. The university’s facilities are mostly concentrated in the welcoming Länggasse district, where student life thrives thanks to numerous associations, events, and support services like the Welcome Center and student union. Excellent public transport, bike-friendly streets, and proximity to the Alps make it easy to explore both the city and Switzerland’s stunning natural landscapes, offering an outstanding quality of life alongside your studies.

details.Additional information: At the Faculty of Theology of the University of Bern, students from diverse religious and ideological backgrounds form a scholarly opinion about aspects of Judaism, Christianity and other religions through dialogue with a range of confessions and religions. Teaching and research at Bern stands out with its strong emphasis on Old Catholic and Protestant Theology, Jewish Studies and Interreligious Studies. In addition, the modern and critical profile of our faculty supports strong practical training. On our website we offer information about BA and MA degrees in Old Catholic and Protestant Theology. details.Description: The University of Birmingham has been challenging and developing great minds for more than a century. Characterised by a tradition of innovation, research at the university has broken new ground, pushed forward the boundaries of knowledge and made an impact on people’s lives.   The university has been welcoming international students onto its campus since its inception in 1900 – and with over 5,000 international students from over 150 different countries, it has one of the largest and most vibrant international student communities in the UK.
details.Academic calendar: Semester 1 (autumn semester): September - December Semester 2 (spring semester): January - March Academic Year - University of Birmingham (https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/undergraduate/courses/academicyear.aspx)
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Statement from the home university that confirms that the student holds an English B2 level on the CEFR scale.
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 60 credits Please note: Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Study load for graduate students: 60 credits Please note: Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: Exchange students cannot enroll in courses offered through the College of Medical and Dental Sciences and Veterinary Medicine.
details.Important links: Website for incoming exchange (https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/international/study-abroad/study-abroad-incoming/index.aspx) Module lists (https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/international/study-abroad/study-abroad-incoming/study.aspx) Read about undergraduate courses here (https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/international/study-abroad/study-abroad-incoming/study.aspx) .
details.Housing: Housing is not guaranteed for students from inside Europe. Students are recommended to apply for on campus accommodation as early as possible. It’s worth considering that housing is easier to secure if you are staying for either the spring and summer term or the full academic year.
details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . As a result, students applying for exchange places in the UK cannot be guaranteed an Erasmus+ grant at the time of application. Eligibility for Erasmus+ funding will depend on whether the host university joins the programme and concludes an Erasmus+ agreement with the University of Copenhagen. Students nominated to a UK university will be informed of their grant eligibility no later than March 2027.
details.Additional information: It is important to keep in mind what campus you wish to have the majority of your courses. It is possible to choose between the following: College of Arts and Law College of Social Science College of Engineering and Physical Sciences College of Life and Environmental Sciences Students will study at least 40 out of 60 credits per semester in their preferred college and 60 credits per semester in their preferred college, if a second (optional) college is not chosen.

details.Description: The University of Bologna, founded in 1088, is widely recognized as the oldest university in the Western world and a prestigious center of academic excellence. With over 90,000 students and a strong international profile, the university offers a vast selection of courses across its 32 departments and five campuses. Exchange students can engage in diverse academic fields such as humanities, social sciences, economics, political science, law, engineering, and sciences. The university’s emphasis on interdisciplinary learning, research, and innovation provides students with rich academic experiences deeply rooted in tradition yet oriented towards the future. Bologna is a vibrant university city, known for its lively student atmosphere, rich cultural heritage, and welcoming environment. The historic city center, with its iconic medieval towers and extensive porticoed streets, offers a dynamic setting where academic life blends seamlessly with local culture, music, art, and cuisine. Its central location in Italy also makes it easy for students to explore other cities and regions, providing an ideal base for cultural and academic exploration.
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Academic calendar: A welcome day is held in the beginning of each semester. Fall semester: Mid-September to the beginning of December. Exam Session 1st semester: Early/Mid-January to mid-February Winter semester: Mid-February to mid-May. Exam Session 2nd semester: Late May to late July. Additional information is available in the academic calendar (https://corsi.unibo.it/magistralecu/Giurisprudenza-Bologna/calendario-didattico-a-a-2019-20) .
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: A language confirmation in English (or Italian) is required confirming that you have sufficient language qualifications corresponding to min. level B2 according to the European CEFR-standards (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) . Later on, you can download a Language Proficiency Documentation level B2 in the application portal Mobility Online under 'Before the Mobility'. A language confirmation will only be needed after you have been nominated to the exchange programme at the University of Bologna. Furthermore, knowledge of Italian language is not required for students studying in English.
details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. One Italian credit (CFU, Credito Formativo Universitario) equals one ECTS credit. Credits are obtained exclusively on passing an exam. The exchange programme is offered to both bachelor and master level law students. As an exchange student you are free to choose both bachelor and master level courses. Although only very few law courses on bachelor level are taught in English. The teaching style at University of Bologna will be different from what you are used to at UCPH as all courses are offered as lectures without any classroom education and without much room for active student participation. Less reading will be required, instead it will be important to attend and take notes during the lectures. Attendance may be mandatory in some of the courses.

details.Description: The University of Bologna, founded in 1088, is widely recognized as the oldest university in the Western world and a prestigious center of academic excellence. With over 90,000 students and a strong international profile, the university offers a vast selection of courses across its 32 departments and five campuses. Exchange students can engage in diverse academic fields such as humanities, social sciences, economics, political science, law, engineering, and sciences. The university’s emphasis on interdisciplinary learning, research, and innovation provides students with rich academic experiences deeply rooted in tradition yet oriented towards the future. Bologna is a vibrant university city, known for its lively student atmosphere, rich cultural heritage, and welcoming environment. The historic city center, with its iconic medieval towers and extensive porticoed streets, offers a dynamic setting where academic life blends seamlessly with local culture, music, art, and cuisine. Its central location in Italy also makes it easy for students to explore other cities and regions, providing an ideal base for cultural and academic exploration.

All BSc courses are taught in Italian, however 3 rd year BSc-students can usually also attend courses from the master's programme provided they have the academic pre-requisites. If you wish to include courses offered by other teaching areas, you must first request formal approval by email from the competent international mobility office. (https://www.unibo.it/en/study/international-experiences/incoming-exchange-students/contacts-for-exchange-students-at-unibo/contacts-of-campuses-international-relations-offices) If you choose an integrated course, you must attend it in its entirety, it is not possible to attend only one module and take a partial exam. Erasmus bachelor students can take both bachelor and master courses, however all bachelor courses are in Italian and economics master courses can only be attended by master students. Please note, that some economics courses can have a limited number of spots, so you will have to ask in advance in order to ensure that you will be able to attend.
