details.Description: The University of Bordeaux is one of France’s major public research universities, hosting over 54,000 students and approximately 6,000 staff members across multiple campuses. It is part of the Initiative of Excellence programme, which supports high-level research and international collaboration. The university is structured around several academic domains and maintains strong ties with national research organisations. Its scale and research output place it among the leading institutions in France, with a focus on interdisciplinary approaches and innovation. The university also participates in European university alliances, reinforcing its international engagement. Bordeaux offers a distinctive setting for those interested in spending time in a region known for its cultural heritage, accessibility, and quality of life. The city is recognised for its architecture, riverfront developments, and active public spaces, and has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It supports a wide range of exhibitions, concerts, and public events throughout the year, many of which are easily accessible to university students. Beyond the city, the surrounding region includes vineyards, Atlantic beaches, and natural parks, all within reach by public transport or short travel. This combination of urban life and regional diversity makes Bordeaux a practical and engaging base for an exchange semester.

You are free to take any course in at the College of Science and Technology, but you have to pay attention to the timetable for each course to avoid overlap in timetable. Some courses in Master level may have some restrictions (due to the limited capacity). The majority of course are taught in French, so you must have a high command of French.

details.Description: The University of Bristol has had a reputation for innovation since its founding in 1876. With a choice of over 200 degree courses covering a broad range of subjects, students at the University of Bristol engage with intellectually challenging courses that encourage independence of mind. The diversity of a centre for cutting-edge art, music and culture, coupled with being a historical city surrounded by countryside, make studying at Bristol a rich and exciting experience. Right in the heart of the city are many University buildings and facilities.

details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . As a result, students applying for exchange places in the UK cannot be guaranteed an Erasmus+ grant at the time of application. Eligibility for Erasmus+ funding will depend on whether the host university joins the programme and concludes an Erasmus+ agreement with the University of Copenhagen. Students nominated to a UK university will be informed of their grant eligibility no later than March 2027.
details.Additional information: Students must have completed at least one year of study at university level at the time of their application which should be evidenced on their transcript. You may apply for an exchange abroad to the University of Bristol for either a single semester or a full academic year. This agreement allows for enrolment in undergraduate modules only. MA-students from the University of Copenhagen considering Univeristy of Bristol must make sure that they can get approval from their faculty to transfer undergraduate (bachelor) modules from this university into their MA-programmes at UCPH. MA-students from the Faculty of Humanities should note that they will not be considered for this agreement , as they cannot get undergraduate modules from this university transfered into their MA-programmes at UCPH.

details.Description: The University of Caen Normandy is a public multidisciplinary institution located in northwestern France. It hosts approximately 30,000 students and employs over 2,000 academic and administrative staff across several campuses in the region. The university is known for its long academic tradition, dating back to its founding in 1432, and for its commitment to research and international cooperation. It maintains partnerships with institutions across Europe and beyond, and supports a wide range of research activities through its laboratories and doctoral schools. Its structure allows for close interaction between students and faculty, and its regional focus contributes to a strong connection between academic work and local development. Caen is a mid-sized city in the Normandy region, offering a combination of historical significance and modern infrastructure. Known for its role in World War II and its medieval heritage, the city also supports a vibrant cultural life, with museums, theatres, and public events throughout the year. Its location near the coast provides access to natural landscapes and outdoor activities, while its transport connections make it easy to reach Paris and other parts of France. For students considering an exchange semester, Caen offers a manageable and well-connected environment with opportunities to engage both academically and culturally.

Students apply for admission to 3 UC campuses after nomination for exchange.

As the duration of an exchange stay is at least two quarters , students must enroll in courses corresponding to 24 units, which is more than the 18 units required to obtain 30 ECTS. Transfer of excess units to ECTS will be handled according to the rules of the relevant UCPH faculty (due to the block structure at the Faculty of Science at UCPH, students from this faculty may consider taking 27 units, as this would give them the opportunity to transfer 45 ECTS before they return for block 4).
details.Restrictions: This agreement is for undergraduate studies only. Students who have passed  240 ECTS or more at university level by the time of departure cannot apply for this agreement. You have to apply for a minimum of two quarters or one semester. If you apply for fall, your exchange period will last from September to March. Spring semester from January to June. There are 9 UC campuses in total. After your nomination from UCPH, you will start your application to UC. You must apply to at least three different campuses , and the University of California Education Abroad programme (UCEAP) will decide which campus you are placed at. University of California health insurance is mandatory. Majors closed for exchange: - Business Administration - Design - Journalism - Medicine, Nursing, veterinary medicine - Law - Limited access to courses in Economics, Business and Computer Science You must select a UC major for your application. - Your major is the subject area where you will spend the majority of your time studying. - This might be a different major from your major at UCPH. - Plan to enroll in two or three courses in your major department each term, with the remainder of your classes in other majors. To do so you must meet the course prerequisites and space must be available in the course. Proof of financial resources when applying for a J1-student exchange visitor visa is required after acceptance to the University of California. You cannot apply for a second time Incoming students can only apply for exchange for a maximum of 1 academic year in total due to UCEAP restrictions. At UC, this is either 3 quarters or 2 semesters. This means, that if you have already been on exchange at UC from KU, you will not fulfill the requirements for attending UC for 2 quarters or 1 semester, as they cannot send you to the same campus again, nor guarantee that your application for a specific campus will be successful.

details.Description: At UC Davis School of Law, the curriculum is designed to provide a solid foundation of practical knowledge and skills that enable our graduates to pursue careers in whatever area of legal practice they may choose, from public service to business litigation to legal scholarship. Each of our faculty members is truly committed to teaching and together they offer a challenging academic program with diverse specialities including but not limited to business law, environmental law, international and comparative law, intellectual property law, immigration law, constitutional law and public interest law.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (:
Classes are taught in English. There are no TOEFL test requirements. 
Still, Davis requires a confirmation from the Faculty of Law in Copenhagen that certifies that the student’s language qualifications are sufficient. As a Danish law student you can apply for a language confirmation which will be based on your examination results in English stated in your ‘studentereksamensbevis’.
details.Restrictions: Law students must follow a full study load of min. 12 credits which correspond to 30 ECTS per semester. Be aware that credit requirements may be different for other exchange students at the University of California, Davis, School of Law. Visa requirements: If you are not a U.S. citizen, a J-1 visa is required for entry to the USA. As an exchange student you must demonstrate access to sufficient funds to cover your living expenses, during the time in the United States. Davis School of Law will provide additional information about this in the admission process. Insurance: In addition to a possible mandatory insurance at your host university, UCHP recommends that Danish students on an exchange programme take out an insurance coverage with a Danish insurance company to make sure that you are sufficiently covered especially when talking about possible need for home transportation to DK or possible coverage during your activities and trips outside the campus area of your host university.
details.Course information: Curriculum The students can choose from the majority of classes in the J.D. curriculum, which corresponds to studies at undergraduate level. Classes are limited in size (especially the seminar classes), so a request does not guarantee registration. The good news is most of our exchange students typically get a good percentage of their top choices Students must maintain a full course load: 4-5 classes and 10-15 units is a typical course load. When a student submits their class requests, they should identify 15-20 units of classes in total, in case one or two classes are full, or if they decide to drop one class after the first week. There are certain small number of classes that require prerequisites, but if the exchange student has experience in that area, that can be taken into consideration. For the fall semester, class schedules will not be released until mid-to-late April. For planning purposes, the majority of the classes that ran this fall will run next fall. However, there will be some changes, as there is a natural effort to expand and update the curriculum and add new, interesting classes for students. The style of teaching is based on the socratic method, meaning students are expected to actively participate in class discussions and cold calling may be used.

details.Description: Established in 1873 by scholars from Oxford and Cambridge, the University of Canterbury, in Christchurch, New Zealand, has an international reputation for academic excellence in both teaching and research. Teaching staff are actively involved in research and publishing in their areas of speciality. As a result, even undergraduate students can expect to be taught by lecturers who are at the forefront of knowledge in their field. The University’s world‐class education is also enhanced by the many outstanding international academics who visit each year on our staff exchange programmes. Students may be taught by academic staff from the universities of Oxford or Cambridge, among many others. The University is situated in a spacious landscaped campus in the suburb of Ilam, Christchurch, only 15 minutes from the central city and 10 minutes from the International Airport. The campus is attractively landscaped, with plenty of green space to relax with friends between lectures. Modern facilities include four libraries, computer suites with 24‐ hour access, lecture theatres, laboratories, studios, six halls of residence and a host of student services and facilities, including cafés, bars, a health centre and pharmacy, recreation facilities, childcare facilities, shops, an art gallery and an events centre. Learn more about Christchurch (https://www.christchurchnz.com/visit/plan-your-visit/seasonal-guides/winter)

details.Description: The University of Coimbra, founded in 1290 by King Dinis, is the oldest continuously operating university in Portugal and one of the oldest in the world. Relocated permanently to Coimbra in 1537, it occupies the historic Royal Palace, now known as the Paço das Escolas, and has been recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2013. The university enrolls over 25,000 students, with around 20 percent coming from abroad, and is organized into eight faculties offering a wide range of bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral programs. Blending centuries of tradition with modern academic excellence, it is especially renowned in fields such as medicine, engineering, social sciences, and the humanities. The campus is home to remarkable landmarks like the Baroque Biblioteca Joanina, which houses tens of thousands of historic volumes, and a botanical garden dating back to 1772. Living in Coimbra as a student means becoming part of a lively city where academic life and local culture are closely intertwined. The medieval old town and university buildings create a unique atmosphere, deeply shaped by traditions like the student capes and annual ceremonies such as Queima das Fitas and Latada. Students find community through the Associação Académica de Coimbra, the oldest student union in Portugal, which organizes a wide variety of cultural and sports activities, from theater and music to rugby, chess, and rowing. With its scenic riverside location along the Mondego, rich academic heritage, and vibrant student life, Coimbra offers an immersive and memorable university experience.

details.Description: The University of Crete, established in 1973, is a public, research-oriented institution with campuses in Rethymno and Heraklion. It serves a student body of approximately 20,000 undergraduates and 2,500 postgraduates, supported by over 500 academic staff and 420 administrative personnel. The university is organized into five schools and sixteen departments, offering a wide range of academic disciplines. It is known for its strong emphasis on research and international collaboration, participating actively in European programs such as Erasmus and maintaining partnerships with institutions across Europe and the United States. A unique feature of the University of Crete is its close integration with regional research centers, including the Foundation for Research and Technology – Hellas (FORTH), which enhances opportunities for students to engage in high-level scientific work. Crete, the largest and most populous of the Greek islands, offers a rich cultural and natural environment for students. The island combines ancient history, Mediterranean landscapes, and a vibrant local culture shaped by diverse influences from Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East. Students can explore archaeological sites, hike through dramatic gorges, and enjoy local cuisine rooted in the renowned Cretan diet. Public transport connects the university campuses with nearby towns and beaches, making it easy to experience the island’s varied offerings. A fun fact: Crete is home to two of the world’s few pink sand beaches, Balos and Elafonissi, adding a unique natural attraction to the student experience.

details.Description: The University of Crete, established in 1973, is a public, research-oriented institution with campuses in Rethymno and Heraklion. It serves a student body of approximately 20,000 undergraduates and 2,500 postgraduates, supported by over 500 academic staff and 420 administrative personnel. The university is organized into five schools and sixteen departments, offering a wide range of academic disciplines. It is known for its strong emphasis on research and international collaboration, participating actively in European programs such as Erasmus and maintaining partnerships with institutions across Europe and the United States. A unique feature of the University of Crete is its close integration with regional research centers, including the Foundation for Research and Technology – Hellas (FORTH), which enhances opportunities for students to engage in high-level scientific work. Crete, the largest and most populous of the Greek islands, offers a rich cultural and natural environment for students. The island combines ancient history, Mediterranean landscapes, and a vibrant local culture shaped by diverse influences from Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East. Students can explore archaeological sites, hike through dramatic gorges, and enjoy local cuisine rooted in the renowned Cretan diet. Public transport connects the university campuses with nearby towns and beaches, making it easy to experience the island’s varied offerings. A fun fact: Crete is home to two of the world’s few pink sand beaches, Balos and Elafonissi, adding a unique natural attraction to the student experience.

details.Description: The University of Eastern Finland, established in 2010 through the merger of the University of Joensuu and the University of Kuopio, is a prestigious institution with campuses in Joensuu and Kuopio. details.Description: The University of Freiburg, officially known as Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg, is one of Germany’s oldest and most respected universities, founded in 1457. It currently hosts around 24,000 students and employs over 8,000 staff nad almost 5,000 doctoral candidates across eleven faculties. The university is recognized for its strong research output, particularly in the life sciences, humanities, and sustainability studies, and is part of the German Excellence Strategy. A defining feature of Freiburg is its close collaboration with external research institutions such as the Fraunhofer and Max Planck Societies, offering students access to a broad academic network and research opportunities beyond the university itself. Situated in the southwest of Germany near the borders of France and Switzerland, Freiburg is a vibrant university town known for its compact layout, green surroundings, and active student life. The city has a population of about 230,000 and is often cited as one of Germany’s most environmentally conscious and bicycle-friendly cities. Freiburg’s location at the edge of the Black Forest provides easy access to hiking, skiing, and other outdoor activities, making it an attractive destination for students seeking both academic engagement and recreational opportunities. Its international atmosphere and strong local support for education contribute to a welcoming environment for exchange students.

details.Description: Situated between the Alps and the Jura mountains, at the southwestern tip of Switzerland and Lake Geneva, Geneva is in the heart of Western Europe. Its ideal geographical location has made the city a prosperous hub for trade and exchanges of all kinds. https://www.unige.ch/exchange/en/incoming/why-geneva/#_msocom_1 This cosmopolitan city is home to more than 180 nationalities and is recognized worldwide for its spirit of openness and tolerance. Considered the smallest of the major world capitals, Geneva, which is home to some thirty international organizations including the UN, WTO, WHO and ILO and more than 300 NGOs and permanent missions of foreign states, has a true international vocation.This multicultural environment is reflected at the University of Geneva, where about one third of the students are foreign nationals. The university pursues a very active policy of international relations; in particular, it participates in numerous bi- or multilateral agreements, networks and programs such as Erasmus and Socrates. Ideally located near the most famous ski areas of the Alps, not far from the Mediterranean, while being anchored in Central Europe, Geneva (https://www.geneve.ch/) offers the rare advantages of a cosmopolitan city on a human scale. Cuisine and music from all over the world are found here. Lovers of green spaces will find an atmosphere conducive to meditation in its parks or on the shores of Lake Geneva. Culture (https://www.geneve.ch/en/themes/culture) lovers will be spoilt for choice, thanks to the presence in Geneva of one of the most prestigious opera scenes (https://www.gtg.ch/) in Europe, several film festivals (https://www.giff.ch/) , and numerous concert halls and theaters. The University of Geneva takes an active part in this cultural scene. Its film club and choir in particular attract large audiences. But Geneva also lives to the rhythm of a multitude of associations, representing the most diverse countries and interests, which make it uniquely suited for the exchange of ideas and traditions.

details.Description: Situated between the Alps and the Jura mountains, at the southwestern tip of Switzerland and Lake Geneva, Geneva is in the heart of Western Europe. Its ideal geographical location has made the city a prosperous hub for trade and exchanges of all kinds. https://www.unige.ch/exchange/en/incoming/why-geneva/#_msocom_1 This cosmopolitan city is home to more than 180 nationalities and is recognized worldwide for its spirit of openness and tolerance. Considered the smallest of the major world capitals, Geneva, which is home to some thirty international organizations including the UN, WTO, WHO and ILO and more than 300 NGOs and permanent missions of foreign states, has a true international vocation.This multicultural environment is reflected at the University of Geneva, where about one third of the students are foreign nationals. The university pursues a very active policy of international relations; in particular, it participates in numerous bi- or multilateral agreements, networks and programs such as Erasmus and Socrates. Ideally located near the most famous ski areas of the Alps, not far from the Mediterranean, while being anchored in Central Europe, Geneva (https://www.geneve.ch/) offers the rare advantages of a cosmopolitan city on a human scale. Cuisine and music from all over the world are found here. Lovers of green spaces will find an atmosphere conducive to meditation in its parks or on the shores of Lake Geneva. Culture (https://www.geneve.ch/en/themes/culture) lovers will be spoilt for choice, thanks to the presence in Geneva of one of the most prestigious opera scenes (https://www.gtg.ch/) in Europe, several film festivals (https://www.giff.ch/) , and numerous concert halls and theaters. The University of Geneva takes an active part in this cultural scene. Its film club and choir in particular attract large audiences. But Geneva also lives to the rhythm of a multitude of associations, representing the most diverse countries and interests, which make it uniquely suited for the exchange of ideas and traditions.

details.Description: Glasgow University is an international law school with a rich heritage.  Law was one of the four original faculties established by the university upon its founding in 1451. The subject has been taught continuously since 1714. Today, Glasgow University teach students from over 30 countries with a staff from across the world.  There is a diverse research interests ranging from the United Nations and international courts and tribunals, to copyright issues in the digital age.
details.Academic calendar: Semester 1: Mid-September to early December. Exams in mid-December. Semester 2: Early January to early May. Exams in May. details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Glasgow has waived their language test requirements for Danish law exchange students who have a Danish ‘studentereksamen or HF diploma’. Instead of a TOEFL or IELTS test you apply for a language confirmation from the Faculty of Law in Copenhagen. A language confirmation will only be needed after you have been nominated to the exchange programme in Glasgow. The language confirmation will be based on your grades in English from your ‘studentereksamen’ or HF diploma and it will exempt you from taking a TOEFL or IELTS test. You will receive a special language proficiency form from Glasgow after your nomination which you must upload in your application for a language confirmation.
details.Study load: 60 credits = 30 ECTS The normal average workload is 60 Glasgow credits equivalent to 30 ECTS per semester. Course levels Courses at levels 1 and 2 are normally undertaken by Glasgow students during their first two years of study. Level 3 and 4 courses are upper-level undergraduate courses that require at least two years background experience in the subject area that will be studied at Glasgow. UCPH encourages our law students to apply for law courses at level 3 or 4. See link to course catalogue below at 'Important links'. Please note that the majority of courses at level 3 (on third year) and level 4 (on fourth year) are full year courses. For students who arrive in January, courses on level 3 and 4 will be limited. In connection to full-year courses, semester 1 students can take the first part of the course, for half of the available credits (obviously not an option for semester 2 students).  This means that if you will not be in Glasgow at the time of the examination of the whole year course, you will be asked to submit another piece of assessment in lieu of the examination.

After the application procedures you will receive information from the University of Glasgow about visa procedures. There may be differences in the requirements for a stay of 6 months' duration compared to a stay beyond that period. Warning - if you go on student exchange in the last semester of your master degree, a transcript delay may postpone the completion of your master degree! Generally, at British universities official transcripts are delayed with approx. 3-4 months into the next semester due to an audit for a Board of Examiners. In urgent cases, UCPH try to obtain confirmation on the validity of a provisional transcript – but we cannot give you any guarantee in advance.

details.Description: The University of Gothenburg, founded in 1891, is one of Sweden’s largest and most respected universities, with around 58,000 students. It offers a broad academic portfolio across eight faculties with plenty of elements available in English. The university is renowned for its high-quality research often ranking among the top 200 universities worldwide. The university does not sit on one single sprawling campus; instead its faculties and departments are spread across a number of major locations within the city of Gothenburg Living in Gothenburg adds to the appeal. Sweden’s second-largest city, with about 600,000 residents, combines a lively urban environment with the relaxed feel of a coastal town. Students enjoy the city’s canals, green spaces, vibrant music and food scenes, and excellent public transport that makes exploring easy. Meanwhile, there are plenty of outdoor possibilities, including quick escapes to the nearby archipelago.

details.Description: The University of Göttingen, officially Georg-August-Universität Göttingen, is a research-oriented public university with a strong international reputation, particularly in the natural sciences and humanities. Founded in 1737, it currently enrolls around 30,000 students and employs over 4,000 academic staff. The university is part of several major research networks and maintains close ties with institutions such as the Max Planck Society, which has multiple institutes located in Göttingen. A notable feature of the university is its emphasis on academic freedom and its long-standing tradition of fostering critical thinking and interdisciplinary collaboration. Göttingen seems to pulsate with a thirst for knowledge. It is a city shaped by students and academic life more than anywhere else in Germany. A total of 44 Nobel laureates are associated with Göttingen. Some were born in the city, while others came here to study, teach or conduct research. Göttingen is a compact university town in central Germany, with a population of approximately 120,000. Known as the "City of Knowledge", the city’s identity is closely tied to its academic community, and students make up a significant portion of the population. This creates a lively and student-focused atmosphere, with a wide range of cultural events, cafés, and public spaces geared toward young people. Göttingen’s location offers easy access to other major cities such as Hanover and Kassel, while its green surroundings and historical architecture provide a pleasant environment for study and daily life. The city’s manageable size and strong support for student initiatives make it particularly welcoming for exchange students.

details.Description: The University of Göttingen, officially Georg-August-Universität Göttingen, is a research-oriented public university with a strong international reputation, particularly in the natural sciences and humanities. Founded in 1737, it currently enrolls around 30,000 students and employs over 4,000 academic staff. The university is part of several major research networks and maintains close ties with institutions such as the Max Planck Society, which has multiple institutes located in Göttingen. A notable feature of the university is its emphasis on academic freedom and its long-standing tradition of fostering critical thinking and interdisciplinary collaboration. Göttingen seems to pulsate with a thirst for knowledge. It is a city shaped by students and academic life more than anywhere else in Germany. A total of 44 Nobel laureates are associated with Göttingen. Some were born in the city, while others came here to study, teach or conduct research. Göttingen is a compact university town in central Germany, with a population of approximately 120,000. Known as the "City of Knowledge", the city’s identity is closely tied to its academic community, and students make up a significant portion of the population. This creates a lively and student-focused atmosphere, with a wide range of cultural events, cafés, and public spaces geared toward young people. Göttingen’s location offers easy access to other major cities such as Hanover and Kassel, while its green surroundings and historical architecture provide a pleasant environment for study and daily life. The city’s manageable size and strong support for student initiatives make it particularly welcoming for exchange students.

You generally select several teaching modules. A module is a self-contained course unit consisting of one or more sub-courses. Thus, a module can consist of one or more lectures, seminars, or exercise courses. Please select only entire modules and not individual partial courses, otherwise you may not be able to take the exam. At the Faculty of Agricultural Sciences, you can normally join the lectures from the BSc courses without any problems and without prior registration. In contrast, the number of participants for seminars, exercises, laboratory work and excursions are limited. Please inquire early at the respective chair whether you can be accepted. Exchange students can take module examinations, but are not allowed to write a Bachelor or Master thesis.

details.Restrictions: Exchange programme for master level law students only. As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. The University of Iceland offers a complete course package with approximately 4-5 courses totaling 30 ECTS per semester. The teaching style seems to be similar to UCPH with bit less groupwork in Iceland.

details.Additional information: When the Faculty of Law in Copenhagen has nominated you for an exchange place at the University of Iceland, you have to apply for admission within the application deadlines which may vary a bit from year to year. A mentor system is offered. Reykjavík University does not offer a lot of sports opportunities. Instead you may be recommended to visit the local swimmingpools, spas or try outdoor activities in the Icelandic nature like swimming in hot springs, hiking etc.

details.Description: The University of Iceland is the country’s oldest and largest university, with roughly 14,000 students enrolled across undergraduate, graduate, and PhD programmes. It comprises five schools and over 25 faculties, offering more than 400 programmes in many fields including sciences, humanities, health and social sciences. Classes are mainly taught in Icelandic, but there is a growing number of English-taught courses, especially at Master’s level. Reykjavík offers a vibrant cultural life, easy access to nature, and a welcoming atmosphere. You’ll be close to museums, cafés and arts events, while also having quick access to outstanding natural beauty: volcanic landscapes, geothermal pools, glaciers, waterfalls and long summer days (or northern lights in winter).

The university is in the twin cities of Champaign and Urbana (total population 207,000) in east-central Illinois. Situated about 140 miles south of Chicago, 125 miles west of Indianapolis, and 180 miles northeast of St. Louis.

details.Description: The University of Jyväskylä is a dynamic and esteemed multidisciplinary institution in Finland. With six faculties and independent institutes, it stands as one of the largest and most popular universities in the country. Founded in 1863 as the first Finnish-speaking teacher training college, Jyväskylä Teacher Seminary, it has evolved into a nationally and internationally recognized research university. Known for its expertise in education, human sciences, and natural sciences, the University of Jyväskylä attracts top-tier students and is highly selective. Embrace a transformative academic journey at this prestigious institution, ranked as the second largest university in Finland.
details.Academic calendar: Autumn semester: August – December Spring semester: January – May
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (:
A language test certificate is not required from exchange students. Students wishing to study at the University of Jyväskylä as
exchange students should be able to follow university lectures
in English or Finnish, participate in seminar discussions and
understand written material in their field. In addition, most
courses require writing essays and research papers. This means that applicants should be at least B1 but preferably B2 (or
higher) level users of the English language. These requirements
do not apply to students whose Finnish skills are good enough
to carry out their studies in Finnish.

details.Description: Nestled between the Alps and the Adriatic Sea, Alpen-Adria-Universität Klagenfurt is a modern, research-driven university located in one of Austria’s most picturesque regions, Carinthia, near the shores of Lake Wörthersee, not far from the borders of Italy and Slovenia. As the leading academic institution in Carinthia, it offers a vibrant and international study environment with a strong commitment to innovation, sustainability, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Exchange students benefit from a wide range of English-taught courses across faculties such as humanities, technical sciences, management, and social sciences, as well as from personalized support services and a welcoming campus culture. With its dynamic academic offerings and high quality of life, the university provides an ideal setting for a rewarding and enriching exchange semester. The university has around 1700 staff and 13,000 students. Work and research are carried out at AAU’s four faculties. Since it was founded in the year 1970, the university has become firmly established as the leading institution of academic education in Carinthia, and serves as an important hub for the acquisition, exchange and transfer of knowledge across the entire Alps-Adriatic Region.

The University of Konstanz is comprised of thirteen departments that are divided into three faculties: the Faculty of Sciences, the Faculty of Humanities and the Faculty of Politics - Law - Economics. At the international level, the University of Konstanz advances select and sustainable partnerships with over 70 research-focused universities in order to promote scientific collaboration and student exchange.

details.Description: Discover the University of Lapland, a renowned international and multidisciplinary university located in Rovaniemi, on the Arctic Circle. With expertise in art and design, education, law, social sciences, and Northern and Arctic issues, as well as tourism research, this university offers a diverse range of academic disciplines. For the Faculty of Law, the University of Lapland is a key player in legal education, responsible for educating a significant portion of Finland's lawyers. Their innovative degree structure combines various modes of study, fostering a balance between practical skills and theoretical knowledge. Within the faculty, three prominent institutes specialize in Air and Space Law, Commercial Law, and Law and Informatics. Additionally, the faculty provides a comprehensive selection of English-taught courses, ensuring accessibility for international students.

details.Description: You may apply for an exchange abroad to the University of Leeds for either a single semester or a full academic year. This agreement allows for enrolment in undergraduate and postgraduate modules. University of Copenhagen MA-students considering taking undergraduate modules only - or a mix of undergraduate and postgraduate modules at the Univeristy of Leeds must make sure that they can get approval from their faculty to transfer undergraduate (bachelor) modules from the host university into their programmes here at UCPH. MA-students from the Faculty of Humanities should note that they cannot get undergraduate modules from this university transfered into their MA-programmes at UCPH.
details.Academic calendar: Autumn term: September - January Spring term: January - June
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: English level B2 on the CEFR scale - transcript from high school with the grade 4 or higher in English is accepted.
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 60 credits Please note: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Study load for graduate students: 60 credits Please note: Full year: Conversion is not applicable for full year stays at this university. Study load requirement is higher when transferring credits corresponding to a full academic year. Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: Restricted study areas: Medicine, Veterinary Medicine, and Dentistry. Media and Communications students Limited availability. Leeds may be able to accept a limited number of students that have a major in media and/ or communication. Students  may only take a limited number of courses in this subject area - and must therefore also consider courses from other teaching schools at Leeds. Important information about provisional results and receiving your transcript of records (karakterudskrift) from Leeds: Semester 1 / autumn semester Even if semester 1 ends in January, Leeds cannot produce an official transcript of records (karakterudskrift) until the end of July. This is because the January exam results remain provisional until external exam board meetings in late June. University of Leeds will instead provide a provisional transcript for all students who are studying at Leeds for semester 1. This may delay your final transfer of credits at UCPH, as not all faculties accept provisional transcript of records for credit transfer. Postgraduate courses Academic transcripts for postgraduate modules are not released until November after studies have ended at Leeds. This means, students going on exchange in e.g the autumn semester, will not be able to transfer credits earned at Leeds before November in the subsequent academic year. Mix of undergraduate and postgraduate courses If you choose a mixture of undergraduate and postgraduate modules, Leeds will send you a transcript in July, but the postgraduate results will be provisional until November and could change. Leeds will automatically send you another transcript in November, which will show all your official results. Please also note that provisional marks/results rarely change.
details.Course information: About module selection Students should complete the module enrolment form sent in their acceptance email with their preferred module codes. The Teaching Schools will then enrol them on the modules. When the University of Leeds accept you to the study abroad programme, you will be classed as undergraduate, but this does not prevent you from selecting postgraduate modules as Leeds have a postgraduate agreement with UCPH. If applying for postgraduate module(s), applicants will need to show that they meet the module’s prerequisites on their academic transcript. If you would like to know in advance whether or not it will be possible for you to study some specific postgraduate level modules, you can contact the relevant teaching school - please remember to include your transcript of records in the email. Please find a list of the schools' study abroad coordinator contacts here (https://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-exchange-and-study-abroad/doc/school-contacts-incoming-study-abroad-students) .
details.Important links: Website for incoming exchange (https://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-exchange-and-study-abroad/) Undergraduate module (course) information (https://www.leeds.ac.uk/incomingstudy) Postgraduate module (course) information (https://www.leeds.ac.uk/incomingstudy) . The ‘isa’ box must be ticked to find the modules available to incoming study abroad students.
details.Housing: University of Leeds guarantees university accommodation for international students. After you have received a letter of acceptance and your University of Leeds ID number, you must apply for accommodation (http://accommodation.leeds.ac.uk/info/4/applying/3/deadlines_and_apply) directly with the accommodation office and meet their application deadlines: September arrival: apply by 1 July January arrival: apply by 1 December If you will be studying at University of Leeds for semester 1 only, University of Leeds will offer you an accommodation contract that finishes during the middle of the January exam period.
details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . Eligibility for Erasmus+ funding will depend on whether the host university joins the programme and concludes an Erasmus+ agreement with the University of Copenhagen. Students nominated to a UK university will be informed of their grant eligibility no later than March 2027.
details.Additional information: Students must have completed at least one year of study at university level at the time of their application which should be evidenced on their transcript.

details.Description: KU Leuven is one of Europe’s leading research universities, consistently ranked among the top institutions worldwide for innovation and academic excellence. Founded in 1425, it is the oldest university in Belgium and currently hosts over 64,000 students, including more than 15,000 international students from over 140 countries. With 15 faculties offering nearly 230 degree programmes, KU Leuven provides a comprehensive and interdisciplinary academic environment. details.Description: The University of Liège (ULiège) is a public research university and the only comprehensive institution in French-speaking Belgium offering a full range of academic disciplines. It hosts over 25,000 students and employs more than 3,000 staff members across 11 faculties and several research centres. ULiège is known for its strong commitment to open science, interdisciplinary collaboration, and civic engagement. Its structure encourages cross-faculty cooperation and supports research that addresses complex societal challenges. The university also places emphasis on internationalisation, welcoming students and researchers from over 120 countries and maintaining active partnerships across Europe and beyond. The university’s main campus is located in Sart Tilman, a green and spacious area just outside the city of Liège, while other facilities are integrated into the urban centre. Liège is a mid-sized city in eastern Belgium, close to the borders of Germany and the Netherlands, offering easy access to major European cities like Brussels, Paris, and Cologne. Known for its industrial heritage and cultural diversity, Liège has a long history of migration and international exchange, making it a relevant and engaging setting for students interested in global and societal issues. The city combines accessible public transport, a lively cultural scene, and a student-friendly atmosphere, providing a balanced environment for both academic focus and everyday life.

The University of Limerick (UL), founded in 1972 and granted university status in 1989, is a forward-thinking, research-led institution known for its strong emphasis on innovation, collaboration, and real-world learning. UL offers a wide range of academic programs through its four faculties: Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences; Education and Health Sciences; Science and Engineering; and the Kemmy Business School, which holds prestigious international accreditations. The university is particularly noted for its co-operative education model, which integrates work placements into many degree programs, and its close partnerships with industry and public institutions. With a student population of around 16,500, including a thriving community of international and exchange students, UL provides a supportive and dynamic academic environment. Located on a scenic riverside campus just outside the city of Limerick, the university blends modern architecture with natural beauty. The campus is known for its welcoming atmosphere, green spaces, and iconic footbridges across the River Shannon. Limerick itself is a friendly, student-oriented city that offers a rich cultural life, from galleries and music venues to sports and local festivals. Its manageable size, affordability, and lively student scene make it an appealing destination for international students. Whether you're exploring the nearby Wild Atlantic Way or enjoying the strong sense of community on campus, studying at UL offers a well-rounded experience both academically and personally.

details.Description: You may apply for an exchange abroad to the University of Liverpool for either a single semester or a full academic year. This agreement allows for enrolment in undergraduate modules only. MA-students from the University of Copenhagen considering Univeristy of Liverpool must make sure that they can get approval from their faculty to transfer undergraduate (bachelor) modules from this university into their MA-programmes at UCPH. MA-students from the Faculty of Humanities should note that they will not be considered for this agreement , as they cannot get undergraduate modules from this university transfered into their MA-programmes at UCPH.
details.Academic calendar: Semester 1 (autumn semester): September - January Semester 2 (spring semester): January - June University of Liverpool term dates page (https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/term-dates/)
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Students studying at the University of Liverpool for less than 6 months may submit a letter from their home university confirming their level of English. Students may use this English Qualification Form (https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/media/livacuk/study/international/study-abroad/English,Qualfication,Form.pdf) as proof of their level of English, and can upload this completed form to their application in lieu of a formal qualification. If you are planning on studying at University of Liverpool for a full academic year, please read about the language requirements on this website. (https://www.kent.ac.uk/courses/english-language-requirements)
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 60 credits Please note: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: Undergraduate admission only. At the University of Liverpool, exchange students can apply to all academic fields except courses offered through its Schools of Dentistry, Veterinary Science, Health Sciences, Medicine and Liverpool Law School. The Management School is open to students who are majoring within business related subjects. Students who are not majoring in a business-related subject may only take up to two modules per semester from the Management School. A list of those restricted courses are contained in the University of Liverpool’s Module Guidance which is available for potential exchange students to consider prior to applying for such a course at https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/global-opportunities/inbound/study-in-liverpool/academic/. (https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/student-administration/managing-my-studies/module-registration/)
details.Important links: Website for inbound students (https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/global-opportunities/visiting-students/) Module guidance (https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/student-administration/managing-my-studies/module-registration/) including course lists and restricted course list
details.Housing: If you are staying for Semester 1 only, you can apply for one of the rooms available in the Study Abroad Village (Tudor Close & Melville Grove). You should apply as early as you are able to secure your place. If you are staying for Semester 2 only, you are guaranteed a place in on-campus University accommodation. Where possible you will be placed in the Study Abroad Village. If you wish to take up your place, apply via Liverpool Life. If you are staying for the full academic year, you are guaranteed a place in a University of Liverpool Halls of Residence. If you wish to take up your place, apply via Liverpool Life. More information on the University Halls of Accommodation page. (https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/global-opportunities/visiting-students/accommodation/)
details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . As a result, students applying for exchange places in the UK cannot be guaranteed an Erasmus+ grant at the time of application. Eligibility for Erasmus+ funding will depend on whether the host university joins the programme and concludes an Erasmus+ agreement with the University of Copenhagen. Students nominated to a UK university will be informed of their grant eligibility no later than March 2027.

details.Description: The Faculty of Law at the University of Lucerne is the youngest law faculty in Switzerland. Since October 2001, it offers a curriculum based on the Bologna Model. Since then, the Lucerne University Faculty of Law has experienced an increase in popularity and number of students. The Lucerne Faculty of Law offers an accomplished and prestigious program, which provides students with excellent opportunities in the job market, teaches skills essential for internships and work, and prepares them to score high (above average) on the Cantonal lawyer’s exams.
details.Academic calendar: An orientation week is held before the start of each semester - with mandatory attendance (without any charges). Fall semester: Mid-September to December (exams included). Spring semester: Mid-February to early June (exams included) See link to academic calendar (https://www.unilu.ch/en/study/dates-and-information/semester-dates/faculty-of-law/)
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: German is the main language of instruction at the University of Lucerne. Law classes are taught in German and in English. According to Lucerne it should be possible to take a full study load of 30 ECTS with law courses taught in English. Danish Law students will be waived from the English language requirements below if you have passed the bachelor law course ‘International Law’ at UCPH. To ensure full participation in our programmes non-native English speakers or students who are not studying on an English-taught programme at their home university must provide one of the following documents: - TOEFL IBT 85 - IELTS 6.5 - Duolingo English Test (DET) 120 - We may also accept letters from language course coordinators or academic staff who can confirm that a student has a C1 level on the Common European Framework for Languages ( CEFR (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) ), or that the student has studied and passed English-taught courses. In this case please name the titles of the English-taught courses and refer to the grade in the academic transcript. Please note that students nominated to study on our German-taught programmes will not be required to submit proof of English proficiency. Although a language course is recommended if you take German law courses. At Lucerne, a German Short Course will be offered.
details.Restrictions: Law courses in English are only offered from master’s level onwards; therefore, exchange students are only accepted if they are in their final bachelor’s year or in their master’s degree.
details.Course information: All law courses offered in English will be master level courses and these are accessible for both bachelor and master level exchange students. The majority of law courses have a value of 5 ECTS (a few guest lecture courses have a value of 2 ECTS). As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad.
details.Important links: See the link to course offers (https://www.unilu.ch/en/study/courses-exams-regulations/faculty-of-law/courses/#section=c27548) . The Faculty of Law at the University of Lucerne (https://www.unilu.ch/en/faculties/faculty-of-law/) The University of Lucerne (https://www.unilu.ch/en/) Information for incoming students (https://www.unilu.ch/en/international/mobility/student-mobility/incoming-students/)
details.Housing: There are a limited number of rooms available for exchange students at the student residence. Students have the possibility to apply for a room during the online application process. It cannot always be guaranteed that students get a room in the student residence. See addition info on Housing information (https://www.unilu.ch/en/international/mobility/student-mobility/incoming-students/housing/)
details.Scholarships: Students applying for this university have so far been automatically nominated for a SEMP (Swiss-European Mobility Program) grant. Switzerland is currently seeking to join the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 if they will join. As a result, students applying for exchange places in Switzerland will receive either a SEMP grant or an Erasmus Scholarship.
details.Additional information: See info on Studying in Lucerne (https://www.unilu.ch/en/study/studying-in-lucerne/) When the Faculty of Law in Copenhagen has nominated you for an exchange place at University of Lucerne, you have to apply for admission within the application deadlines which may vary a bit from year to year. Switzerland is a visa-free country, but the Cantonal Office of Migration has implemented new regulations having the effect that exchange students need a residence permit for a stay at the University of Lucerne. As an exchange student you must pay the fee of approx. CHF 70. However, the University of Lucerne applies for the residence permit on behalf of all incoming exchange students. As part of this process, your parents will have to sign a document from the University of Lucerne saying “we are responsible for all costs relating to the exchange semester at the University of Lucerne”. Or alternatively, you must provide proof of financial funds (CHF 10'500 per semester) on a bank account. In this context, please let us assure you that all exchange students are exempt from paying tuition fee at the University of Lucerne.

details.Description: You may apply for an exchange abroad to the University of Manchester for either a single semester or a full academic year. This agreement allows for enrolment in undergraduate modules only. MA-students from the University of Copenhagen considering Univeristy of Manchester must make sure that they can get approval from their faculty to transfer undergraduate (bachelor) modules from this university into their MA-programmes at UCPH. MA-students from the Faculty of Humanities should note that they will not be considered for this agreement , as they cannot get undergraduate modules from this university transfered into their MA-programmes at UCPH.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: September-January Spring semester: February-June Please visit this link (https://www.manchester.ac.uk/about/key-dates/) for details about the key dates at The University of Manchester.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: The standard admissions requirement is IELTS 6.0 with not less than 5.5 in any one component or a corresponding result form another accepted test - see the list below. Country specific tests: Danish STX/HF/HHX or HTX with min 7 for English results. English B corresponds to level B2 on the CEFR-scale, which is accepted by Manchester as a 6.0 IELTS result. English A corresponds to level C1 on the CEFR-scala. For students planning to study at University of Manchester for 1 semester the following documents are required: 1) a transcript of records from high school with English on level B2 on the ECFR scale and 2) a document from the university confirming a level of English B2 on the CEFR scale. For students planning to study at University of Manchester for a full academic year must supply the same documents as stated above with one of the following: IELTS Academic (UKVI or non-UKVI) TOEFL iBT Home Edition Pearson Test of English - Academic Trinity College London Integrated Skills in English (ISE I, ISE II, ISE III) Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE) and Certificate in Proficiency in English (CPE) International Baccalaureate Michigan Cambridge Language Assessments (CaMLA): Examination for the Certificate of Proficiency in English (ECPE) LanguageCert (UKVI version Besides the general language requirements stated above students must also meet any equivalent subject area language requirements (where these are higher) to access units in those subject areas. Subject area requirements can be found under the relevant listing in the course unit search on the webpage: https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/study-abroad-exchange/unit-search/ (https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/study-abroad-exchange/unit-search/) . Please note that no Humanities subject areas accepts a score of lower than IELTS 6.5 or equivalent. If a student’s degree programme is taught entirely in English , Manchester will also accept a letter on headed paper from the home institution confirming that this is the case.
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 60 credits Please note: Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: Undergraduate admission only. Not open for exchange students: Medicine, Veterinary Medicine, Pharmacy, Dentistry, Business, Electrical Engineering You must be able to evidence at least two complete semesters of study on your academic transcript at the time of your application. Law: Law students can enrol onto undergraduate level courses 1,2 and 3, but cannot enrol onto Master’s level courses. As level 3 course units are typically heavily oversubscribed, Law majors who plan to join Manchester for Semester 2 of the academic year need to make an early application. Manchester recommends applying by 1 June. Computer Science: Computer Science course units are very heavily oversubscribed. History: Most Level 3 course units are heavily oversubscribed, particularly Modern History courses. Study Abroad / exchange students who are majoring in History and already have an extensive background in the subject may be considered for Level 3 course units, but will be subject to an interview on arrival, and a place on a Level 3 course unit cannot be guaranteed. Students wishing to access Level 2 History courses should also have sufficient background study in the subject. History majors who plan to join us for Semester 2 of the academic year and who wish to take Level 3 History course units need to make an early application .  Manchester recommends applying by 1 June. Music: All Music course units have prerequisites. Students must be a music major to be eligible for consideration for these course units. Psychology: Level 3 Psychology courses are only open to students majoring in Psychology, in years 3 or 4 of their undergraduate degree, with a GPA of 3.3 or above. Psychology – students cannot take the Year 2 unit PSYC21061 Statistics and Data Analysis if they will not be available for the semester 1 exam period. Psychology – students with no previous Psychology training in Research Methods and Statistics cannot take the following Year 2 units: Cognition, Topics & Issues in Social Psychology, Cognitive Neuroscience, Interventions to Improve Mental Health & Wellbeing. Creative Writing: Students applying for Level 3 Creative Writing course units must supply an example of written work (eg a poem or a story). You should email this piece of writing to exchangestudy@manchester.ac.uk (mailto:exchangestudy@manchester.ac.uk) after receiving your offer letter.
details.Important links: Website for incoming exchange (https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/study-abroad-exchange/) Course unit list (https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/study-abroad-programmes/study-abroad/course-units/subject-list/)
details.Housing: Students coming for one semester only are not guaranteed a room in Manchester accommodatioon, but under normal circumstances are usually allocated one: International students’ accommodation at The University of Manchester (https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/accommodation/)
details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . As a result, students applying for exchange places in the UK cannot be guaranteed an Erasmus+ grant at the time of application. Eligibility for Erasmus+ funding will depend on whether the host university joins the programme and concludes an Erasmus+ agreement with the University of Copenhagen. Students nominated to a UK university will be informed of their grant eligibility no later than March 2027.
details.Additional information: Students must have completed at least one year of study at university level at the time of their application which should be evidenced on their transcript.

details.Description: The University of Mannheim is one of the leading higher educational institutions in Germany. This has been confirmed by numerous rankings, awards, by surveys among employers and by the German Excellence Initiative. The university's profile is shaped by its emphasis on business administration, economics, and social sciences. Staff members at six schools and departments teach and carry out research in Business Administration, Economics, the Humanities, Social Sciences, Law and Business Informatics and Mathematics. University of Mannheim has 12,000 students. The campus has an international and diverse student population with over 2,000 international students. Most lecture halls are inside the Schloss, one of the largest baroque buildings in the world. The campus is within walking distance from the city center.

details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student, you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. The University of Mannheim requires that exchange students arrive at least one week before the start of lectures to enrol and attend our mandatory Welcome Week.
details.Course information: See law course offers (https://www.uni-mannheim.de/en/academics/coming-to-mannheim/exchange-students/courses/course-catalog/law-all/) for both bachelor and master level courses. Research and teaching activity at the Department of Law is clearly oriented towards business and economic law. In recent years the Department of Law has earned the reputation of being one of the leading German schools in the areas of business law and economic law.

details.Description: Established in 1853, the University of Melbourne is Australia's second oldest university. The University of Melbourne is a public-spirited institution that makes distinctive contributions to society in research, teaching and learning, and engagement. It is consistently ranked among the leading universities in the world, with international rankings of world universities placing it as number 1 in Australia and number 37 in the world (Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2024). Melbourne offers broad undergraduate degrees and world-leading graduate programs to about 54,000 students each year, 44% being international students from 150+ countries. Campus is located in the heart of Melbourne and there are currently over 200 clubs affiliated to the University of Melbourne Student Union (UMSU). Consistently voted as one of the world’s most livable cities, Melbourne is the cultural and sporting capital of Australia with many festivals and sporting events held throughout the year. With 38% of the population born overseas and 140 cultures represented, Melbourne is extremely multi-cultural and welcoming of people from all backgrounds. Melbourne’s food scene is world class and boasts more coffee shops per capita than any other city in the world! Check out Melbourne Global Instagram Account (https://www.instagram.com/melbourneglobal/)

Please note that not all UCPH Master’s (graduate) programmes allow credit transfer of bachelor (undergraduate) courses into their programmes. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.

details.Description: The University of Milan stands as a leading institution in Italy, recognized for its substantial investments in research infrastructure and fostering human capital. With the ever-changing landscape of knowledge, these two elements are crucial in addressing complex societal and industrial challenges. The university comprises eight faculties and two schools, encompassing a wide range of disciplines such as Agricultural and Food Sciences, Exercise and Sports Sciences, Humanities, Law, Linguistic and Cultural Mediation Sciences, Medicine, Pharmacy, Political, Economic & Social Sciences, Science & Technology, and Veterinary Medicine. In terms of student life, the university offers opportunities for engagement and enrichment beyond the classroom. The University Sports Centre (CUS) serves as an amateur sports association that has been promoting and organizing university sporting activities for over 70 years. Students have access to a variety of sports at affordable rates, both within the center's events and in affiliated sports facilities. Moreover, the university has established a network of relationships and signed agreements with cultural institutions and associations in Milan and other cities. This allows for vibrant cultural exchanges between the academic and local communities, providing students with discounts at museums, theaters, cinemas, and more, further enhancing their educational experience. details.Description: The University of Milan stands as a leading institution in Italy, recognized for its substantial investments in research infrastructure and fostering human capital. With the ever-changing landscape of knowledge, these two elements are crucial in addressing complex societal and industrial challenges. The university comprises eight faculties and two schools, encompassing a wide range of disciplines such as Agricultural and Food Sciences, Exercise and Sports Sciences, Humanities, Law, Linguistic and Cultural Mediation Sciences, Medicine, Pharmacy, Political, Economic & Social Sciences, Science & Technology, and Veterinary Medicine. In terms of student life, the university offers opportunities for engagement and enrichment beyond the classroom. The University Sports Centre (CUS) serves as an amateur sports association that has been promoting and organizing university sporting activities for over 70 years. Students have access to a variety of sports at affordable rates, both within the center's events and in affiliated sports facilities. Moreover, the university has established a network of relationships and signed agreements with cultural institutions and associations in Milan and other cities. This allows for vibrant cultural exchanges between the academic and local communities, providing students with discounts at museums, theaters, cinemas, and more, further enhancing their educational experience. Through its commitment to research, education, and the holistic development of its students, the University of Milan remains at the forefront of academic excellence and actively contributes to the intellectual, cultural, and social fabric of both Milan and the wider academic community.

details.Description: The University of Mons (UMONS) is a public university located in the Walloon region of Belgium, close to the border with France. It hosts approximately 10,000 students, 25% of them international students, and employs over 1,000 academic and administrative staff. The university is organized into seven faculties and several research institutes, covering a broad range of disciplines. Its relatively small size allows for close interaction between students and faculty, fostering a collaborative academic environment. The university also places emphasis on multilingual education and cross-border cooperation, especially with institutions in neighbouring France. Mons, the city where UMONS is located, is a regional capital with a rich historical background and a growing cultural profile. It is known for its UNESCO-listed belfry, annual festivals, and role as European Capital of Culture in 2015. The city offers a manageable scale and a student-friendly atmosphere, with affordable living costs and accessible public transport. Mons is situated near the French border and is well connected to Brussels and other major European cities, making it a practical base for exploring Belgium and beyond. For students interested in studying in a bilingual and internationally engaged setting, the University of Mons offers a balanced combination of academic focus and regional accessibility.

details.Description: The University of Murcia, founded in its modern form in 1915, is a public institution and the largest university in the Region of Murcia, serving approximately 38,000 students. It offers a wide range of academic disciplines across multiple campuses, including La Merced in the city center and Espinardo to the north. The university is known for its commitment to research, innovation, and regional development, with specialized campuses dedicated to health sciences, sports, and environmental studies. It maintains strong ties with local industries and international partners, and its facilities include research institutes, libraries, and cultural centers. Murcia is a southeastern Spanish city known for its Mediterranean climate, historical architecture, and student-friendly atmosphere. The city offers affordable living, efficient public transport, and a relaxed pace of life, making it well-suited for academic study. Students can explore local markets, festivals, and nearby natural attractions such as the Mar Menor lagoon. A fun fact: Murcia is often called the “Garden of Europe” due to its extensive agricultural production, especially of fruits and vegetables, much of which is exported across the continent.

details.Description: The University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences (BOKU), is a teaching and research center for renewable resources, which are necessary for human life. It is BOKU's objective to help make a considerable contribution to the conservation and protection of resources for future generations by providing diversity in its fields of study. The original campus was built in 1896 in the Türkenschanzpark in Vienna's 18th and 19th districts. details.Description: The university was established in 1949 and supports a community of more than 59,000 students, around 15,000 being international students from 120+ countries. UNSW Sydney is a globally recognised university, ranked among the top 20 worldwide and a leader in research, innovation, and teaching excellence. With over 63,000 students and a vibrant exchange program, UNSW offers a dynamic academic experience enriched by strong industry connections and a global outlook. The university is committed to shaping forward thinking, environmentally conscious and socially engaged students who will make a positive impact in the world. The main UNSW campus is located at Kensington, seven kilometers from the center of Sydney. UNSW Student Life (Arc) offers 3000 clubs to get social, get active and make the most of the time at UNSW. UNSW also has the Aussie Mate Program, where students can join the planned social activities throughout the semester and meet other exchange- and UNSW students. Experience our beautiful campus and see your future at UNSW Sydney (https://www.360tour.unsw.edu.au/)

(https://www.student.unsw.edu.au/calendar/exchange/inbound) NB: From the start of 2028 and onward UNSW will adopt a new academic calendar (https://www.unsw.edu.au/academic-calendar-transition) with a semester structure: Spring (semester 1): February - June Autumn (semester 2): August - November

details.Study load for undergraduate students: 24 units of credit = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Study load for graduate students: 24 units of credit = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Conversion and levels: Study load is calculated according to the level of the specific course. Please note that not all UCPH Master’s (graduate) programmes allow credit transfer of bachelor (undergraduate) courses into their programmes. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: It is not possible to apply for just one term, as you cannot obtain 30 ECTS in one term. It is not possible to begin at UNSW in term 2, as term 2 is only open for continuing students. The following study areas are not available to Exchange students: - Courses in the Doctor of Medicine, UNSW Canberra and the AGSM MBA Program - Arts and Social Sciences: INST, GLST, DANC, EDST and Postgraduate psychology courses - Law: Students are not able to take both LAWS and JURD courses simultaneously - Art and Design: Intensive courses - Business: MARK2999, MARK3999, MARK4999, FINS3100, FINS3200 and MARK6xxx courses and GBAT course Find a comprehensive list here (https://sway.cloud.microsoft/LUMxAzRKDvS7n8nE)

details.Description: The University of Nizwa (UoN) was established in the Sultanate of Oman in 2004 as a faculty governed not-for-profit private university. It is located 140 km from the national capital of Muscat in the interior region of Al-Dakhiliya near the historic former capital of Nizwa. The University seeks to provide a progressive and safe learning environment that is respectful of the traditions and values of the Sultanate. Since its inception, the guiding philosophy of UoN has been to provide students with a high quality education that prepares them to contribute meaningfully to the economic, artistic and aesthetic growth of the country. Graduates, irrespective of their majors, are expected to be capable lifelong learners with skills in numeracy, communications, critical thinking and problem solving. Alumni will possess an appreciation of their culture, values on which it is founded and shared values of humanity in general. In the short time since the inaugural class of 1200 students began taking courses on 16 October 2004 the University has expanded tremendously, both in physical size and in the number and diversity of programs offered to students. At this time the University offers over 30 undergraduate majors and 6 masters programs to a student body of nearly 6500. Construction is underway nearby on a new state of the art campus to support the continued growth of the university and its academic offerings.

Nottingham is organized into five constituent faculties, within which there are more than 50 schools, departments, institutes, and research centers. Nottingham has about 45,500 students from more than 150 countries. The Students' Union hosts over 200 student societies. Choose from hobbies, sports and volunteering. There may be differences in the requirements for a stay of 6 months' duration compared to a stay beyond that period. Warning - if you go on student exchange in the last semester of your master degree, a transcript delay may postpone the completion of your master degree! In urgent cases, UCPH try to obtain confirmation on the validity of a provisional transcript – but we cannot give you any guarantee in advance.

details.Description: The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and largest university, founded in 1811, and today home to around 27,000 students. There are more than 800 courses taught in English across all faculties, making it quite accessible for exchange students. The university is spread across several campuses: the major one is Blindern, but there are additional facilities at places like Ullevål and Tøyen. Oslo, the capital of Norway, offers a unique combination of urban life and natural beauty, making it an attractive destination for students. The city is surrounded by forests and fjords, with outdoor activities like hiking, skiing, and kayaking easily accessible via public transport. Oslo is known for its cultural diversity, vibrant arts scene, and commitment to sustainability. Students can enjoy museums, music festivals, and a lively café culture, all within a compact and walkable city center.
