details.Description: The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and largest university, founded in 1811, and today home to around 27,000 students. There are more than 800 courses taught in English across all faculties, making it quite accessible for exchange students. The university is spread across several campuses: the major one is Blindern, but there are additional facilities at places like Ullevål and Tøyen. Oslo, the capital of Norway, offers a unique combination of urban life and natural beauty, making it an attractive destination for students. The city is surrounded by forests and fjords, with outdoor activities like hiking, skiing, and kayaking easily accessible via public transport. Oslo is known for its cultural diversity, vibrant arts scene, and commitment to sustainability. Students can enjoy museums, music festivals, and a lively café culture, all within a compact and walkable city center.

details.Restrictions: Exchange programme for both bachelor and master level law students. You must take 30 ECTS per semester As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. The first number of the course number code corresponds to the level of the course: 0 = introductory courses, 1-3 = bachelor level, 4-5 = master level, 9 = PhD level.

details.Additional information: The Faculty of Law in Oslo is the oldest and largest educational and research institution within the field of law in Norway. The Faculty of Law in Oslo educates about 75% of all new legal candidates in Norway, and is the studyplace for about 4 200 students. We are divided into six Departments/Centres. The larger part of the Faculty is situated in the classical University buildings in the centre of Oslo. In addition to the traditional fields of study within law, our researchers also explore more modern aspects of law - such as Environmental Law and eCommerce. In addition, the faculty holds a Department of Criminology and Sociology of Law and a Centre for Human Rights. When The Faculty of Law in Copenhagen has nominated you for an exchange place at Oslo University, you have to apply for admission within the application deadlines which may vary a bit from year to year.

details.Description: Nau mai, haere mai ki Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka – a globally recognised university nestled among the natural beauty of New Zealand’s spectacular South Island. The University of Otago is Aotearoa New Zealand’s first university, founded in 1869, and is the top university in the country for educational performance (TEC Educational Performance Indicators). Our Dunedin campus is recognised as one of the world’s most-beautiful campuses, with impressive historic and modern architecture, situated just a short walk from the main city centre. Dunedin is Australasia’s only true student city, offering an unmatched student experience with over 20,000 students living, working, and studying in Dunedin, creating an energy and atmosphere you will only find at Otago. Experience a true “kiwi” student lifestyle in the lively neighbourhoods surrounding campus, living as a community in Uniflats, self-catering flats. Otago is ranked #1 in the country for international student learning, with high student satisfaction rates, and world-class research-led teaching. For the adventure seeking student, experience the duality of study and travel that is highly appealing and accessible in Otago. Join our community of international students from more than 100 countries! Discover the University of Otago through the eyes of our international students! (https://youtu.be/x-UYrcApL00?si=Q7VAGG9kMlXYoJJm)

details.Description: The University of Perpignan Via Domitia (UPVD) is a public institution located in southern France, serving approximately 10,000 students and supported by around 900 academic and administrative staff. It offers a multidisciplinary academic environment and maintains active research centres in areas such as environmental science, law, and social sciences. The university is part of several regional and international networks and supports collaboration with institutions across Europe and the Mediterranean. Its relatively compact size allows for accessible student services and close interaction between students and faculty, contributing to a focused and supportive academic setting. Perpignan is situated near the French-Spanish border, between the Pyrenees mountains and the Mediterranean Sea. The city offers a distinctive regional character shaped by Catalan heritage, with a walkable centre, active cultural calendar, and access to both coastal and inland landscapes. Its location makes it well suited for students interested in exploring southern France and nearby regions, with good transport links to cities such as Montpellier, Toulouse, and Barcelona. The combination of urban amenities and natural surroundings provides a balanced environment for study and everyday life during an exchange semester.

details.Description: The University of Pisa, established in 1343, is one of Italy’s most prestigious public universities, with a long-standing tradition in scientific and humanistic research. It currently hosts over 50,000 students and employs more than 3,000 academic and administrative staff. The university is particularly renowned for its contributions to mathematics, physics, and engineering, and maintains strong ties with national research institutions such as the National Research Council (CNR). A unique aspect of the University of Pisa is its close integration with cutting-edge research facilities, offering students direct access to advanced laboratories and collaborative projects. Situated in the Tuscany region, the city of Pisa offers students a vibrant yet manageable environment, with a rich historical backdrop and easy access to both coastal and inland destinations. The city is well-connected by public transport and lies just an hour from Florence, making it an ideal base for exploring central Italy. Pisa’s compact size and student-centered atmosphere make it easy to navigate and settle into daily life. A fun fact: while the Leaning Tower is its most famous landmark, Pisa is also home to one of world's oldest botanical gardens, founded in 1544, which continues to serve as a research and teaching facility for the university.

A fun fact: while the Leaning Tower is its most famous landmark, Pisa is also home to one of world's oldest botanical gardens, founded in 1544, which continues to serve as a research and teaching facility for the university.

details.Description: The University of Porto, established in 1911, is one of Portugal’s top public research universities and the country’s second largest by enrollment. It serves around 28,000 students, including approximately 11,000 postgraduate students, across 13 faculties, a business school, and a range of specialized institutes, supported by more than 2,300 academic staff. The university offers a wide selection of programs in fields such as economics, management, engineering, law, humanities, science, and the arts, with over 60 bachelor’s degrees, and more than 160 master’s programs. U.Porto’s mission is to create scientific, cultural, and artistic knowledge, to offer advanced education strongly anchored in research, to drive the social and economic value of knowledge, and to actively contribute to the progress of the communities it serves. Its School of Economics and Management is particularly well regarded, fostering close connections with businesses and international institutions and preparing graduates for competitive global careers. Living in Porto as a student means enjoying a vibrant, welcoming city known for its rich culture, historic charm, and affordable lifestyle. The cost of living is relatively low compared to many other Western European cities, with budget-friendly options for food, housing, and public transportation. Porto’s extensive metro, bus, and train networks make it easy to explore, while the atmospheric old town, riverside cafés, music venues, and art spaces add to the lively student experience. University associations organize a wide variety of cultural, sports, and volunteer activities that help students quickly feel part of the community. With friendly locals and easy access to Portugal’s coastline and beautiful northern landscapes, studying in Porto offers a dynamic and fulfilling university life.

The University of Potsdam is an international community with many faces and stories. Its international atmosphere is created by its students from all parts of the world, who decide to study in Potsdam - as well as by the internationally experienced professors and lecturers.

Over 21,500 being international students from 142 countries. Consistently ranked among the world's top universities. The University of Queensland (UQ) offers award-winning teaching, world-class indoor and outdoor learning environments, and outstanding facilities. UQ offers more than 220 clubs and societies spread across the three campuses: the St Lucia campus (https://campuses.uq.edu.au/st-lucia) , the Herston campus (https://campuses.uq.edu.au/herston) , and the Dutton Park campus (https://campuses.uq.edu.au/dutton-park) . UQ staff and students can use a free intercampus bus service that runs between St Lucia and Gatton campuses. Home to 5 of Australia's 11 World Heritage destinations and boasting warm weather all year round, discover why Queensland is the best choice to study and live. Explore what it's like living in Queensland! (https://study.uq.edu.au/university-life/living-in-queensland)

details.Description: The University of Salerno, with origins dating back to the medieval Schola Medica Salernitana, was formally re-established in 1944 and has since grown into a modern academic institution with over 35,000 students. Located in the town of Fisciano, the university operates a large, integrated campus that brings together teaching, research, and student life in one location. It is particularly recognized for its investment in digital infrastructure and sustainability, offering students access to advanced facilities and a well-organized academic environment. Unlike many Italian universities, the University of Salerno is structured as a campus university, which fosters a strong sense of community and makes student services easily accessible. The university is situated in the Campania region, just a short distance from the Amalfi Coast and the city of Salerno. This location offers students a mix of natural beauty, historical sites, and modern urban life. Salerno itself is a lively coastal city with a walkable historic center, a scenic promenade, and regular cultural events. The region is well-connected by public transport, making it easy to explore nearby destinations such as Naples, Pompeii, and Paestum.

details.Description: The University of Salzburg (Paris Lodron University), founded in 1622 and re-established in 1962, is the largest institution of higher education in the province of Salzburg. With approximately 18,000 students and 2,900 staff members across six faculties and 34 departments, it offers a diverse and interdisciplinary academic environment. Exchange students are welcomed into a vibrant international community and can choose from around 90 degree programmes, many of which include English-taught courses. The university’s central location in the historic and culturally rich city of Salzburg—combined with its modern facilities and strong research orientation—makes it an ideal destination for students seeking both academic excellence and an inspiring living experience in the heart of Europe. Salzburg is one of the safest cities in the world, and the University’s excellent student-to-staff ratio provides students with a supportive environment and a wonderful learning culture. The University’s twenty sites are located in and around Salzburg’s historical center, which is a UNESCO listed world heritage site. Situated in the heart of Europe, Salzburg offers fantastic connections to neighbouring countries and to some of Austria’s most beautiful alpine national parks. It is also a culturally vibrant city, home to world-famous performing arts and music festivals. Operating in this setting, the University of Salzburg offers international students and scholars abroad a unique range of experiences.

details.Description: The University of San Diego School of Law is recognized for the excellence of its faculty, depth of its curriculum and strength of its clinical programs. Each year, USD educates approximately 800 Juris Doctor and graduate law students from throughout the United States and around the world. The law school is best known for its offerings in the areas of business and corporate law, constitutional law, intellectual property, international and comparative law, public interest law and taxation. USD School of Law is one of the 84 law schools elected to the Order of the Coif, a national honor society for law school graduates. The law school's faculty is a strong group of outstanding scholars and teachers with national and international reputations and currently ranks in the top 20% (36th out of 204) among U.S. law schools in scholarly impact according to a 2018 study. The school is accredited by the American Bar Association and is a member of the Association of American Law Schools. Founded in 1954, the law school is part of the University of San Diego, a private, independent, Roman Catholic university chartered in 1949.
details.Agreement name: University of San Diego - School of Law

details.Academic calendar: An orientering program is held at the beginning of each semester. Fall semester: Orientation will take place before the start of classes. Classes start around mid-August – with exams in December. Winter semester: Orientation will take place before the start of classes. Classes start within the first week of January – with exams until mid-May.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Applicants must establish competency in English through successful completion of the TOEFL exam (minimum 93 on iBT) or the IELTS exam (minimum 7.0). The language test result must be sent directly from TOEFL or IELTS institute to the host university.
details.Restrictions: Law students must follow a full study load of min. 12 credits which correspond to 30 ECTS per semester. Be aware that credit requirements may be different for other exchange students at San Diego School of Law.
details.Course information: Exchange students are required to enroll in one mandatory course: Introduction to U.S. Law (worth 2 credits); when you apply for pre-approval of courses you can also apply for this course as part of your full study load of 12 credits. Courses: Students may select their remaining courses from an approved list provided by the academic advisor, which is comprised of graduate level courses from the School of Law curriculum. Generally, it is possible to change course choices in the beginning of the semester. Most courses are taught using the socratic method, meaning students are expected to actively participate in class discussions and cold calling may be used. It is mandatory to come to class, in contrary to Denmark.

details.Housing: Housing: Many exchange students choose to live off-campus, either within walking distance to the campus or in nearby beach neighbourhoods which are approximately ten minutes from campus by car. On-campus housing is extremely limited and may not be available for exchange students. Later in the process, exchange students interested in living on campus should contact the USD Housing Office to determine whether on-campus housing is available.

details.Additional information: Visa requirements: Exchange students must demonstrate access to sufficient funds to cover their living expenses, during their time in the United States (expect approx. $ 17,000 or more). San Diego School of Law will provide additional information about this in their admission process. Insurance: All students must either (1) demonstrate access to sufficient international health insurance; or (2) sign a promissory note which confirms their intent to purchase the USD provided health insurance upon their arrival. In addition to a possible mandatory insurance at your host university, UCHP recommends that Danish students on an exchange programme take out an insurance coverage with a Danish insurance company to make sure that you are sufficiently covered especially when talking about possible need for home transportation to DK or possible coverage during your activities and trips outside the campus area of your host university. details.Description: At the Brazilian postgraduate level, the so-called stricto sensu postgraduate programs are divided into two levels: mestrado (master's degree) and doutorado (doctoral/PhD degree). These programs may differ in structure from those offered abroad. Therefore, international students enrolled in subjects whose curricula at their home institutions are structured differently, such as Bologna second-cycle (Master's) degrees, are highly recommended to attend courses at USP preferably at the undergraduate level.

The Ribeirão Preto School of Economics, Administration, and Accounting (Faculdade de Economia e Administração de Ribeirão Preto – FEARP) requires applicants to enroll in a number of subjects that correspond to at least 16 credits. The School of Architecture and Urbanism (Faculdade de Arquitetura e Urbanismo – FAU) and the School of Economics, Business, and Accountancy (Faculdade de Economia, Administração, Contabilidade e Atuária – FEA) receive a large number of applications each semester and have limited capacity to admit all exchange students. Please refer to their Local International Offices before nominating students/applying. It is highly recommended that students intending to apply for the above-mentioned schools consider the possibility of applying to other schools as well.
details.Important links: Website (https://www5.usp.br/#english) Academic Calendar (https://uspdigital.usp.br/mundus/jupCalendario2022.jsp?codmnu=10755)
details.Housing:
There are no accommodation options for exchange students within the
campuses. Search for accommodation must be carried out by the students
themselves, according to their economic conditions and interests. USP
strongly recommends that students take part in the USP iFriends program (http://www.usp.br/internationaloffice/en/index.php/usp-ifriends) in order to get more information about accommodation. Applicants may
opt to take part in the buddy program when filling out the online
application form.
details.Scholarships:
Students applying for this university are automatically considered for KU’s Internationalisation
scholarship.
details.Additional information: To be eligible for a KU exchange spot, students must have completed at least one year of study (equivalent to 60 ECTS) by the time they apply for admission to the host university. This must be documented on their transcript by the time of applying to the host university. First-year bachelor students should note that applications to the host university are submitted before the start of each semester — typically between March and April for the autumn semester and between September and November for the spring semester. First-year master's students are considered to meet this requirement based on their completed bachelor's degree.

details.Description: It is possible to apply for an exchange abroad to the University of Sheffield for an entire academic year. This agreement allows for enrolment in undergraduate modules only. MA-students from the University of Copenhagen considering Univeristy of Sheffield must make sure that they can get approval from their faculty to transfer undergraduate (bachelor) modules from this university into their MA-programmes at UCPH. MA-students from the Faculty of Humanities should note that they will not be considered for this agreement, as they cannot get undergraduate modules from this university transfered into their MA-programmes at UCPH.
details.Academic calendar: Typical semester dates Autumn Semester - September to February Spring Semester - February to June Click here for current semester dates (https://sheffield.ac.uk/about/dates/current-and-future-semester)
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: All students studying at the University of Sheffield not from a majority English speaking country are required to provide evidence of their English language proficiency in their application. This includes students who will be studying for a single semester.
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 60 credits per semester. Please note: Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: Courses not open for exchange students going to Sheffield on this agreement: All courses in Health Science (including Medicine and Veterinary Medicine).
details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . As a result, students applying for exchange places in the UK cannot be guaranteed an Erasmus+ grant at the time of application. Eligibility for Erasmus+ funding will depend on whether the host university joins the programme and concludes an Erasmus+ agreement with the University of Copenhagen. Students nominated to a UK university will be informed of their grant eligibility no later than March 2027.
details.Housing: Students can apply online for University owned accommodation once they have received their applicant number. University housing is only guaranteed for students studying in Sheffield for the full academic year. Students can also apply for private sector housing if they prefer. www.sheffield.ac.uk/accommodation

details.Description:
The university was founded in 1956 and support a community of almost 50,000 students. USF is
situated in the vibrant and diverse Tampa Bay region with campuses in Tampa, St. Petersburg
and Sarasota-Manatee. USF Intercollegiate Athletics is home to 17 men's and women's teams,
including football, basketball, baseball, softball and soccer, competing at the NCAA level.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: August-December Spring semester: January-May Please note that the spring semester begins very early compared to the spring semester at UCPH. You should only apply for the spring semester, if you do not have exams in January at UCPH.
details.GPA for graduate admission: 9 (Danish scale) - please note that when applying for graduate level in the US you have to fulfill the grade requirement from the department at your host university. Each department has their own grade requirement for graduate level students - and it is often very high - at least above 9  but more often between 10 and 12.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: TOEFL-test: 79
details.Restrictions: The agreement is primarily open for undergraduate students, except undergraduate Law Students. Getting accepted at graduate level and getting courses at graduate level is harder and requires a much higher GPA (at least 10, but preferably closer to 12) Psychology, Computer Engineering/Science, Media and Broadcasting courses in Mass Communications, Accounting courses and some selected special program courses are not available to exchange students as well as Law courses. Restricted courses: Nursing, Pharmacy, Honors College, Real Estate, and Accounting. Departmental review at USF required: Chemistry, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Music, and Education
details.Important links: Website for Incoming Exchange (https://www.usf.edu/orientation/international/) Program Discovery (https://educationabroad.global.usf.edu/index.cfm?FuseAction=Programs.ProgramDiscovery)
details.Housing:
The Housing and Meal Plan Applications must be completed as soon as possible upon
notification of acceptance. If you plan to apply for on-campus housing, you must obtain the
Meningitis and Hepatitis vaccines and submit the confirmation as part of your Health History
Form to USF to be considered for housing.
details.Scholarships:
Students applying for this university are automatically considered for KU’s Internationalisation
scholarship.
details.Additional information: Fall semester applicants: If you want to apply for the fall semester at this university, you need to apply in the first application round (with deadline in November), as this is the only time fall semester spots will be offered

details.Description: You may apply for an exchange abroad to the University of Southampton for either a single semester or a full academic year. This agreement allows for enrolment in undergraduate and postgraduate modules.
details.Academic calendar: Semester 1 (autumn semester): late-September – late-January Semester 2 (spring semester): late-January - late-June Term dates (https://www.southampton.ac.uk/about/term-dates)
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: CEFR level B2, IELTS overall score of 6.5 or an equivalent standard in other qualifications Component scores for individual language competencies may vary according to programme. English language entry requirements (https://www.southampton.ac.uk/studentadmin/admissions/admissions-policies/language.page)
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 30 ECTS or 60 CATS (Southampton credits) Please note: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Study load for graduate students: 30 ECTS or 60 CATS (Southampton credits) Please note: Full year: Conversion is not applicable for full year stays at this university. Study load requirement is higher when transferring credits corresponding to a full academic year. Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: Courses not open for exchange students: All courses in Health Sciences, Medicine and the Faculty of Engineering and Physical Sciences. Study areas included in this agreement: Faculty of Arts and Humanities History English Language and Literature Film Studies Archaeology Modern Languages and Linguistics Music (excluding Performance modules) Philosophy Graphic Design Fine Art Game Design Fashion Design/Textile Design Faculty of Social Sciences Law Southampton Business School (including Finance and Marketing) Mathematics Economics Social Sciences (including Sociology, Criminology and Social Statistics) Politics and International Relations Education Faculty of Environmental and Life Sciences Psychology Geography and Environmental Science Ocean and Earth Sciences Biological Sciences
details.Important links: Website for incoming exchange (https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/exchanges/come-to-southampton.page) Course finder (https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses)
details.Housing: Southampton can offer accommodation for Semester 1 and Semester 2 provided students apply by 1. August at the latest for accommodation for Semester 1 (autumn start) and by 1. December for accommodation for Semester 2 (Spring start). In the case where University accommodation cannot be provided, support will be given to find private alternatives. Please read more on this website (https://www.southampton.ac.uk/student-life/accommodation) .
details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . Eligibility for Erasmus+ funding will depend on whether the host university joins the programme and concludes an Erasmus+ agreement with the University of Copenhagen. Students nominated to a UK university will be informed of their grant eligibility no later than March 2027.

details.Description: University of South-Eastern Norway is a well-rounded university that serves around 18,000 students, spread across eight campuses. USN was founded following the merger of a number of former university colleges, on January 1st 2016. It offers a wide array of programmes and has courses in both English And Norwegian. The locations of USN’s campuses provide a unique blend of student life, accessibility and natural surroundings. The surrounding region features scenic landscapes, forests, lakes and smaller towns. Many of the towns where USN is based are compact and quite walkable. Public transit is generally reliable and gives access to Oslo and other hubs.
details.Agreement name: University of South-Eastern Norway - Erasmus - Nordlys
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Academic calendar: Autumn semester: mid August to mid December Spring semester: January to mid June Academic calendar (https://www.usn.no/english/newstudents/academic-calendar)

details.Study load: 30 ECTS
details.Important links: Page explaining the campuses (https://www.usn.no/om-usn/campusene) Main site for exchange students (https://www.usn.no/getfile.php/13860235-1750678943/usn.no/en/For%20partners/USN%20FACT%20SHEET%20Januar%202025.pdf) English course catalogue (https://www.usn.no/english/academics/find-programmes)

details.Scholarships: Students applying for this university are automatically nominated for the Erasmus+ scholarship.

details.Academic calendar: Semester 1: Martinmas semester (autumn semester): September – December Semester 2: Candlemas semester (spring semester): January – May
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Accepted proof of language proficiency depends on the study area you are applying for: Faculty: English language requirements profile: Arts and Divinity (all Schools except the School of English) Profile 3-D (https://www.st-andrews.ac.uk/subjects/entry/language-requirements/profiles/#d.en.105748) Arts and Divinity (School of English) Profile 1-D (https://www.st-andrews.ac.uk/subjects/entry/language-requirements/profiles/#d.en.105639) Science Profile 7-D (https://www.st-andrews.ac.uk/subjects/entry/language-requirements/profiles/#d.en.105830) OBS: TOEFL iBT Home Edition, PTE Academic Online, and the online version of the LanguageCert International ESOL, will not be accepted as evidence of English language proficiency.
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 60 credits Please note: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Study load for graduate students: 60 credits per semester. Please note: Full year: Conversion is not applicable for full year stays at this university. details.Restrictions: Not open for exchange students: Faculty of Medicine
details.Important links: Website for incoming exchange (https://www.st-andrews.ac.uk/study-abroad/at-st-andrews/) Course catalogue (https://www.st-andrews.ac.uk/study-abroad/at-st-andrews/studies/)
details.Housing: Please read about accommodation and how to apply here (https://www.st-andrews.ac.uk/study-abroad/at-st-andrews/applying/accommodation/)

details.Description: The University of Stavanger is a mid-size public research university with around 13,000 students. It offers a wide range of programmes through its six main faculties covering most disciplines. While Norwegian is the main language of instruction, many courses especially at the master’s level are taught in English. Stavanger is a lively, coastal city in southwest Norway, combining urban amenities with nearby natural beauty. The Ullandhaug campus is about a 12-minute bus ride from the city centre, making it fairly accessible, and there are also good cycling options and public buses that connect campuses and residential areas. In your free time you can explore fjords, beaches, hiking paths, forests nearby, and enjoy cafés, shops and cultural events in Stavanger itself.
details.Academic calendar: Autumn semester: mid August to mid December Spring semester: from January to June Academic calendar (https://www.uis.no/en/student-pages/academic-calendar)
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: It is not required to take a language test to be admitted to either English or Norwegian courses, but a good level of either is expected.
details.Restrictions: You may request courses across different faculties and departments. Master's level courses are not available to Bachelor students. To be able to sign up for a course, you must fulfill any prerequisites.
details.Important links: Main site for exchange students (https://www.uis.no/en/studies/collaboration/inbound-exchange) Course catalogue (https://www.uis.no/en/studies/collaboration/courses-offered-to-inbound-exchange-students)
details.Housing: International students will be given a housing application code upon registration of study application. You should use this given code to apply for student housing. Housing is not guaranteed. Link to housing page (https://www.uis.no/en/student/accommodation)
details.Scholarships:
Students applying for this university are automatically nominated for the Erasmus+
scholarship

details.Description: The University of Strasbourg is a public research university located in Strasbourg, Alsace, France, with over 52,000 students. The French university traces its history to the earlier German-language Universität Straßburg, which was founded in 1538, and was divided in the 1970s into three separate institutions: Louis Pasteur University, Marc Bloch University, and Robert Schuman University. In 2009, the fusion of these three universities reconstituted a united University of Strasbourg.
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Academic calendar: First semester/autumn: September - January Second semester/spring: January - May
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: In general, visiting French universities require a high level of French. Often, lectures are conducted in French even if the language of instruction is suppposed to be in English. In accordance with the European self-assessment CEFR-grid (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) : Level B1 in French is mandatory Level B2 in French is strongly recommended A few degree programmes are taught partly in English. However, you still need to have sufficient fluency in written and spoken French to fully cope with your courses.
details.Course information: At info for incoming exchange students (https://ecogestion.unistra.fr/international/incoming-exchange-students/) - you can find detailed course information at the headline 'Courses/cours' - click on arrows for: Autumn semester courses ... Spring semester courses ... The majority of courses are taught in French - although a limited number of courses are taught in English. NB: If you are a bachelor student, you can enroll in one master course. However, access to this course has to be agreed on by the teachers.
details.Important links: See homepage of the University of Strasbourg (https://en.unistra.fr/) See info on welcome days (https://www.unistra.fr/fr/agenda/2026/accueil-des-etudiants-internationaux) See info on university sports (https://sport.unistra.fr/fr/) See info on Carte Culture (https://carte-culture.org/)
details.Housing: International students are eligible to apply for accommodation in a university hall of residence although you cannot be guaranteed anything.
details.Scholarships: Students applying for this university are automatically considered for the Erasmus+ grant.

details.Description: The University of Sydney is a world-leading institution committed to academic excellence and groundbreaking research. As Australia’s first university, it offers a rich tradition of innovation and intellectual discovery across a broad spectrum of disciplines. Exchange students benefit from access to inspiring teaching, state-of-the-art facilities, and a supportive learning environment designed to help you reach your full potential. With a strong global outlook and vibrant campus life, the University of Sydney fosters connections that extend far beyond the classroom, enriching your academic journey and future career. Studying in Sydney provides an unparalleled lifestyle experience that complements your academic pursuits. With a student community of over 70,000 individuals, the university offers a diverse and welcoming environment where you can connect with peers from all over the world. Sydney itself is a thriving global city, known for its iconic landmarks, stunning beaches, and vibrant cultural scene. On campus, you’ll find more than 200 student clubs and societies spanning interests from sports and arts to academic and cultural groups, providing endless opportunities to engage, grow, and make lasting friendships. This dynamic blend of city life and campus community ensures your exchange experience will be as enriching personally as it is academically. Hear about the USyd exchange experience! (https://youtu.be/JnMKWka1jg0?si=RDUNA1Ozd9Og4Ffi)
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Academic calendar: Spring (Semester 1): February – June Autumn (Semester 2): July - November
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: You must provide ONE of the following: TOEFL 85 IELTS score 6.5 with no bands below 6.0 Studentereksamen: Grade 7 at Level A or Grade 10 at Level B (year grades). There is a 10-year time limit for the studentereksamen to the date you commence a study abroad or exchange program. Studentereksamen: passed Level A + signed CEFR form from UCPH Some faculties may have higher language requirements for undergraduate and post graduate students Find more information here. (https://www.sydney.edu.au/study/how-to-apply/international-students/english-language-requirements.html)
details.Restrictions: Postgraduate Medicine, Dentistry & Psychology are not open to exchange students. Law, Veterinary Science and Media & Communications are open to students enrolled in those specific degrees only. Areas with specific requirements, fx prerequisite requirements: - Accounting (ACCT units) and Business Law (CLAW units) - Information Systems (INFS units) - Marketing (postgraduate – MKTG5000 and higher units) - Operations Management and Econometrics (QBUS units) - Social Work (SCWK units) - and all units taught by the following faculties: Health Sciences and Veterinary Science
details.Important links: Study Abroad & Exchange Guide (https://www.sydney.edu.au/content/dam/corporate/documents/study/study-abroad/study-abroad-inbound-guide.pdf) Course Catalogue (https://www.sydney.edu.au/study/study-options/study-abroad-at-sydney.html) (see 'Available study units' toward bottom of the page) International Student page (https://www.sydney.edu.au/study/international-students.html) Key dates (https://www.sydney.edu.au/students/key-dates.html)
details.Housing: Study Abroad and Exchange students are each guaranteed accommodation at one of our preferred providers: Urbanest, Queen Mary Building (QMB) and the residential colleges. See more information here. (https://www.sydney.edu.au/study/accommodation.html)

details.Academic calendar: Because you will be participating in clinical rotations, you will not necessarily follow the normal semester structure. The start date depends on when the different rotations are offered, and when you want to start your exchange.
details.Study plan: Only for students who are planning an alternative differentiation. Read more about alternative differentiation. (https://kunet.ku.dk/studie/veterinaermedicin-ka/Sider/Emne.aspx?topic=Alternativ%20differentiering&topicId=2476576e-edcf-4a26-aff2-69155b608b4f#2476576e-edcf-4a26-aff2-69155b608b4f)
details.Course information: You will participate in clinical rotations for 8-12 weeks. Each clinic week equates to 1.5 ECTS credits. You can choose between rotations at the three university hospitals: The University Veterinary Teaching Hospital Sydney (UVTHS) The University Veterinary Teaching Hospital Camden (UVTHC) The Avian, Reptile and Exotic Pet Hospital Camden (AREPH) Find information about the rotations in the University of Sydney’s course catalogue. (https://www.sydney.edu.au/courses/courses/pc/doctor-of-veterinary-medicine.html)
details.Important links: On campus you will be able to participate in various sports activities and clubs. Read more about campus life. (https://sydney.edu.au/campus-life.html) The University of Sydney requires that veterinary students are vaccinated against Q fever before they can participate in clinical training. You must therefore arrive in Australia two weeks before the teaching starts, so you can be vaccinated. The vaccine costs AUD 255 (approx. DKK 1,300). The vaccine against Q fever is not available in Denmark. Read more about Q fever (https://www.sydney.edu.au/students/animal-veterinary-science-vaccinations.html%20) What do other students say about studying abroad? (https://kunet.ku.dk/studie/sider/RedirectToTopic.aspx?topicId=334b090d-9838-4acd-a023-68b0aff97107)
details.Housing: In principle, the University of Sydney offers accommodation for international students. You apply for accommodation after you have applied for admission as an exchange student. However, in our experience it is very difficult to find accommodation via the university because of the short duration of the stay. So you should be prepared to look for accommodation yourself – which can be both expensive and difficult. Read more about accommodation via the University of Sydney. (https://sydney.edu.au/campus-life/accommodation.html)
details.Scholarships: UCPH offers two grants for studies abroad. UCPH’s internationalisation grant (https://kunet.ku.dk/studie/sider/RedirectToTopic.aspx?topicId=37a24826-2020-4b3a-ab0a-2b697f9c8118) The Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences’ outgoing mobility grant (https://kunet.ku.dk/studie/sider/RedirectToTopic.aspx?topicId=5277ace7-ec89-4541-89a0-834301563450) You will automatically apply for an internationalisation grant when you are nominated for an exchange place but you must actively apply for the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences’ Outgoing Mobility Grant. You can also apply for funding from private foundations and grants. Read more under Foundations and Grants on Study Information (https://kunet.ku.dk/studie/medicin-ka/Sider/Emne.aspx?topic=Fonde%20og%20legater&topicId=c4df78e7-cb36-42f3-8ea9-bdddf2dfe57e#c4df78e7-cb36-42f3-8ea9-bdddf2dfe57e)

As Australia’s first university, it offers a rich tradition of innovation and intellectual discovery across a broad spectrum of disciplines. Exchange students benefit from access to inspiring teaching, state-of-the-art facilities, and a supportive learning environment designed to help you reach your full potential. With a strong global outlook and vibrant campus life, the University of Sydney fosters connections that extend far beyond the classroom, enriching your academic journey and future career. Studying in Sydney provides an unparalleled lifestyle experience that complements your academic pursuits. With a student community of over 70,000 individuals, the university offers a diverse and welcoming environment where you can connect with peers from all over the world. Sydney itself is a thriving global city, known for its iconic landmarks, stunning beaches, and vibrant cultural scene. On campus, you’ll find more than 200 student clubs and societies spanning interests from sports and arts to academic and cultural groups, providing endless opportunities to engage, grow, and make lasting friendships. This dynamic blend of city life and campus community ensures your exchange experience will be as enriching personally as it is academically. Hear about the USyd exchange experience! (https://youtu.be/JnMKWka1jg0?si=RDUNA1Ozd9Og4Ffi)

To account for their BA-thesis, students on this agreement must follow "PHAR4913 – Pharmacy Honours". The structure of PHAR4913 is: 4 small written assignments (5% each) – aimed at getting the students started early with the writing process 1 supervisor assessment (engagement) 5% Poster presentation and Q&A session 15% Written thesis 60% Academic staff at Sydney Pharmacy School will contact UCPH-students after enrollment and try to match a fitting project and supervisor to their research interest. details.Description:
Estonia, in North-Eastern Europe, is home to the Johan Skytte Institute of Political Studies at the
University of Tartu. The institute itself is located in the heart of Estonia's second largest town,
Tartu, which is home to around one hundred thousand people. The town's long university
traditions and academically oriented environment laid the foundation for the strong principles
of the Skytte Institute. Our focus areas are English
linguistics and CLIL (Content language integrate learning method), youth work, Teaching Russian
as a foreign language and IT.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: Late August to end of January Winter semester: Early February until late June An orientation course (https://ut.ee/en/orientation-course) is offered at the beginning of each semester See additional information in the academic calendar on: https://oigus.ut.ee/en/study-regulations-and-guidelines (https://oigus.ut.ee/en/study-regulations-and-guidelines)
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Classes are taught in English for international students. A good knowledge of English is essential for studying at University of Tartu as an exchange student. Therefore, a language confirmation is required confirming that you have sufficient language qualifications corresponding to min. level B2 in the self-assessment CEFR-grid (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) . You can apply for a language confirmation from the Faculty of Law in Copenhagen and the confirmation will be based on your grades in English from your ‘studentereksamen’ or HF diploma. A language confirmation will only be needed after you have been nominated to the exchange programme at the University of Tartu.
details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student, you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad.
details.Course information: Generally, all law courses have the value between 3 - 6 ECTS. See link to course descriptions below under 'Important links'. Apply for pre-approval of courses: When you have received confirmation from UCPH about an exchange place at the University of Tartu, you must apply for pre-approval of the courses you intend to take as an exchange student. The processing time for applications of pre-approval of courses may take 4-6 weeks in Cph. The pre-approval of your courses have to be completed before you can obtain a signed learning agreement (containing your course titles) which has to be uploaded in your application for admission in mid-April.
details.Important links: See link to courses taught in English (https://ois2.ut.ee/#/courses) insert 'Law' (as an element in your search criteria), do also insert additional sortering criteria like the academic year and and also info in 'detailed search'. details.Additional information: The University of Tartu is situated in southeast Estonia - approx. 2 hours and 40 minutes by bus  from the capital city Talinn. The School of Law is part of one of the four oldest faculties of the University of Tartu (UT), i.e. Faculty of Social Sciences. However, lawyers have been educated there ever since the university was founded in 1632. As the only university in Estonia liable for teaching and developing teaching activities in the field of law, The School of Law ensures the training of highly qualified lawyers and to make sure that research and development is undertaken in all areas of Estonian law. School of Law incorporates the bulk of Estonia’s legal research potential and actively participates in shaping Estonia’s legal policy. A buddy programme is offered at UT. When the Faculty of Law in Copenhagen has nominated you for an exchange place at University of Tartu, you have to apply for admission within the application deadlines which may vary a bit from year to year.

details.Description: The university was founded in 1846 and supports a community of more than 35,000 students, 7,000 being international students from all over the world. Become an exchange student at the University of Tasmania and take advantage of Tasmania's unique and stunning environment. With 45% of our island State being National Park or World Heritage listed, it is no wonder that some of Tasmania's most breathtaking destinations, including Cradle Mountain and Tasman National Park, feature prominently in the Lonely Planet's 1000 Ultimate Adventures Guide. Stunning beaches to surf, mountains to climb and rivers to raft, Tasmania the home of the Tassie Devil and the gateway to Antarctica will become your living playground, with the university being the epicentre of your state-sized class room. With exceptional teaching staff excelling in areas including Zoology, Geography and Environmental studies, Marine and Antarctic science, Law, Aboriginal studies, Journalism and Media, combined with Summer rock concerts, Winter festivals and an art and cafe scene that will 'knock your socks off', the University of Tasmania can offer you an inspirational and diverse study experience, both enriching academically, socially, culturally and environmentally. details.Description: In 1988, the former New South Wales Institute of Technology, founded in 1964, became the University of Technology Sydney. UTS is one of the largest universities in Australia with a total enrolment of over 45,000+ students. Study in award-winning labs and collaborative classrooms and work with the tools and technologies that are shaping your industry. Each year we welcome more than 1000 study abroad and exchange students from around the world – just like you. With students from 120 different countries, UTS is an exciting place to be! The main campus, City Campus, is located right next to Central station and Victoria Park. UTS is part of the Australian Technology Network of universities: a group of five prominent universities committed to working with industry and government to deliver practical and professional courses. See what it is like studying abroad at the University of Technology Sydney (https://www.utsstudyabroad.com/)

details.Restrictions: U.S. Constitutional Law for Foreign Lawyers: All exchange students are required to take this 2-credit course to build a strong foundation for their legal studies at Texas Law. Class schedule: Exchange students will be sent a list of approved courses before orientation. They are not permitted to take 1L-only required courses or courses with prerequisites. https://law.utexas.edu/courses/?page=all (https://law.utexas.edu/courses/?page=all) Clinics: Exchange students are permitted to take the following clinics: Actual Innocence, Capital Punishment (prerequisite: Capital Punishment course must be taken concurrently or have been taken previously), Civil Rights, Disability Rights, Entrepreneurship & Community Development, Environmental, Human Rights, Immigration, Law & Religion, and Transnational Worker Rights. All clinics require an application. Exchange students will be sent an email when the application opens. Student need to pay some fees as exchange students at UT Austin: Fee bill (2022): Created after course registration at orientation. Includes the following fees: (1) Mandatory UT Student Health Insurance Plan (https://global.utexas.edu/isss/advising-services/insurance/costs), (2) $125 International Student and Scholar Services fee, and (3) $10 UT Student ID card fee. Must be paid by the 4th class day or classes will be dropped. Orientation: Orientation is mandatory. Orientation sessions will cover logistics and programming, classroom skills, curriculum and course selection, group advising, Intro to U.S. Law, Law School tour, Intro to Legal Research, Tarlton Library Tour, Pro Bono, Intro to U.S. Legal Writing, Intro to Common Law Principles, journals and student orgs presentations, etc. Class attendance: Regular and punctual attendance is required in all courses, and faculty members may adopt more specific attendance policies. Listening at a later time to a recorded class session is not a substitute for attendance.Because attendance is required, registration for courses that meet at the same time or at overlapping times is not permitted. https://law.utexas.edu/student-affairs/academic-services/policies-andprocedures/ attendance/#:~:text=Regular%20and%20punctual%20attendance%20is,not%20a%20substitute%20for%20attendance.

details.Description: The University of the Faroe Islands is a small but respected institution with about 1000 students. The university offers programs and courses mainly in Faroese and Danish, with some courses available in English. Its size and focus on regional issues provide a distinctive opportunity to study topics related to sustainability, marine resources, and the arctic region. The university is located in Tórshavn, the capital of the Faroe Islands, a small and charming city that combines traditional Nordic character with modern conveniences. The city is compact and quite hilly and offers a warm and friendly atmosphere. Surrounded by stunning cliffs, green valleys, and the open sea, the city provides easy access to hiking trails and breathtaking nature, making it a perfect setting for students who enjoy the outdoors.

details.Description: The University of the Pacific, McGeorge School of Law has grown into an internationally recognized leader in the field of legal education since its establishment in 1924. Its location in Sacramento, the capital of California, has shaped its focus on public law, international law and advocacy. Our success is built on a distinguished faculty, high quality students, committed and involved alumni, and a beautiful, spacious campus with state-of-the art classrooms and student facilities. Yet it is also built on vision. McGeorge is an institution on the move, a dynamic law school that is changing and growing to meet the challenges of the global economy and to educate the lawyers who will be tomorrow’s leaders.
details.Agreement name: University of the Pacific - McGeorge School of Law in Sacramento
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Academic calendar: Exchange students can choose between Fall and Spring, although most exchange students come in the Fall. Fall semester: Starts in mid August – with exams in December before Christmas. Spring semester: Starts in early January – with exams until mid/late May See additional info in the academic calendar (https://www.mcgeorge.edu/students/academics/calendars-and-schedules) . An orientation programme is offered each semester a few days before the classes begin. With a student exchange in the spring semester be aware that classes may start in early January. Generally, at American universities class attendance is mandatory. Careful planning is required when you select courses (exams) for the preceding fall semester in Copenhagen – in order to avoid that your presence is not required at two places at the same time.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: At McGeorge School of Law all courses are taught in English. Students should be able to study law fluently in English, both orally and in writing. You can fulfill the language requirement with a language confirmation from the University of Copenhagen. The language confirmation will be based on your grades in English from your ‘studentereksamen’ or HF diploma and it will exempt you from other language requirements. A language confirmation will only be needed after you have been nominated to the exchange programme, where you can retrieve it in Mobility Online. Without a Danish ‘studentereksamen’ or ‘HF-bevis’ McGeorge will require a TOEFL test. See language test requirements for undergraduate students (https://www.pacific.edu/admission/undergraduate/test-scores) .
details.Restrictions: Law students must follow a full study load of min. 12 credits which correspond to 30 ECTS per semester. Be aware that credit requirements may be different for other exchange students at McGeorge School of Law.
details.Course information: See info on law course offers below at 'Important links'. ‘Legal English’ (1 credit) is a mandatory course for international exchange students; when you apply for pre-approval of courses you can also apply for this course as part of your full study load of 12 credits. The style of teaching is based on the socratic method, meaning students are expected to actively participate in class discussions and cold calling may be used.

details.Additional information: Address: Sacramento Campus 3200 Fifth Ave. Sacramentto, CA 95817 The University is situated in the State of California. Distance to San Francisco approx. 2.5 hours by train. McGeorge School of Law is a rather small law school like many others in the US (with approx. 600 law students). You may expect a rather small group of law exchange students. Visa requirements: If you are not a U.S. citizen, a J-1 visa is required for entry to the USA. As an exchange student you must demonstrate access to sufficient funds to cover your living expenses, during the time in the United States. McGeorge School of Law will provide additional information about this in the admission process. Insurance: In addition to a possible mandatory insurance at your host university, UCHP recommends that Danish students on an exchange programme take out an insurance coverage with a Danish insurance company to make sure that you are sufficiently covered especially when talking about possible need for home transportation to DK or possible coverage during your activities and trips outside the campus area of your host university. Additional costs: Although tuition fee is waived for exchange students, you are still responsible for paying the fees below: University’s student bar association, $50 Student wellness, and $165 Mandatory health insurance fees $1,793 The fees are subject to future changes. In some instances, the health insurance may be waived if you have comparable insurance that meets the University requirements.

details.Description:
The University of Tokyo, also known as "Todai" was established in 1877 as the first
national university in Japan. As a leading research university, Todai offers courses in
essentially all academic disciplines at both undergraduate and graduate levels and
conducts research across the full spectrum of academic activity. The university aims
to provide its students with a rich and varied academic environment that ensures
opportunities for both intellectual development and the acquisition of professional
knowledge and skills.
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester : September/October to March* (transcripts are issued in April) Spring semester : April to August/September* (transcripts are issued in September) *The actual period of study (including examination periods) varies depending on the College/Faculty. Academic Calendar (u-tokyo.ac.jp) (https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/current-students/university_calendar.html) Important! UTokyo usually issues transcripts in September (after Spring exchange) and in April (after Fall exchange), which is later than other universities. Please make sure this will not conflict with your subsequent plans, particularly if the exchange is in your final semester of your bachelor's degree, as this will affect the timing of your credit transfer.
details.GPA for graduate admission: 7 Please check the minimum GPA requirement and other conditions set by each graduate school: Prerequisites for USTEP Type G Applicants (u-tokyo.ac.jp) (https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/content/400229952.pdf) . If there is no specified GPA requirement for the graduate school you intend to apply for, please note that University of Tokyo prefers students with a higher GPA and excellent academic performance.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: Type U (For Undergraduate) - English: A minimum TOEFL iBT score of 90, IELTS 6.5, Cambridge "C1 Advanced", or DET 120 and/or - Japanese: JLPT N1 Students who wish to take courses taught in Japanese need JLPT Level N1. The different departments may have different requirements for the minimum level. Students who want to take courses taught in Japanese should check very early in the application process when there are available test dates for the JLPT in Denmark. There may only be 2 annual tests (typically December and July). It can be necessary to sign up for a test before you know, whether you have been awarded an exchange spot at University of Tokyo to make sure that you will have the test result in time for the application deadline at University of Tokyo. Type G (For Graduate): Graduate students must refer to the language requirement for the graduate school they wish to apply to: Prerequisites for USTEP Type G Applicants (u-tokyo.ac.jp) (https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/content/400229952.pdf)
details.Study load for graduate students: 8 credits = 30 ECTS Please note that not all UCPH Master’s (graduate) programmes allow credit transfer of bachelor (undergraduate) courses into their programmes.
details.Restrictions: First and second year undergraduate students are not accepted for USTEP. For students enrolled in three-year undergraduate programs, they must have finished at least 1.5-year (3 semesters) of their degree programme at the time of their arrival at UTokyo. Students are advised to check the course catalogue about which language their preferred courses are taught in. Type G applicants must in addition to the general requirements also meet the conditions set by the Graduate School they intend to apply for: Prerequisites for USTEP Type G Applicants (u-tokyo.ac.jp) (https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/content/400229952.pdf)
details.Course information: Exchange students can apply to the USTEP Type U (undergraduate) or USTEP Type G (graduate) program depending on their purpose of participation and/or their proficiency in the English and/or Japanese language. Type U is designed for undergraduate students to take various courses given in English and/or Japanese in the various Faculties/College in accordance with their English and/or Japanese language proficiency. Type G is designed for graduate students. Type G participants will belong to one of the Graduate Schools to which they are admitted and will be able to take various courses or conduct research under the guidance of a faculty advisor. Type G is only open to graduate students. Important information for graduate students: Type G applicants are expected to submit a detailed and well-developed study plan to UTokyo, ensuring that it is well aligned with the course offerings of the intended Graduate School and the research expertise of the department and faculty member(s). Failure to do so may result in rejection. Graduate students should only apply for this agreement, if they are able to develop an excellent study plan that meets the expectations described above, or if they are able to obtain a pre-approval of undergraduate courses abroad as part of their graduate degree program at UCPH, in which case, they should consider applying as Type U exchange students.

The University of Toronto was founded in 1827 and supports a community of over 90,000
graduate- and undergraduate students. UofT has three campuses: St. George (UTSG),
Mississauga (UTM) and Scarborough (UTSC).
The UTM campus is the second-largest division of UofT and is situated 33 kilometres west of
Toronto. It is easy to get from UTM to down town Toronto as there is a shuttle bus that students
can take free of charge between UTM and the city. The UTM campus boasts a vibrant research
environment and many of its faculty and researchers are recognized internationally for their
innovative work.

details.Description: The University of Tours (Université de Tours) is a public institution located in the Centre-Val de Loire region, serving a student population of approximately 32,000 across seven faculties and several research units. It employs over 2,700 academic and administrative staff and supports a wide range of disciplinary and interdisciplinary research activities. The university is particularly engaged in regional development and maintains partnerships with national research organisations such as CNRS and INSERM. Its integration with local institutions and its role in supporting both scientific and cultural research give it a distinctive position among French universities, especially in terms of its regional impact and accessibility. Tours is a mid-sized city situated along the Loire River, known for its historical architecture, public gardens, and role as a gateway to the Loire Valley. The city offers a balanced environment for student life, with cultural events, libraries, and public transport well integrated into the urban landscape. Its location provides access to nearby castles, vineyards, and natural areas, making it a practical base for regional exploration. Tours is also well connected by rail to Paris and other major cities, offering convenience for travel during an exchange semester. For students seeking a manageable and culturally rich setting, the University of Tours presents a well-rounded option.

details.Description: The University of Trento ( Università degli Studi di Trento ) is located in Trento and nearby Rovereto. It has been able to achieve considerable results in didactics, research, and international relations according to CENSIS and the Italian Ministry of Education. The University of Trento was founded in 1962 as a Higher University Institute for Social Sciences. It then became the first Faculty of Sociology in Italy. UniTrento is widely recognized as a dynamic and innovative research and teaching institution with strong connections to industry and top-class services. National and international classifications consistently rank the University of Trento as one of the top Italian universities. In addition to traditional lectures, there is much emphasis on laboratory work and small seminar groups. UniTrento is a medium-sized university, where it is easy for students and teachers to interact and there is a continuous exchange of ideas across many different disciplines: in short, the virtuous dynamism of a small university. Furthermore, because of long-term international relations, UniTrento is a vibrant, multi-cultural university which fosters an enriching and stimulating learning environment. The university is located in one of the most gorgeous natural environments in the world, the Dolomites, and it combines strong links to the territory with a steady expansion of international outreach.

details.Description: The University of Trento ( Università degli Studi di Trento ) is located in Trento and nearby Rovereto. It has been able to achieve considerable results in didactics, research, and international relations according to CENSIS and the Italian Ministry of Education. The University of Trento was founded in 1962 as a Higher University Institute for Social Sciences. It then became the first Faculty of Sociology in Italy. UniTrento is widely recognized as a dynamic and innovative research and teaching institution with strong connections to industry and top-class services. National and international classifications consistently rank the University of Trento as one of the top Italian universities. In addition to traditional lectures, there is much emphasis on laboratory work and small seminar groups. UniTrento is a medium-sized university, where it is easy for students and teachers to interact and there is a continuous exchange of ideas across many different disciplines: in short, the virtuous dynamism of a small university. Furthermore, because of long-term international relations, UniTrento is a vibrant, multi-cultural university which fosters an enriching and stimulating learning environment. The university is located in one of the most gorgeous natural environments in the world, the Dolomites, and it combines strong links to the territory with a steady expansion of international outreach.

details.Description: The University of Turin, founded in 1404, is one of Italy’s largest and most respected public universities, with a student population of over 80,000 and more than 4,000 academic and administrative staff. It offers a broad academic portfolio across 27 departments and maintains a strong reputation in both humanities and sciences. The university is known for its commitment to research excellence and internationalization, with numerous partnerships and exchange agreements worldwide. A notable feature is its integration with local institutions and industries, which provides students with opportunities for practical experience and interdisciplinary collaboration within the city and region. Turin, located in the Piedmont region of northwestern Italy, is a dynamic city with a rich cultural and industrial heritage. It offers students a mix of historical architecture, contemporary art, and green spaces, all within a well-connected urban setting. The city is known for its cafés, museums, and proximity to the Alps, making it attractive for both academic and leisure activities. Public transport is efficient, and the cost of living is generally lower than in other major Italian cities.

details.Description: Welcome to the University of Turku, Finland's third-largest university in terms of student enrollment. With eight faculties and a shared campus with Åbo Akademi University, the University of Turku offers a diverse and vibrant academic environment. Collaboratively, these two universities provide a wide range of high-quality academic courses taught in English. Turku Law School, renowned for its commitment to excellence, conducts cutting-edge education and research across a wide academic spectrum. The faculty's dedicated teachers and researchers actively engage in public discourse, contributing their expertise to important discussions. As a cooperative organization involving two universities in Turku, Turku Law School benefits from a rich academic network and collaborative opportunities.

details.Description: Discover the essence of business-focused education and international collaboration at the University of Vaasa. As a multidisciplinary university, it prioritizes key areas such as management and change, energy and sustainable development, and finance and economic decision-making. With a modest student population of approximately 5,000, the University of Vaasa offers a close-knit and personalized learning experience. Located in the picturesque neighborhood of Palosaari, alongside the city's historic cotton mill, part of the university's campus is nestled within the charming premises. details.Description: The University of Valencia, founded in 1499, is one of Spain’s oldest and most prominent public universities. It serves a student population of over 60,000 and offers a wide range of academic disciplines across its faculties. The university is known for its strong research output, particularly in health sciences, environmental studies, and social sciences, and maintains active international collaborations. Its campuses—Blasco Ibáñez, Tarongers, and Burjassot-Paterna—are integrated into the city and provide students with access to modern facilities, libraries, and research centers. Valencia is a Mediterranean city known for its blend of historical architecture, contemporary design, and student-friendly atmosphere. The city offers efficient public transport, including metro, tram, and bike-sharing systems, and is well-connected to beaches, parks, and cultural venues. Students can enjoy local festivals, such as Las Fallas, and explore the City of Arts and Sciences, a major architectural and cultural complex. A fun fact: Valencia is the birthplace of paella, one of Spain’s most iconic dishes, traditionally cooked over an open fire in wide, shallow pans.

details.Description: Founded in 1365, the University of Vienna is one of Europe’s oldest and most prestigious institutions of higher learning. Today, it hosts approximately 85,000 students, including nearly 30,000 international students from over 120 countries. With 15 faculties and 5 centres, the university offers an exceptionally broad academic portfolio, encompassing 187 degree programmes across disciplines such as humanities, natural sciences, social sciences, law, and economics. Renowned for its cutting-edge research, the university has received over 140 ERC grants and proudly counts Nobel laureates among its faculty. Exchange students benefit from a wide selection of English-taught courses, modern facilities, and a vibrant academic community committed to innovation and global engagement. Located in the heart of Austria’s capital, the University of Vienna offers students the opportunity to live and study in one of the world’s most liveable cities. Vienna is a cultural and intellectual hub, known for its rich history, classical music heritage, and dynamic arts scene. With over 2 million residents and a strong international presence, the city combines historical charm with modern infrastructure, excellent public transport, and a high quality of life. Students can enjoy everything from world-class museums and concert halls to green parks and cafés, all within walking distance of the university’s central campus. For those seeking both academic enrichment and cultural exploration, Vienna provides an ideal setting for a memorable and rewarding exchange experience.

details.Restrictions: As an exchange student, you must have minimum 2 years (120 ECTS) completed before beginning your exchange – no exceptions. You  have to select courses in the field of study that you have been nominated for. As a 3 rd year bachelor student, you can usually also attend courses from the master's programme provided you have sufficient knowledge on the subject. This must be clarified in advance with the mobility coordinator. Incoming students are expected to take at least 16 ECTS per semester in the nominated field of study. If you are interested in taking courses from a different field of study, this counts as taking courses outside your nominated field of study. This must be discussed with the mobility coordinator of the other field of study AFTER your arrival in Vienna. However, there is no guarantee that a place will be available. Please be aware that you will need to have appropriate German language skills if you wish to study at the University of Vienna as most of the courses are held in German. It is recommended that students who do not have sufficient German skills read up on the exact course offer in English in due time.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (:
German is the main language of instruction at the University of Vienna. Law classes are taught in German and in English.
Exchange students who wish to study at the University of Vienna do not need to submit an official language certificate or language confirmation. However, during the online nomination procedure your home university must confirm that you have sufficient language skills.
details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student, you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad.
details.Course information: Exchange programme for both bachelor and master level law students. Most courses have the value of 2, 3 or 4 ECTS credits, therefore be aware that you must complete many courses to meet the requirement of 30 ECTS per semester. Incoming Students can choose between undergraduate and graduate courses. See also the information about seminars further down. Types of Courses At the Faculty of Law, different types of courses are offered: In the course catalogue you can see the abbreviations: lectures (VO), courses (KU), practical exercises and case studies (both UE), seminars (SE), repetition courses (RE), conversation classes (KO), Moot Courts (MC), excursions (EX) and practical work courses (PR). When you choose to go to Vienna you will receive additional information about the different categories. Students can achieve a higher number of ECTS credits in some lectures and seminars. University of Vienna recommends students to follow a mix of courses, lectures and 1-2 seminars. Seminars: Generally, Vienna recommends that students who enjoy writing papers attend max. two seminars per semester. At first, students will be awarded 4 ECTS if they participate in a seminar and give an oral presentation. Furthermore, you can obtain 4 ECTS additionally, if you write a written paper (approx. 25-page paper) which amounts to 8 ECTS in total per seminar. The course catalogue will only be available a few weeks before the beginning of each semester. Vienna generally recommends that international students register for more courses than you need as you may not receive a place in all the courses that you have applied for.

For those seeking both academic enrichment and cultural exploration, Vienna provides an ideal setting for a memorable and rewarding exchange experience.

details.Restrictions: As an exchange student, you must have minimum 2 years (120 ECTS) completed before beginning your exchange – no exceptions. You  have to select courses in the field of study that you have been nominated for. As a 3 rd year bachelor student, you can usually also attend courses from the master's programme provided you have sufficient knowledge on the subject. This must be clarified in advance with the mobility coordinator. Incoming students are expected to take at least 16 ECTS per semester in the nominated field of study. If you are interested in taking courses from a different field of study, this counts as taking courses outside your nominated field of study. This must be discussed with the mobility coordinator of the other field of study AFTER your arrival in Vienna. However, there is no guarantee that a place will be available. Please be aware that you will need to have appropriate German language skills if you wish to study at the University of Vienna as most of the courses are held in German. It is recommended that students who do not have sufficient German skills read up on the exact course offer in English in due time.

details.Description: The university was founded in 1965 as part of a government initiative to expand higher education. It has been a mark of Warwick's strategy to encourage and facilitate admission from those less well-advantaged and from poorer backgrounds. The university has around 29,500 full-time students. The university is located outside the city of Coventry, England - close to Birmingham.
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
