details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: See info on the English language requirements (https://warwick.ac.uk/services/studentopportunity/studentmobility/studyatwarwick/applicationprocess/english_language_requirements_-_exchange_students.pdf) * Some departments set specific department requirements.
details.Study load: 60 credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: The exchange agreement is not open for master level students. Undergraduate/bachelor students must have completed as a minimum one full-year of studies at UCPH in advance of the student exchange programme.
details.Course information: Most modules/courses are year-long, meaning that students have a wider selection of modules if they start their placement September/October. Arriving in January may restrict module availability and students are advised consider the part-year module handbook (https://warwick.ac.uk/services/studentopportunity/studentmobility/studyatwarwick/moduleinformation) very carefully. You are required to take undergraduate level modules unless the agreement between our universities specifies you can take postgraduate modules. For more information on credits and modules including course descriptions, please see the module handbook. (https://warwick.ac.uk/services/studentopportunity/studentmobility/studyatwarwick/moduleinformation/partyearstudents-examinationmethods/)

details.Scholarships: The UK is currently seeking to rejoin the Erasmus+ programme for the 2027/28 academic year, but it will not be known until spring 2027 which UK universities will participate . As a result, students applying for exchange places in the UK cannot be guaranteed an Erasmus+ grant at the time of application. Eligibility for Erasmus+ funding will depend on whether the host university joins the programme and concludes an Erasmus+ agreement with the University of Copenhagen. Students nominated to a UK university will be informed of their grant eligibility no later than March 2027.
details.Additional information: The University of Warwick is located 25 minutes by train from Birmingham and 1 hour by train from London.

details.Description:
University of Washington is a public institution founded in 1861. Located in the University
District neighborhood (known as the U District) just north of downtown Seattle, the university
supports a community of more than 54,000 students. UW is a multi-campus university in
Seattle, Tacoma and Bothell. Tacoma and Bothell is approximately 20-30 minutes from
downtown Seattle, but can be easily reached by bus.
details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: September - March (fall and winter quarter) Spring semester: January - June (winter and spring quarter) Autumn quarter: September-December Winter quarter: January-March Spring quarter: March-June Please note: You CANNOT apply for the fall quarter only. If you apply for the fall, you will have to stay for 2 quarters (fall & winter), which is from September to March Please note that the spring semester begins very early compared to the spring semester at UCPH. You should only apply for the spring semester, if you do not have exams in January at UCPH.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: TOEFL-test: For tests after Jan. 21, 2026: Minimum: 4,0, Recommended 4.5, for tests taken before Jan.21, 2026: minimum 76 (recommended 105) or IELTS: 6.0 (recommended 7.0) or DuoLingo: 110 (recommended 131)
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 18 credits = 30 ECTS - Immigration requirement: To meet the immigration requirements, all students at this university must enroll in 12 credits per quarter. As the duration of an exchange stay is at least two quarters, students must enroll in courses corresponding to 24 credits, which is more than the 18 credits required to obtain 30 ECTS. Transfer of excess credits to ECTS will be handled according to the rules of the relevant UCPH faculty (due to the block structure at the Faculty of Science, students from this faculty may consider taking 27 credits, as this would give them the opportunity to transfer 45 ECTS before they return for block 4).
details.Restrictions: The agreement is for undergraduate studies only. All undergraduate exchange students will be admitted through the College of Arts & Sciences. If you are a graduate student at University of Copenhagen when you go abroad, you need to be able to transfer undergraduate courses to your degree at UCPH as you will not be allowed to follow graduate courses. If you read reports from previous exchange students at UW, you might see that they were graduate students and took graduate courses - the rules have changed since then and from 2023 the agreement is only open for undergraduate studies. It is not possible to apply for the fall semester only. You can either apply for the fall +winter quarter (September-March), the winter + spring quarter (January-June), or the full academic year (September-June). This is one of the very few exchange agreements outside Europe where you can apply for a full academic year abroad. If you choose 'fall semester' in the application form that means September-March (fall and winter quarter) for this agreement. Spring semester means January-June (winter and spring quarter) Professional programs including those offered by the Foster School of Business, Information School, School of Medicine, School of Nursing, and School of Pharmacy, as well as any fee based programs are not available to exchange students.  STEM courses (especially Computer Science and Engineering) have some limitations. Degree seeking students and departmental exchange students are given priority The following courses are extremely competitive so students should plan to take courses outside of these areas: - Business - Communications - Economics - Psychology - Law, Societies & Justice - Math
details.Important links: Website for Incoming Exchange (https://studyabroad.washington.edu/) Course catalogue (http://www.washington.edu/students/crscat/)

details.Description: Established as the State's first university in 1911 and founded with a mission to "advance the prosperity and welfare of our communiyties," the University opeened in 1913 to just 184 students. Today, more than 28,000 students are enrolled from 115 countries. For more than 100 years, we have contributed to the intellectural, cultural and economic development of Western Australia, the nation and our world. At UWA, sport plays a central role in the lives of students and promotes a healthy campus culture. Whether you’re training for a gold medal or looking for a spin, dance or Pilates class, UWA Sport offers programs and membership options to suit everyone. Compared to other major cities around the world, Perth is the perfect place to live, work and study. Not only is it one of the most liveable cities in the world (15th in the world to be exact), but it’s also more affordable than Sydney and Melbourne too (Worldwide Cost of Living Report 2023, Economist Intelligence Unit). University of Western Australia from an international perspective (https://youtu.be/KZD8htgIs8Q?si=5e7hHtgG0Tro25ID)

details.Description: UW-Madison has long been recognized as one of America’s great universities, regularly ranked as one of the top public research universities in the United States. Many of UW-Madison’s academic programs are ranked among the best in the nation with 9000+ courses and 400+ degree programs. A public, land-grant institution, UW-Madison offers a complete spectrum of humanities, social science, business, science, and engineering courses. Madison is the capital of Wisconsin and one of the hubs of education, business, and culture in the state, known for a vibrant entertainment and performing arts scene. Madison residents are active, and spend time in parks, on bike paths, and in and around Madison’s four lakes. Madison has frequently been ranked as one of the best places to live in the United States.

details.Description: The University of Wollongong enjoys an international reputation for world-class research, exceptional teaching quality and graduate outcomes. We are a young and vibrant university with undiminished ambitions. We value our research capacity to work on complex interdisciplinary problems. Our spirit of inquiry drives our research and learning environments and our objective of earning a place in the top 1% of the world’s universities. With 120 clubs and societies, live acts on campus each year, it’s just a matter of choosing between them. Being Australia’s 9th largest city and just over an hour from Sydney, Wollongong is a vibrant city that offers the perfect Australian lifestyle. It’s affordable, easy to get around and enjoys a lower cost of living than other Australian cities. Situated on the shores of the Pacific Ocean between the mountains and the sea, students can enjoy a relaxed coastal lifestyle with 17 patrolled surf beaches. Take a virtual campus tour (https://www.uow.edu.au/about/locations/campus-map/virtual-tours/)

details.Description: The University of York is situated on a beautiful parkland campus close to one of Britain’s most historic cities. Established in 1963, the university has expanded to more than thirty departments and centers, covering a wide range of subjects. The University has just below 19,000 students and places an emphasis on small class sizes, personal attention and guidance. The university has a lively, cosmopolitan campus with its own shops, banks, bars and restaurants.

details.Description: The University of Zurich (UZH), founded in 1833, is the largest university in Switzerland, enrolling around 28,000 students and supported by roughly 3,700 full‑time faculty . It offers the broadest range of subjects of any Swiss higher education institution, with seven faculties covering medicine, law, economics, natural sciences, humanities, theology, and veterinary medicine . UZH is internationally recognized for cutting‑edge research in life sciences, biomedical studies, climate science, and social sciences - featuring leading institutes such as the Institute of Molecular Life Sciences - and encourages a strong interdisciplinary approach . About 25% of students come from abroad, creating a vibrant multicultural academic environment with many research partnerships and study programs open to international applicants . Living in Zurich as a student means immersing yourself in a cosmopolitan yet manageable city with excellent transport and abundant social opportunities. Zurich’s well‑connected public transport and bike‑friendly streets make getting around easy, with student discounts available . Campus life is dynamic - UZH’s Academic Sports Association (ASVZ) offers over 120 sports activities, while the student union (VSUZH) and a dozen-plus associations organize academic, cultural, and political events . International students can join clubs ranging from acapella ensembles and environmental groups to investment clubs and political societies . Although Zurich’s cost of living is high, many students find shared flats through WOKO or nearby towns, and experience suggests that engagement in sports and social events helps with integration, even for those new to German . Overall, UZH offers a rich blend of top-tier academics, diverse extracurriculars, and Swiss urban life steeped in culture and connection.

Zurich’s well‑connected public transport and bike‑friendly streets make getting around easy, with student discounts available . Campus life is dynamic - UZH’s Academic Sports Association (ASVZ) offers over 120 sports activities, while the student union (VSUZH) and a dozen-plus associations organize academic, cultural, and political events . International students can join clubs ranging from acapella ensembles and environmental groups to investment clubs and political societies . Although Zurich’s cost of living is high, many students find shared flats through WOKO or nearby towns, and experience suggests that engagement in sports and social events helps with integration, even for those new to German . Overall, UZH offers a rich blend of top-tier academics, diverse extracurriculars, and Swiss urban life steeped in culture and connection.

details.Description: Established in 1477, Uppsala University is the oldest and prestigious university in Sweden and the Nordic region. Located in Uppsala, it offers a wide range of academic disciplines across its nine faculties, including the renowned Faculty of Law. With a strong emphasis on research and international collaboration, the Faculty of Law provides a vibrant research environment and highly regarded legal education. The unique training model and active involvement of prominent researchers ensure high-quality education and enriching research experiences for students. The university's historic legacy and commitment to excellence make it a sought-after destination for students and scholars alike. With about 52,000 students in a compact city of just over 230,000 residents, Uppsala has a uniquely youthful atmosphere where bikes outnumber cars and student life shapes much of the local culture. The city is known for its beautiful river views, historic university buildings, and cozy cafés that fill with students studying or socializing. A big part of life here revolves around the traditional student “nations”—13 social clubs that organize everything from formal dinners and choirs to club nights and themed parties, making it easy to meet people and dive into Swedish traditions. Despite being a historic city, Uppsala feels dynamic and international, offering plenty of cultural events, outdoor activities, and excellent train connections to Stockholm just 40 minutes away.

details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: There are no official language requirements. All courses are taught in English or Swedish. Exchange students must, however, have a high level of proficiency in English corresponding to min. level B2 in the self-assessment CEFR-grid (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-2-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-self-assessment-grid) .
details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student, you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. The majority of law courses have the value of 15 ECTS. Block-structure is used, i.e. generally you have one law course per block with the possibility of immersion. Law courses taught in English are offered at master level but are accessible for both bachelor and master exchange students. Courses consist mainly of seminars with a few lectures. The teaching method used at the Faculty of Law is problem-based like in UCPH. You prepare for classes in groups or individually before seminar classes, where active class participation is expected, so thorough preparation may be required. Please note that attendance at all seminars is compulsory. Assignments submitted during the semester may be part of the final grading in some courses.

details.Additional information: Uppsala University has exiting student life with many student associations called student unions and student nations creating a vibrant atmosphere with a lot social events. The campus in Uppsala is located 70 km north of Stockholm and 30 km from the international airport Stockholm Arlanda. Green transportation by train from Copenhagen is also an option. From Uppsala you can easily go on day trips to Stockholm or other destinations in the vecinity. When the Faculty of Law in Copenhagen has nominated you for an exchange place at the University of Uppsala, you have to apply for admission within the application deadlines which may vary a bit from year to year.

details.Restrictions: As a law exchange student you must follow a full study load of minimum 30 ECTS per semester while you are abroad. Generally, courses have a value of 7.5 ECTS - meaning four courses will be required. As a bachelor student you will only be given access to bachelor level courses. The course selection is a bit limited at bachelor level - but please be aware that courses categorized as period 1 and period 2 are block-sections held within semester 1. A wide varity of courses are offered on master level - but only in the fall semester. Please observe that no master courses taught in English are offered in semester 2. The teaching style at Utrecht University may seem different with more focus on theoretical aspects compared to UCPH with a more case-based education. Preparation of assignments will be expected both during the semester but also at the final exams usually in combination with other types of examination. Therefore, keep an eye on the examination type(s) good time in advance. Also be aware that some written exams are held as closed book exams.

details.Study plan:
Utrecht offers 10 weeks of clinical training and/or the opportunity to do a project in practice (research project) with a research group. Clinical rotations
You will complete the clinical rotations at the three hospitals: • The Companion Animals Clinic • The Equine Clinic • The Farm Animals Clinic Each rotation lasts five weeks, which means that you will be able to do two rotations during your exchange. You can participate in clinical rotations at all three hospitals or only at one hospital. A normal day in the clinic starts at 8 am and ends at 5 pm. However, this may vary depending on the number of patients and cases. Each clinic week equates to 1.5 ECTS credits. Doing a 10-week clinic equates to 15 ECTS credits. Project in practice/research project If you want to do a project in practice during your stay at Utrecht University, you must mention this when applying for admission once you have been recommended for an exchange place. You will then make an agreement directly with the research group with the help of the coordinator in Utrecht. Read more about the project in practice on Study Information at UCPH. (https://kunet.ku.dk/studie/veterinaermedicin-ka/Sider/Emne.aspx?topic=Erhvervsprojekt&topicId=184477ef-bbf4-4e38-9e52-02622e613907#184477ef-bbf4-4e38-9e52-02622e613907)

details.Description: Victoria’s teaching and research is built on a proud tradition of academic excellence stretching over more than 100 years. This excellence naturally transfers to, and enriches, the teaching and learning we offer, and illustrates the calibre of discovery and the cutting-edge knowledge of our staff. We are also ranked within the world’s top 150 universities in a significant number of subjects, including law, arts and social sciences, psychology, earth sciences and information technology. At Victoria, you will join a warm, open and diverse community of students from over 100 countries. Excellent support networks, such as our International Buddy Programme, combined with initiatives like our unique Kitea Impact Programme (https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/students/student-life/kitea) , produce globally aware graduates who are ready for a rapidly changing world. We look forward to welcoming you to Victoria and to Wellington and assisting you to take advantage of the world-class opportunities that are available to you here. Wellington regularly ranks as one of the most liveable cities in the world. It is compact, safe, friendly, and a great place to live. But don’t take our word for it—come and see for yourself! Get a glimpe of Wellington has to offer, and why so many people choose to study here. (https://youtu.be/FwDP3Xyfo60?si=_qS7anqgibjvkjjS)

details.Description: The Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (VU or VU Amsterdam) is a public research university in Amsterdam, Netherlands, founded in 1880. The VU is one of two large, publicly funded research universities in the city, the other being the University of Amsterdam (UvA). The translation of the Dutch name Vrije Universiteit is "Free University". "Free" refers to independence of the university from both the State and the Dutch Reformed Church. Both within and outside the university, the institution is commonly referred to as "the VU". VU Amsterdam is a unique university with faculties in the humanities, STEM, social sciences and medical sciences. Our education and research are closely linked. We combine our top position in research with a strong social orientation, which has resulted in an excellent international reputation. Our education and research are distinctly multidisciplinary. This is reinforced by the fact that our faculties are all located on one campus. We are a true campus university in the heart of the Zuidas Knowledge District, sharing its excellent national and international position and accessibility. The VU has more than 29.500 students.

However, for advanced courses (level 300 and up), a background in that field of study is required. - Bachelor’s students are not allowed to follow courses at Master’s level. - Students who wish to take Dutch-taught courses should reach out to incoming@vu.nl.
details.Course information: Exchange students must always select courses from the exchange study guide Selecting courses from our regular bachelor's or master's programmes is not possible. You find the exchange study guide of courses offered here (https://vu.nl/en/education/more-about/exchange-courses) As a BSc exchange student, you are strongly encouraged to follow one of the Minors offered by the VU. These are pre-packaged selections of approximately five related courses that span the entire semester. Also note that some courses have specific entry requirements, which means you must have a relevant academic background in order to be allowed to take these courses. It is not possible to do any type of research project while on exchange at VU (https://vu.nl/en/education/more-about/exchange-nomination-application) . If you wish to do an internship or research project, you will have to arrange it yourself by finding a supervisor. The supervisor in turn will have to arrange your registration at the university.

details.Additional information:
Ever since it was founded in 1880, VU Amsterdam has been known for its distinctive approach to knowledge. 
VU stands for universal university values such as academic freedom and independence, which is reflected in its name (‘Vrije University’ is the Dutch abbreviation for ‘free university’): free from the church, state and any commercial interest.
Located in lively and multicultural Amsterdam, the city with the largest concentration of students in the Netherlands and where English is the second language, VU is a single building complex campus in the business district of Amsterdam.

details.Description: In Wageningen, you learn about nature, sustainability and improving everyone's life daily. "To explore the potential of nature to improve the quality of life." That is the mission of Wageningen University & Research (WUR). The strength of WUR lies in its ability to join the forces of specialised research institutes and the university. It also lies in the combined efforts of the various fields of natural and social sciences. This union of expertise leads to scientific breakthroughs that can quickly be put into practice and be incorporated into education. As such, studying in Wageningen guarantees premium quality education and an international quality benchmark on your curriculum vitae. WUR hosts an international student environment (25 % of the student population) and is less than an hour by train from Amsterdam, making it an ideal destination for exchange students. WUR consistently ranks as one of the best universities in Europe and the world within Agriculture, Forestry, and Environmental Sciences.

All the MSc- and the 3rd year BSc-courses are taught in English, as well as many 2nd year BSc courses. BSc students may apply for MSc courses if they fulfill the requirements of the specific course. Students are allowed to apply for courses at departments outside of their department of enrollment (if they fulfill the requirements), but students are advised to take as many courses within their field of study as possible. It is recommended that you choose courses from one specific programme; fitting your preference and background. This guarantees a coherent and well-balanced selection. BSc minors at Wageningen University are usually 24 ECTS and are taught in the first or second semester. If you need more ECTS than the minor offers, you can simply add another course to a minor.

details.Description:
Waseda University, established in 1882, has 13 faculties covering 22 research areas. 56,000
students in total and 4,000 foreign students are learning together on campus. The Center for
Japanese Language is an educational institution that provides year round Japanese courses
for Waseda's 1,700 international students.
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Academic calendar: Fall Semester: September - February (Transcripts are issued in May) Spring Semester: March/April - August (Transcripts are issued in October) Academic Calendar for exchange students (waseda.jp) (https://www.waseda.jp/inst/cie/en/exchange/application#anc_45) Important! Waseda issues transcripts in May (after Fall exchange) and in October (after Spring exchange), which is later than other universities. Please make sure this will not conflict with your subsequent plans, particularly if the exchange is in your final semester of your bachelor's degree, as this will affect the timing of your credit transfer.
details.GPA for undergraduate admission: You must check the GPA requirement for each school, however most schools demand a GPA of 3.0 of 4.0 = approx. minimum 7 (C) on the ECTS scale.
details.GPA for graduate admission: You must check the GPA requirement for each school, however most schools demand a GPA of 3.0 of 4.0 = approx. minimum 7 (C) on the ECTS scale.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: An official language test score report (TOEFL, IELTS, TOEIC, JLPT) is required by most exchange students depending on the school you apply to. Applicants must meet the language requirement each school has set. Further details can be found here: https://www.waseda.jp/inst/cie/en/exchange/application (https://www.waseda.jp/inst/cie/en/exchange/application) English Based Program : All applicants are required to submit a copy of a valid test score (TOEFL, IELTS, etc. - please see each school’s requirements) regardless of nationality. English language requirements may be waived if your current degree programme is officially taught entirely in English (requires certification by your Faculty/Department). Japanese Based Program: All applicants including those who hold Japanese citizenship are required to submit a JLPT certificate. Japanese Language Program: Students must have at least one academic year of Japanese language learning experience at university, high school, or Japanese language school before the enrollment of JLP.
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 16 credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Study load for graduate students: 8 credits = 30 ECTS Please note: - Timeframe: The above conversion applies for students going abroad in the academic year 2023-2024 and onwards. - Conversion and levels: Study load is calculated according to the level of the specific course. Please note that not all UCPH Master’s (graduate) programmes allow credit transfer of bachelor (undergraduate) courses into their programmes. - Exceptions to the conversion: Conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: It is not possible to apply to Waseda for exchange in the first semester of the graduate programme. Applicants must have completed at least one semester before the application period at Waseda University begins (i.e. before February for exchange in the following Fall semester, and before November for exchange in the following Spring semester). details.Description: Modern society increasingly demands the members who have broad educational experience, are capable of communicating in English – the international common language – and aspire to realize a free and fair society. In 2004, SILS was established with an original concept and curriculum designed to meet this demand. Specifically, SILS aims to contribute to the development of the following types of students: *Students who aspire to try to resolve the problems facing our globalizing world *Students who are conscious of the distinctiveness of their own culture but also aim to live harmoniously in a multi-cultural society *Students who understand the fundamentals of various academic fields and also have interests in innovative, interdisciplinary scholarly pursuits *Students with the ability to express their own views in a foreign language.

Lecture courses: 2 credits correspond to 1 class (= 90 minutes) for 15 weeks = 22.5 hours of teaching. Lecture courses are offered as 2 or 4-credit courses (1 or 2 classes per week, respectively). details.Description: Washington and Lee University was founded in 1749. Being one of the smallest of the nation's top-tier law schools, Washington and Lee School of Law (W&L Law) is located in a college town in the majestic Shenandoah Valley of Virginia, a three-hour drive from Washington, DC and within an hour of several other metropolitan areas. W&L Law has long been an innovator in legal education, and these innovations have allowed the school to build a singular community that educates students for character and challenges them to solve the problems they will face in a complex world. It fosters a desire not simply to act, but to act intelligently and ethically.

details.Academic calendar: Fall semester: Runs from mid/late-August until early December – with exams in Dec. An Orientation Program is held before the start of the fall semester. Spring semester: Runs approx. from early January until mid-April – with exams in mid and late April. An Orientation Program is not held in the spring semester. See additional information in their calendar (https://law.wlu.edu/calendar/2023-24-law-academic-calendar) .
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: All law courses are taught in English. Students should be studying law fluently in English, both orally and in writing. However, there are no language test requirements for Washington and Lee. Instead, Washington and Lee requires a confirmation from the University of Copenhagen that certifies that the student’s language qualifications are sufficient. A language confirmation will, however, only be needed after you have been nominated to the exchange programme. At that stage, you will be able to retrieve a language confirmation from UCPH in Mobility Online.
details.Restrictions: Law students must follow a full study load of min. 12 credits which corresponds to 30 ECTS per semester. Be aware that credit requirements may be different for other exchange students at Washington and Lee School of Law.
details.Course information: See the course descriptions (https://catalog.wlu.edu/content.php?catoid=42&navoid=4085) - as an exchange student you can take upper-level courses. In relation to the course registration process, be aware that a drop/add period runs around the first two weeks of the semester. The style of teaching is based on the socratic method, meaning students are actively involved and some professors may use cold calling. The professors will expect that you are well prepared for classes and that you are ready to answer their questions and participate in class discussions. Be aware that your participation in class may also count towards your final grade. Expect a high workload at this university as preparations for active class participation and the amount of reading material may be higher compared to UCPH.

details.Additional information: A Orientation Program will not be held in the spring semester - meaning you will have to be more active in order to get social contacts or to network, check e.g. availability of student organizations, sports facilities ... Also be aware that Washington and Lee is a small Law School with a low procentage of international students. In Mobility Online, you can find additional info in reports from former students who went on student exchange to Washington and Lee. Visa requirements: If you are not a U.S. citizen, a J-1 visa is required for entry to the USA. As an exchange student you must demonstrate access to sufficient funds to cover your living expenses, during the time in the United States. Washington and Lee University will provide additional information about this in the admission process. Insurance: In addition to a possible mandatory insurance at your host university, UCPH recommends that Danish students on an exchange programme take out an insurance coverage with a Danish insurance company to make sure that you are sufficiently covered especially during your activities and trips outside the campus area of your host university and in case an urgent situation should occur with need of home transportation for DK.

details.Description: The University was founded in 1989 and is one of the largest universities in Australia with 42,000 students. We’re ranked among the top two per cent of universities in the world, with a growing international reputation for research-led, student-centred learning. Unlike the traditional lecturer-down approach, our pioneering model of  co-created learning treats our students as partners in their education. We empower students to share ideas and develop their creativity through a range of degrees. WSU is a multi-site university with campuses spread across Greater Western Sydney, including Bankstown; Blacktown/Nirimba; Campbelltown; Hawkesbury; Parramatta and Penrith. A Shuttle Bus drives from campus to campus making it easy to access all of the WSU facilities. Sydney is one of the most liveable and picturesque global cities. With the world's largest natural harbour, 100km of coastline and beaches to explore, and an abundance of cultural activities year round, it's no wonder that Australia's largest city is consistently ranked internationally as one of the top 12 urban centres to visit or live in. See why you should choose Western Sydney University (https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL08mMPK6iVGb4FdQD19QMIl3wTNNbLfqo)

details.Description:
The Yale Graduate School of Arts and Sciences is one of fourteen schools composing
Yale University and the only one that awards the degrees of Doctor of Philosophy,
Master of Philosophy, Master of Arts, and Master of Science. The work of the
Graduate School is carried on in the divisions of the Humanities, Social Sciences, and
Biological and Physical Sciences. Fifty-six departments and programs offer courses of
study leading to the Ph.D. degree. There are nineteen programs that terminate with
the master’s degree. Yale University comprises three major academic components: Yale College (the

professional schools. In addition, Yale encompasses a wide array of centers and
programs, libraries, museums, and administrative support offices. Approximately
11,250 students attend Yale.

details.Description: Yeungnam University has been continuously and consistently progressing forward with the purpose of realizing the calling of the times in contemporary Korean history. Subsequent to the chaos after the Independence and the Korean War, the Korean people’s aspiration was to “revive the nation through education”. This was engraved in the founding spirit of our university, and the “Patriotic Spirit, Educational Spirit, and Productive Instruction” which has continued for more than 70 years and contributed to creating a new history. In the era we live in, what is called the Fourth Industrial Revolution, Yeungnam University once again aims to become the protagonist of “creating a new history” through dauntless challenges and innovations. Ever ambitious to outperform our achievements, we will lead the paradigm shift in higher education to foster creative and liberal talent required by the knowledge-based society instead of the standardized one demanded by the industrial society.

details.Restrictions: 15 Yonsei credits corresponds to 30 ECTS per semester. Be aware that credit requirements may be different for other exchange students at Yonsei University. Undergraduate course numbers range from 1000 (lower division) to 4000 (upper division). For example, ECO1234 would be a lower division course and ECO4567 would be an upper division course. 5000-level courses and above are graduate courses. details.Description: At Osgoode, we encourage you to think differently. To reflect on what has value. To welcome diverse views. And once grounded in the fundamentals, to choose your own path, gaining practical experience as you find solutions to important legal challenges. Throughout our long history, we’ve always viewed the practice of law as far more than a means to an end. It’s a journey that takes you from deciding what matters to creating meaningful impact. And it starts here.
details.Agreement name: York University - Osgoode Hall Law School
details.Disclaimer: We strive to keep the agreement information updated. However, the information is subject to changes by the exchange partner.
details.Academic calendar: Orientation events take place during the first week of Fall term. Fall semester: Late August to December – including exams Winter semester: Early January to late April – including exams* *Please note that the spring semester begins very early compared to the spring semester at UCPH. You should only apply for the spring semester, if you do not have exams in January at UCPH or if you plan carefully.
details.Accepted proof of language proficiency (: All courses are taught in English. An English proficiency Letter is required but this requirement has been waived for Danish law exchange students, meaning no documentation will be required to confirm your language skills.
details.Study load for undergraduate students: 15 credits = 30 ECTS Please note that the credit conversion does not apply to mandatory stays (HUM) or clinical electives (SUND) abroad.
details.Restrictions: You must be enrolled at master level at UCPH when the exchange programme begins - although you can only take courses at undergraduate level at Osgoode Hall Law School.
details.Course information: See info on courses and seminars. (https://www.osgoode.yorku.ca/courses-and-seminars/) The course list is updated every year once the new courses are confirmed. 15 credits correspond to 30 ECTS per semester. Be aware that credit requirements may be different for other exchange students at Osgoode Hall Law School. Exchange students can only register for undergraduate courses, i.e. JD courses. The basic law degree at Osgoode, a J.D., is technically classified as an undergraduate degree, but is really a post-graduate degree with virtually all JD students already holding at least a bachelor’s degree before starting the JD. In other words, an Osgoode JD is not a first degree for students. Students ballot for courses in late May/early June. Information is emailed to students after their application is processed. All course selections are done online, and students are notified of their enrolments in July.
details.Important links: See info for international students (https://yorkinternational.yorku.ca/international-students/) See the homepage of Osgoode Hall Law School (https://www.osgoode.yorku.ca/) Health Insurance Requirements: Exchange students studying in Canada are required to purchase the University Health Insurance Plan (UHIP) which is approximately $255.00 Cdn. Estimated Cost of Living per semester: Please refer to our site (https://www.osgoode.yorku.ca/programs/juris-doctor/financial-services/budgeting/)
details.Housing: On campus housing may be available to students who apply by the deadlines. Please note that demand is very high and there is no guarantee of obtaining on campus housing (https://www.yorku.ca/housing/) .

details.Restrictions: Schulich School of Business and School of Arts, Media, Performance & Design are not open for exchange students from UCPH. Master of Conference Interpreting not available for exchange students. Psychology: Graduate Psychology is not available. Undergraduate Psychology - upper level (3/4000) courses have limited access for exchange students. Electrical Engineering and Computer Science is not available to exchange students. Graduate courses in all Engineering subjects are not available either. Graduate Political Science courses are not available for exchange students Graduate Biology programme is not available for exchange students. Undergraduate Biology program has very limited courses available for exchange students. School of Information & Technology not available Undergraduate: • Social Work - not available • Criminology - not available • School of Information & Technology - not available • Economics - limited course availability • Administrative Studies - limited course availability It may be difficult to get a full semester with only 4th year courses (level 400) so please be sure that you can also get 3rd year/300 level courses pre-approved by your study board (this is mainly an issue for students who are graduate-level/kandidat students at UCPH and studying at undergraduate level in Canada). Law students interested in studying at the Osgoode Hall Law School should apply to this school specifically on their application.
details.Course information: Exchange students are not permitted to take courses virtually at YorkU from overseas. Exchange students should ensure return flights are arranged to accommodate the end of the examination period. Some courses require students to be present in Toronto for examinations. Exchange students will enroll into courses online. If courses are reserved or restricted, exchange students may seek permission from the course department to add the course. Students may be required to provide additional information proving they meet course prerequisites. Permission to enroll may not be granted. At times, students must wait up to 2 weeks prior to semester start date to begin enrolling.
